signals.title: [Bug]: Admin-only route denials return 401 instead of 403, and are recorded in Prometheus with exception_status="None"
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a non-admin user calls an admin-only management route, the proxy correctly refuses the request but reports the refusal incorrectly in two ways. **Problem 1 — the client receives 401 instead of 403.** Authentication succeeded: the proxy identifies the caller well enough to name their role and user ID in the error message, and other requests in the same session succeed with the same key. The request is refused purely on authorization, so the correct status is **403 Forbidden**. Returning **401** is misleading. It tells the client its credentials are invalid, when in fact the key is valid, retrying with it is correct, and re-authenticating will not help. The proxy already returns 403 for comparable permission denials elsewhere. **Problem 2 — the failure is recorded in Prometheus with `exception_status="None"`.** The denial carries no status code at the point metrics are recorded; the HTTP status is only decided later, when the error is turned into the client response. Prometheus therefore records: ``` litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric_total{exception_class="Exception", exception_status="None", route="/key/aliases"} ``` This is not limited to one endpoint. In our deployment the same label pair is produced by at least ten admin-only routes, all triggered by non-admin users loading Admin UI pages: `/key/aliases`, `/organization/list`, `/team/list`, `/tag/list`, `/policies/list`, `/prompts/list`, `/user/available_roles`, `/search_tools/list`, `/search_tools/ui/available_providers`, `/in_product_nudges`. These denials are indistinguishable by label from real infrastructure failures, which also appear as `exception_class="Exception"`, `exception_status="None"` — database-connectivity failures during auth, for example. There is no label that separates a routine permission denial from an outage, so they cannot be excluded from a proxy error-rate alert. **What I expected:** a 403 response, recorded with a matching `exception_status="403"` so that routine authorization denials can be told apart from proxy failures. ### User Flow The flow fails at step 3: the viewer is told their credentials are invalid, when in fact their credentials are fine and they simply lack permission. 1. A teammate with the `internal_user_viewer` role signs in to the Admin UI at `http://localhost:4000/ui` using their virtual key. 2. They open the Virtual Keys page. The page loads and lists the keys they are allowed to see, confirming their key is accepted. 3. The page requests `GET /key/aliases`. The response is **401 Unauthorized**, with body text beginning `Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/key/aliases. Your role=internal_user_viewer`. 4. The viewer reads "Authentication Error" and "401", concludes their key has expired or been revoked, and asks an admin to reissue it. The new key behaves identically. 5. Meanwhile `GET /organization/list` with the same key returns **200 OK**, so the key is demonstrably valid — the two responses contradict each other. 6. On the operations side, the 401 from step 3 is counted as a proxy failure with no status attached. It cannot be told apart from a database outage, so the error-rate alert fires and pages the on-call for what was only a viewer opening a page. Authorization consequence: no user gains access they should not have — the route is correctly refused. The cost is that a legitimate viewer is told their identity is invalid, and an operator cannot distinguish routine denials from real failures. ### Proof the bug occurs ```yaml router_settings: redis_host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST redis_port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT redis_password: os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD litellm_settings: cache: True cache_params: type: redis host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT password: os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD supported_call_types: [] callbacks: ["prometheus"] service_callback: ["prometheus_system"] prometheus_metrics_config: - group: "traffic_total_requests" metrics: - "litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric" include_labels: - "status_code" - "requested_model" - "route" - group: "traffic_failed_requests" metrics: - "litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric" include_labels: - "exception_status" - "exception_class" - "requested_model" - "route" ``` Version: v1.81.3-stable **Problem 1 — 401 returned for an authorization failure** Preceding request in the same session, same virtual key — succeeds, confirming the caller is authenticated: ``` INFO: 10.x.x.x:<> - "GET /organization/list HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` Seconds later, the same session requests an admin-only route. **Client response: 401 Unauthorized** (expected: 403 Forbidden): ``` LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: auth_exception_handler.py:78 - litellm.proxy.proxy_server.user_api_key_auth(): Exception occured - Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/key/aliases. Your role=internal_user_viewer. Your user_id=<> Requester IP Address: 10.x.x.x Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py", line 1154, in _user_api_key_auth_builder _ = await common_checks( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<11 lines>... ) ^ File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py", line 285, in common_checks _is_route_allowed = _is_allowed_route( route=route, ...<4 lines>... valid_token=valid_token, ) File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py", line 407, in _is_allowed_route return _is_api_route_allowed( route=route, ...<3 lines>... user_obj=user_obj, ) File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py", line 362, in _is_api_route_allowed RouteChecks.non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check( ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^ user_obj=user_obj, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<4 lines>... valid_token=valid_token, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ) ^ File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/route_checks.py", line 252, in non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check RouteChecks._raise_admin_only_route_exception( ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^ user_obj=user_obj, route=route ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ) ^ File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/route_checks.py", line 143, in _raise_admin_only_route_exception raise Exception( f"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route={route}. Your role={user_role}. Your user_id={masked_user_id}" ) Exception: Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/key/aliases. Your role=internal_user_viewer. Your user_id=<> ``` **Problem 2 — the denial is recorded with `exception_status="None"`** ```promql sum by (exception_class, exception_status, route) ( increase(litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric_total{exception_class="Exception"}[5m]) ) ``` Ten admin-only routes, all recorded as `exception_status="None"`: The proxy is explicitly configured to emit `exception_status` for this metric (see `include_labels` above) — the label is requested and populated, and its value is the literal string `"None"` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.81.3-stable ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
signals.author: kusha-rapido

signals.title: [Bug]: compression_savings_spend and prompt_caching_savings_spend always $0 with cost-based-routing and multiple deployments per model_name
signals.text: # [Bug]: `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` always $0 when using `cost-based-routing` with multiple deployments per model_name ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? When using `routing_strategy: cost-based-routing` with multiple deployments sharing the same `model_name` (each at a different provider/price point), the daily spend rollup fields `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` are always recorded as `$0.00`, even though compression is actively removing tokens from requests. The root cause is that `compute_savings_spend()` in `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/savings.py` calls `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` which uses `litellm.get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider)` to look up the model's pricing. But for multi-deployment setups the backend model name (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `custom_llm_provider="openrouter"`) is **not** in `litellm.model_cost` — because `shared_backend_model_info()` in `litellm/types/utils.py` explicitly strips all pricing fields from the shared backend key: ```python SHARED_BACKEND_MODEL_INFO_FIELDS = frozenset( ModelInfoBase.__required_keys__ | ModelInfoBase.__optional_keys__ ) - frozenset(CustomPricingLiteLLMParams.model_fields) # <-- removes ALL cost fields def shared_backend_model_info(model_info: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]: return {k: v for k, v in model_info.items() if k in SHARED_BACKEND_MODEL_INFO_FIELDS} ``` So when `_create_deployment()` registers the shared backend key: ```python _backend_alias_cost = {_model_name: _shared_model_info} litellm.register_model(model_cost=_backend_alias_cost) ``` The registered entry contains only `{"litellm_provider": "openrouter", "mode": "chat"}` — no pricing. Subsequent `get_model_info()` calls for that model+provider combination fail with "This model isn't mapped yet", and `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` gracefully returns `(0.0, 0.0)`. The per-deployment pricing IS correctly stored under the deployment's unique `model_info.id` hash, but `compute_savings_spend()` never looks it up by that ID — it only has `model` and `custom_llm_provider` available from the spend log payload. ## What did you expect to happen? `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` should reflect the actual dollar savings using the deployment's configured pricing, even when multiple deployments share a `model_name` with different prices. ## Steps to Reproduce **Config (minimal):** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY input_cost_per_token: 0.0000004225 output_cost_per_token: 0.000000845 model_info: cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.000000035 - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: openai/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/ZEN_API_KEY api_base: https://example.com/zen input_cost_per_token: 0.00000174 output_cost_per_token: 0.00000384 model_info: cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.000000174 router_settings: routing_strategy: cost-based-routing ``` Two deployments, same `model_name`, different providers and prices. Cost-based-routing picks the cheaper OpenRouter deployment. The spend log records `model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `custom_llm_provider=openrouter`. **Verification inside the running container:** ```python import litellm # The shared backend key has NO pricing: print(litellm.model_cost.get("openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro")) # → None (not registered at all, because shared_backend_model_info stripped the cost fields) # get_model_info fails for the backend model+provider combo: litellm.get_model_info(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", custom_llm_provider="openrouter") # → raises: "This model isn't mapped yet" # So compute_savings_spend returns (0.0, 0.0): from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.savings import compute_savings_spend result = compute_savings_spend( model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", custom_llm_provider="openrouter", compression_saved_tokens=100000, cache_read_input_tokens=500000, ) print(result) # SavingsSpend(compression=0.0, prompt_caching=0.0) # Expected: SavingsSpend(compression=0.04225, prompt_caching=0.000203625) # (100k * $0.4225/M = $0.04225 compression, 500k * ($0.4225 - $0.035)/M = $0.000203625 caching) ``` **Observable effect:** - Headroom `/stats` endpoint shows compression is actively working (6.7M tokens removed across 457 requests) - But `/user/daily/activity` shows `compression_savings_spend: 0.0` for all days after switching to multi-deployment cost-based routing **Before/After comparison from our daily activity data:** ``` 2026-08-11 saved_tokens=430430 comp_savings_spend=$0.09 ← single deployment per model_name 2026-08-12 saved_tokens=2256791 comp_savings_spend=$2.34 ← last day with old config 2026-08-13 saved_tokens=0 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ← switched to multi-deployment 2026-08-14 saved_tokens=3939121 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ← compression works, pricing broken 2026-08-16 saved_tokens=543419 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ``` ## Suggested fix `compute_savings_spend()` receives the `model` and `custom_llm_provider` from the spend log payload but not the `router_model_id` (deployment ID). Two possible approaches: **Option A (minimal):** Thread the deployment's `model_info.id` into `compute_savings_spend()` and look up pricing via `litellm.model_cost[model_info_id]` first, falling back to `get_model_info()` only when the ID lookup misses. **Option B (more robust):** Thread the deployment's actual `input_cost_per_token` / `cache_read_input_token_cost` values directly into `compute_savings_spend()` from `litellm_params` / `metadata.model_info`, similar to how `custom_cost_per_token` is already passed in the response-cost path. This removes the dependency on the global `litellm.model_cost` dict entirely for savings calculation. ## Relevant log output No errors are logged — `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` catches the exception from `get_model_info()` and degrades silently: ```python except Exception as e: verbose_proxy_logger.debug( "savings: no model info for provider=%s model=%s (%s)", custom_llm_provider, model, e ) return 0.0, 0.0 ``` Setting `LITELLM_LOG=DEBUG` surfaces: ``` savings: no model info for provider=openrouter model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (This model isn't mapped yet...) ``` ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy, Cost Tracking ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.95.0 (Docker image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0`)

signals.title: [bug]: /v1/messages drops stop_sequences
signals.text: ### check for existing issues - [x] i have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### what happened? on litellm proxy 1.96.2, `post /v1/messages` with `stop_sequences` does not stop the model. the same proxy, same model, `post /v1/chat/completions` with `stop` does. expected: an anthropic client that sends `stop_sequences` gets the same hard stop the openai route already applies. actual: `/v1/messages` returns `stop_reason: end_turn` and the full completion, including the stop token. `/v1/chat/completions` returns `finish_reason: stop` and empty content. live openai gpt-4o-mini, 1/1 each below. capture against a mock (user text `hi` so the token is not in the prompt): `/v1/messages` forwards only `model` / `input` / `max_output_tokens`, 5/5. docs already list `stop_sequences` as dropped on the messages mapping. the openai route still has `stop`, so this is one ingress forgetting to ask. ### user flow before a (hypothetical) fix: a claude code user pointed at the proxy with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` cannot cut generation at a stop token. 1. the admin starts the proxy with an openai deployment and no extra flags. 2. the user sends `post http://127.0.0.1:4011/v1/messages` with `stop_sequences: ["STOPPROBE"]` and a prompt that writes that token first, then a poem. 3. the response is 200, `stop_reason: end_turn`. the text starts with `STOPPROBE` and then the poem. 4. the same user sends `post http://127.0.0.1:4011/v1/chat/completions` with `stop: ["STOPPROBE"]` and the same prompt. that call stops with empty content. after a (hypothetical) fix: both routes honor the stop token. 1. the admin starts the same proxy. 2. the user sends the same `post http://127.0.0.1:4011/v1/messages` with `stop_sequences: ["STOPPROBE"]`. 3. the response is 200 and generation stops at that token (`stop_reason: stop_sequence`, no poem after it). 4. the chat completions call still stops the same way. ### proof the bug occurs config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-mini litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY ``` started as `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4011 --host 127.0.0.1`. version or commit: litellm 1.96.2 (pypi). commands and their full output (live openai gpt-4o-mini; no secrets): `/v1/messages` (stop ignored): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4011/v1/messages \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","max_tokens":80,"stop_sequences":["STOPPROBE"],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write the exact token STOPPROBE as the first word, then write a 40-word poem about cats. Do not skip the token."}]}' ``` observed: http 200, `stop_reason: end_turn`. text: ``` STOPPROBE In shadows soft, they stealthily creep, ...then a full poem... ``` `/v1/chat/completions` (stop honored): ```bash curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4011/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","max_tokens":80,"stop":["STOPPROBE"],"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write the exact token STOPPROBE as the first word, then write a 40-word poem about cats. Do not skip the token."}]}' ``` observed: http 200, `finish_reason: stop`, assistant `content` empty. `STOPPROBE` is not in the body. direct anthropic haiku with the same `stop_sequences` token: `stop_reason: stop_sequence` 3/3. the backend can stop. this ingress does not ask. ### what part of litellm is this about? proxy ### what litellm version are you on ? 1.96.2

signals.title: [Bug]: responses() accepts response_format and silently ignores it — no mapping to text.format, no UnsupportedParamsError
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Closest prior art is discussed at the bottom — none of it covers this. ### What happened? `litellm.responses()` accepts `response_format=...` and silently ignores it. The call succeeds, the caller believes a JSON schema is being enforced, and it is not. `response_format` is the spelling every other litellm surface uses, and the one you naturally reach for coming from `litellm.completion()`. On the Responses API the equivalent capability exists and works — it is spelled `text={"format": {...}}` — but the familiar name is accepted and dropped with no error, no warning, and no log. Three requests, same prompt, same model, asking for a strict JSON schema with a top-level `flags` array (litellm 1.96.2, `gpt-5.4-mini`, 2026-08-16): | request | outcome | |---|---| | no format specified | model invents its own shape: `{"ai_speak": ..., "suggestion": ...}` | | `text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": ..., "strict": True, "schema": ...}}` | **exact requested schema** ✅ | | `response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...}}` | call succeeds, schema **ignored** — model returns its own shape again ❌ | Row 3 is the bug. Row 2 proves the capability is there and reachable. ### Reproduction No API key needed — the parameter is discarded client-side, before any provider mapping or validation runs: ```python from litellm.responses.utils import ResponsesAPIRequestUtils as R SCHEMA = { "type": "object", "properties": {"flags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["flags"], "additionalProperties": False, } def survives(**extra): params = {"input": "hi", "model": "gpt-5.4-mini", "custom_llm_provider": "openai", "kwargs": {}, **extra} return sorted(R.get_requested_response_api_optional_param(params).keys()) print(survives(response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "Flags", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}})) # [] <-- gone, no error print(survives(text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "Flags", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}})) # ['text'] <-- kept print(survives(totally_made_up_param="xyz")) # [] <-- same silent drop for any unknown key ``` Confirmed with `litellm.drop_params is False` (the default). The end-to-end version is just `litellm.responses(model="gpt-5.4-mini", input=..., response_format=...)` and observing that the returned `output_text` does not conform. ### Root cause `responses()` has no `response_format` parameter, so it lands in `**kwargs` and then in `local_vars`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/responses/main.py#L907-L1022 `get_requested_response_api_optional_param()` then narrows to the keys declared on `ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams`: ```python valid_keys = get_type_hints(ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams).keys() non_default_params = PreProcessNonDefaultParams.base_pre_process_non_default_params( ..., default_param_values={k: None for k in valid_keys}, ... ) ``` and `base_pre_process_non_default_params` keeps a key only if `k in default_param_values`: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/utils.py#L3559-L3574 `response_format` is not declared on `ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams` (`text` is), so it is removed here — **before** `_check_valid_arg()` runs. That is what makes it silent rather than loud: the guard that exists to catch exactly this never sees the parameter. The guard itself is fine. Hand it the parameter directly and it produces precisely the error a caller should have gotten: ```python R._check_valid_arg(supported_params=["text", "stream"], non_default_params={"response_format": {...}}, drop_params=False, custom_llm_provider="openai", model="gpt-5.4-mini") # litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: openai does not support parameters: # {'response_format': {...}}, for model=gpt-5.4-mini. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` ... ``` So litellm already implements the correct behaviour for this case — the filter order just makes it unreachable. Note this also means `drop_params=False` does not mean what it says on this path: unknown params are dropped regardless of the setting. ### Why this one misleads rather than merely surprising Probing the capability the obvious way returns the wrong answer about the library. A caller passes `response_format`, gets a 200 and unconstrained output, and concludes the Responses API has no structured-output support — when it has full support under a different name. We shipped a code comment asserting exactly that ("the Responses API has no `response_format`"), and it got repeated into a merged PR as established fact. It took reading litellm's source to find `text.format` sitting right there, working. A test that only asserts the call succeeds passes against the broken version, which is presumably why this survived. ### Proposed fix Map `response_format` onto `text.format`, leaving `text` working exactly as it does today and winning when both are supplied. This is not new machinery — it is the mapping litellm already performs for its own `text_format=` convenience parameter: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/responses/utils.py#L904-L936 `convert_text_format_to_text_param()` calls `type_to_response_format_param()`, which returns a `response_format`-shaped dict **unchanged** when handed one, and then reshapes it into `{"format": {type, name, schema, strict}}`. In other words the conversion from an OpenAI-style `response_format` to `text.format` is already implemented and already on the `responses()` code path; `response_format` just never gets routed into it. One wrinkle worth handling while there: that helper indexes `["json_schema"]["name"]` unconditionally, so the non-schema forms (`{"type": "json_object"}`, `{"type": "text"}`) need a branch — those map to `{"format": {"type": "json_object"}}` and `{"format": {"type": "text"}}`. The same latent `KeyError` is reachable today via `text_format={"type": "json_object"}`. Raising `UnsupportedParamsError` instead would also be defensible, and is strictly better than today. But given the capability exists, litellm's stated job is normalising this kind of cross-API spelling difference, and the conversion code is already written, mapping seems like the better answer. Silently accepting is the one option that misleads. Happy to send the PR — mapping in `responses()`/`aresponses()` next to the existing `text_format` call, with tests that assert the resulting request body actually carries `text.format` (not merely that the call returns 200). ### Prior art Checked before filing; none of these covers it: - **#35582** — `aresponses` silently drops `stop`, same filter, same "no error, no warning". Closed **COMPLETED** on 2026-08-02, but the only comment is the reporter withdrawing it ("will handle client-side"), with no maintainer response and no code change. The mechanism was never addressed. `stop` is also weaker as a report: it arguably has no Responses API equivalent, whereas `response_format` demonstrably does. - **#34926** (open, unanswered) — correctly fingers the same `get_requested_response_api_optional_param` filter, but asks for something different: that `allowed_openai_params` be able to preserve an arbitrary extension field (`client_metadata`) for a custom upstream. A per-deployment passthrough allowlist would not fix a first-class OpenAI parameter with a real Responses API equivalent. - **#35677** (open) — Responses API structured output, but a genuinely different failure: `text.format` is supplied correctly and the Anthropic tool-emulation fallback leaks its envelope into `output_text`. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.96.2 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: xAI web_search_options + a system message raises UnsupportedParamsError on 'instructions' — which xAI does support
signals.text: ### What happened? `web_search_options` on an xAI model fails with `UnsupportedParamsError` whenever the request also carries a system message. `responses_api_bridge_check()` routes xAI + `web_search_options` to the Responses API (`litellm/main.py`, added in `dbc80061`, "Add routing of xai chat completions to responses when web search options is present"). The completion→Responses bridge hoists a string system message into `instructions`. `XAIResponsesAPIConfig.get_supported_openai_params()` then removes `instructions` from the supported list, so `_check_valid_arg` rejects the request: ``` litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: LlmProviders.XAI does not support parameters: {'instructions': 'Answer briefly.'}, for model=grok-4.3. ``` Neither ingredient fails alone — only the combination: | messages | `web_search_options` | result | |---|---|---| | user only | no | OK (`/v1/chat/completions`) | | user only | yes | OK (`/v1/responses`) | | system + user | no | OK (`/v1/chat/completions`) | | system + user | **yes** | **`UnsupportedParamsError`** | **The premise is wrong: xAI does support `instructions`.** It is listed in [xAI's Responses API reference](https://docs.x.ai/docs/api-reference#create-new-response), and the live API accepts it, obeys it, and echoes it back — including alongside a server-side `web_search` tool. Proof below. `drop_params=True` is not a workaround. It drops `instructions`, and `instructions` *is* the caller's system prompt, so the call succeeds having silently discarded it. For anything that puts its real instructions in the system role, silently ignoring them is worse than failing. There is also dead code confirming the two halves disagree: `XAIResponsesAPIConfig.map_openai_params()` pops `instructions` with a debug log, but `_check_valid_arg` raises before it is ever reached. **Expected:** `instructions` is passed through to xAI, so a system prompt and `web_search_options` work together. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix:** a developer whose app asks Grok questions that need current web results cannot use a system prompt at all — the request is rejected before it leaves their process. 1. They send `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/...` via `litellm.completion(model="xai/grok-4.3", ...)` with `messages` containing a `system` message plus a `user` question, and `web_search_options={"search_context_size": "medium"}`. 2. Nothing reaches xAI. They get `litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: LlmProviders.XAI does not support parameters: {'instructions': 'Answer briefly.'}`. 3. They follow the error's own advice and set `drop_params=True`. The call now returns HTTP 200 with a correct, web-sourced answer — but their system prompt was discarded, so a request for "the bare version number and nothing else" comes back as a paragraph of prose. Nothing in the response says the instructions were dropped. 4. They remove the system message to make it work, and lose output-format control on every web-search call. **After a (hypothetical) fix:** the same request succeeds with the system prompt honored. 1. They send the same `litellm.completion(...)` with the `system` message and `web_search_options`. 2. The request reaches xAI, which performs the web search and applies the system prompt. 3. They get back `1.97.0` — current, search-sourced, and formatted exactly as the system prompt demanded. ### Proof the bug occurs SDK setup, no mocks, real xAI API (`GROK_API_KEY` set to a live key, redacted throughout): ```python import litellm, os msgs = [ {"role": "system", "content": "Answer briefly."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Newest litellm version on PyPI?"}, ] litellm.completion( model="xai/grok-4.3", messages=msgs, web_search_options={"search_context_size": "medium"}, api_key=os.environ["GROK_API_KEY"], ) ``` **Version:** reproduced on `v1.96.2` (pip) and on `main` at commit `973329e98`. **Output on `973329e98`:** ``` litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: LlmProviders.XAI does not support parameters: {'instructions': 'Answer briefly.'}, for model=grok-4.3. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy: `litellm_settings: drop_params: true` ``` All four cells of the table above, run on `973329e98` with the outbound request captured at the HTTP layer: ``` === user only, no search === url: https://api.x.ai/v1/chat/completions -> OK === user only, web_search_options === url: https://api.x.ai/v1/responses -> OK tools: [{"type": "web_search"}] === system + user, no search === url: https://api.x.ai/v1/chat/completions -> OK === system + user, web_search_options === UnsupportedParamsError: LlmProviders.XAI does not support parameters: {'instructions': 'Answer briefly.'} ``` **Live xAI calls proving `instructions` is supported** — three direct `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/responses` requests, no litellm involved, 2026-08-16: ``` === 1. instructions only === request: {"instructions": "Always answer with exactly the word BANANA.", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}], "max_output_tokens": 2000} HTTP 200 output_text: BANANA echoed instructions: 'Always answer with exactly the word BANANA.' === 2. instructions + web_search tool === request: {"instructions": "Answer in exactly one short sentence.", "input": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the newest litellm version on PyPI?"}], "tools": [{"type": "web_search"}], "max_output_tokens": 4000} HTTP 200 output_text: **1.97.0** echoed instructions: 'Answer in exactly one short sentence.' === 3. system role in input + web_search === request: {"input": [{"role": "system", "content": "Answer in exactly one short sentence."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is the newest litellm version on PyPI?"}], "tools": [{"type": "web_search"}], "max_output_tokens": 4000} HTTP 200 output_text: **1.97.0** ``` xAI accepts `instructions` (1), accepts it together with a server-side web search (2), and honors it — case 1 returns `BANANA` and nothing else. **Live end-to-end through litellm with the one-line fix applied** (`973329e98` + removing the `instructions` exclusion): ``` content: '1.97.0' finish_reason: stop usage: 7482 / 288 / 7770 ``` The system prompt was `"You must answer with the bare version number and nothing else."` — obeyed exactly, and the 7482 input tokens are the injected live search results. Before the fix this same call raised `UnsupportedParamsError`. ### Suggested fix Delete the `instructions` exclusion from `XAIResponsesAPIConfig` (both the removal in `get_supported_openai_params` and the now-unreachable pop in `map_openai_params`). PR attached, with the two stale assertions inverted and a regression test that drives `litellm.completion()` down the web-search bridge and asserts the system prompt arrives as `instructions`. I checked the alternative — having the bridge leave the system message in `input` rather than hoisting it — and it is not needed here: case 3 above shows xAI accepts that shape too, but since `instructions` works there is no reason to special-case xAI in the shared bridge. **Prior art checked:** no existing issue covers this. #11976 is Perplexity `web_search_options`; #14011 is the OpenAI Responses `web_search` tool; #16962 is web-search tool translation for Gemini/Anthropic. None touch xAI `instructions`. Introduced by the interaction of two changes that were each fine alone: `6fb0a8fc` / #16391 (Nov 2025) added the `instructions` exclusion, and `dbc80061` (Jan 2026) added the web-search routing that made it reachable from `completion()`. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2, and `main` at `973329e98` ### Twitter / LinkedIn details @mhammett / https://www.linkedin.com/in/mhammett1/

signals.title: feat(ui): add comprehensive dark mode support to dashboard
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Closes #10177 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes This enables dark mode for the admin dashboard. The navbar already shipped a dark-mode toggle that was scaffolded but gated off behind `{false && ...}`, with a note to keep it disabled until the dashboard supported dark styles end to end; this wires that toggle up and makes it work. A shared `useDarkMode` hook owns the boolean. It persists the choice to `localStorage`, falls back to the OS `prefers-color-scheme` on first load, and toggles the `dark` class on the document element. The App Router dashboard layout, the legacy root page, and the public model hub all consume the same hook, so the toggle behaves consistently no matter which surface renders the navbar. Previously the legacy page kept its own local dark-mode state that did not persist or set the `dark` class, so Tremor components stayed light; routing it through the hook fixes that. Ant Design is themed centrally through `getAntdTheme` on a `ConfigProvider` (dark algorithm plus component tokens for Menu, Table, Input, Modal, and friends). Tremor has no `ConfigProvider`, so its dark styling lives in `globals.css` keyed off the `.dark` class. An inline pre-hydration script in the root layout sets the `dark` class before first paint to avoid a flash of light mode. The work targets `litellm_oss_branch` per the contribution flow for external PRs. The branch carries only UI changes; no `uv.lock`, dependency, or Python files are touched. ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix To verify locally, run the dashboard and flip the Sun/Moon toggle in the navbar (top right). The selected mode persists across reloads, a fresh session follows the OS setting, and there is no flash of light mode on load. Worth checking the models table, logs, and the playground.

signals.title: fix: strip stale Content-Length in pass-through after gzip decompression
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #25624 When a pass-through endpoint proxies a gzip-compressed upstream response, httpx auto-decompresses the body but `response.headers["content-length"]` still reflects the **compressed** size. `get_response_headers()` strips `content-encoding` but keeps the now-stale `content-length`, causing a mismatch between the header and actual body size. **The fix:** Add `"content-length"` to `excluded_headers` in `get_response_headers()`. FastAPI's `Response(content=bytes)` auto-calculates the correct value from the actual body. This is safe for all cases: - **Gzip responses:** Fixes the mismatch - **Non-gzip responses:** FastAPI calculates the same value as upstream - **Streaming responses:** `StreamingResponse` does not use `Content-Length` ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/pass_through_endpoints.py`: Added `"content-length"` to `excluded_headers` set ## Test plan - [ ] Verify pass-through with gzip-compressed upstream (e.g. BytePlus Ark API) returns correct Content-Length - [ ] Verify non-gzip pass-through responses are unaffected - [ ] Verify streaming pass-through responses are unaffected

signals.title: feat(guardrails): add peyeeye PII redaction & rehydration guardrail
signals.text: ## Summary Adds a built-in `peyeeye` guardrail to LiteLLM that handles the full **redact → LLM → rehydrate** roundtrip for PII in prompts: - **Pre-call**: redacts PII from `messages[].content` via the [peyeeye](https://peyeeye.ai) API. The redaction session id is cached against `litellm_call_id` so the post-call hook can rehydrate without a second client call. - **Post-call**: swaps placeholders in `response.choices[].message.content` back to the original values, then cleans up the session. Detects 60+ built-in entity types out of the box (emails, payment data, secrets, government IDs, medical IDs, travel data, etc.) plus first-class custom entities defined by the user. Two session modes: - **Stateful** (default) — peyeeye holds the token → value mapping under a `ses_…` id. - **Stateless** — peyeeye returns a sealed `skey_…` rehydration key; nothing is retained server-side. This complements the existing Presidio guardrail by adding a hosted option that ships with broader entity coverage and built-in rehydration (Presidio is detection-only out of the box). ## Files - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/peyeeye/__init__.py` + `peyeeye.py` — `PeyeeyeGuardrail(CustomGuardrail)` with pre/post hooks. Auto-discovered by `guardrail_registry.get_guardrail_initializer_from_hooks`. - `litellm/types/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/peyeeye.py` — `PeyeeyeGuardrailConfigModel` for the UI schema. - `litellm/types/guardrails.py` — `SupportedGuardrailIntegrations.PEYEEYE` enum entry + `PeyeeyeGuardrailConfigModel` mixin appended to `LitellmParams`. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_peyeeye.py` — init, pre-call, post-call, stateless, error-path tests. No new dependencies — uses the existing `httpx` async handler. ## Example `config.yaml` ```yaml guardrails: - guardrail_name: "peyeeye-redact" litellm_params: guardrail: peyeeye mode: "pre_call" api_key: os.environ/PEYEEYE_API_KEY - guardrail_name: "peyeeye-rehydrate" litellm_params: guardrail: peyeeye mode: "post_call" api_key: os.environ/PEYEEYE_API_KEY ``` ## Docs PR Companion docs PR: BerriAI/litellm-docs adding `docs/proxy/guardrails/peyeeye.md` and the sidebar entry. ## Test plan - [x] `test_peyeeye_init_requires_api_key` — raises when no key - [x] `test_peyeeye_init_reads_env` — picks up `PEYEEYE_API_KEY` - [x] `test_peyeeye_init_explicit_args` — explicit args take priority - [x] `test_peyeeye_guardrail_config_via_init` — `init_guardrails_v2` accepts the new `guardrail: peyeeye` value - [x] `test_pre_call_redacts_messages_and_caches_session` — replaces user message content, caches session id under `litellm_call_id` - [x] `test_pre_call_stateless_returns_skey` — stateless mode caches the `skey_…` rehydration key - [x] `test_pre_call_skips_when_no_messages` — no API call when there's nothing to redact - [x] `test_post_call_rehydrates_response` — swaps placeholders back to originals, deletes session, clears cache - [x] `test_post_call_noop_without_session` — gracefully no-ops when no session was cached (e.g. only `post_call` configured) - [x] `test_redact_api_error_raises_typed` — surfaces typed `PeyeeyeGuardrailAPIError`

signals.title: fix(redis_cache): apply namespace prefix in delete_cache and async_delete_cache
signals.text: ## Summary - `async_delete_cache` and `delete_cache` in `litellm/caching/redis_cache.py` were not calling `check_and_fix_namespace()` before issuing the Redis `DEL` command - When a `namespace` is configured, `SET` and `GET` correctly prefix the key (e.g. `litellm.caching.caching:cronjob_lock:db_spend_update_job`), but `DEL` targeted the raw key — which does not exist — so it always returned 0 - This caused `PodLockManager` to never explicitly release locks; every lock expired by TTL instead, producing a `failed to release Redis lock` warning on every batch-write cycle for every pod ## Changes - `litellm/caching/redis_cache.py`: add `key = self.check_and_fix_namespace(key=key)` to both `async_delete_cache` and `delete_cache`, matching the pattern used in every other cache method - `tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py`: add `test_delete_cache_applies_namespace` — parametrized over `namespace=None` and `namespace="myns"` — asserting the correct key is passed to `redis_client.delete` in both the async and sync paths ## Test plan - [x] `uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py -v` — all 26 tests pass - [ ] `uv run ruff check litellm/caching/redis_cache.py tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py` — clean - [ ] `uv run mypy litellm/caching/redis_cache.py --ignore-missing-imports` — no issues

signals.title: fix(router): cooldown unreachable deployments for failover
signals.text: Fixes #27362 ## Summary - Allow `APIConnectionError` failures to enter router cooldown instead of being suppressed by string matching. - Add regression coverage proving an unreachable deployment with `allowed_fails=0` is cooled down. - Add routing coverage proving subsequent selection filters the cooled-down deployment and returns a healthy deployment. ## Root Cause `_is_cooldown_required()` returned `False` whenever the exception string contained `APIConnectionError`. For unreachable self-hosted backends, LiteLLM maps connection failures to `litellm.APIConnectionError` with status code 500. The string bypass prevented the failed deployment from entering cooldown, so retries could repeatedly select the same dead host. ## Validation - `uv run pytest tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_cooldown_utils.py::test_api_connection_error_requires_cooldown -q` - `uv run pytest tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_cooldown_utils.py::test_api_connection_error_cooldown_filters_failed_deployment -q` - `uv run pytest tests/local_testing/test_router.py::test_router_cooldown_api_connection_error -q` - `uv run pytest tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_cooldown_utils.py -q` - `uv run pytest tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_helper_utils.py -k "cooldown or deployment_callback" -q` - `uv run black --check litellm/router_utils/cooldown_handlers.py tests/router_unit_tests/test_router_cooldown_utils.py tests/local_testing/test_router.py` - `uv run ruff check litellm/router_utils/cooldown_handlers.py` - `git diff --check`

signals.title: fix(langfuse): guard against None standard_callback_dynamic_params
signals.text: ## Fix: AttributeError when Langfuse is configured via env vars (no per-request dynamic params) ### What was broken When Langfuse is configured via environment variables (the standard setup with no per-request dynamic params), `standard_callback_dynamic_params` is `None` (not `{}`). The `_dynamic_langfuse_credentials_are_passed()` and `get_dynamic_langfuse_logging_config()` functions called `.get()` directly on `None`, raising: ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get' ``` This caused every Langfuse success callback to fail silently — no traces appeared in Langfuse, and the error only showed up in logs. ### What I fixed Added a `params = standard_callback_dynamic_params or {}` guard in both functions, so `.get()` is called on an empty dict when `None` is passed. ### Changes - `litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_handler.py`: - `get_dynamic_langfuse_logging_config()`: guard against None in `params` lookup - `_dynamic_langfuse_credentials_are_passed()`: guard against None in `params` lookup - `tests/logging_callback_tests/test_langfuse_dynamic_credentials.py`: - Added 2 regression tests for None handling ### Testing Added regression tests that verify these functions return `False`/`default config` instead of crashing when `None` is passed. Fixes: BerriAI/litellm#25940

signals.title: feat(cost): support OpenAI regional/data-residency 10% uplift via service_tier="regional"
signals.text: ## Summary OpenAI now charges a 10% premium when using regional/data-residency processing on the latest GPT models (see [pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)). LiteLLM didn't account for this — cost tracking for requests opting into regional processing was 10% under-reported. This adds a `regional` value to the `ServiceTier` enum and 10%-uplifted `*_regional` pricing keys to every OpenAI model in `model_prices_and_context_window.json` that already has priority-tier pricing (gpt-5 family, gpt-5.1/5.2/5.3/5.4/5.5 families and codex/chat variants, gpt-4.1 family, gpt-4o family, o3, o4-mini). Above-272k-tokens variants on gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5 also get a regional counterpart. The existing `service_tier` resolution chain (optional_params, response attribute, usage attribute, explicit argument) already covers the customer-facing API surface, so passing `service_tier="regional"` anywhere now produces the correct cost. ## Customer-facing usage ```python import litellm resp = litellm.completion( model="gpt-5", messages=[...], service_tier="regional", # 10% uplift applied ) litellm.completion_cost(completion_response=resp) ``` Or, if `service_tier` is set on the response object by OpenAI itself, no client change is needed — `completion_cost()` picks it up automatically. ## Code changes - `litellm/types/utils.py` — add `ServiceTier.REGIONAL`; add `*_regional` fields to `ModelInfoBase` and `CustomPricingLiteLLMParams`. - `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` — generalize `_get_service_tier_cost_key` to iterate `ServiceTier` (so future tiers slot in without code changes). - `litellm/utils.py` — expose new `*_regional` keys via `get_model_info()`. - `model_prices_and_context_window.json` + `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` — 101 new `*_regional` entries across 30 OpenAI models (10% uplift). - `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py` — extend JSON schema validator with regional keys. ## Test plan - [x] `make test-unit` style runs: `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/test_llm_cost_calc_utils.py` (47 passed) and `tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py` (41 passed). - [x] `tests/test_litellm/test_utils.py::test_aaamodel_prices_and_context_window_json_is_valid` passes (JSON schema). - [x] Six new dedicated regional tests cover: standard regional pricing, case-insensitive tier value, fallback when model has no regional keys, above-272k regional pricing, regional cost-key resolution, enum membership; signals.title: fix(volcengine): translate reasoning_effort to thinking parameter
signals.text: ## Title fix(volcengine): translate `reasoning_effort` to `thinking` parameter (handle `'none'` → `disabled`) ## Relevant issues Fixes the remaining gap from #13039. Builds on #13598 / #14569. ## Problem After #14569, passing `extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}` correctly disables Doubao thinking. However, the standard OpenAI parameter `reasoning_effort='none'` is silently dropped: `VolcEngineChatConfig.get_supported_openai_params` does not declare `reasoning_effort`, so the parent `OpenAIGPTConfig._map_openai_params` filters it out **before** reaching the VolcEngine thinking-translation block. The model receives a request with no thinking directive and falls back to its default (thinking ON), so `reasoning_content` is still produced. ### Reproduction (against `volcengine/doubao-seed-1-6-...`) ```python r = completion(model="volcengine/...", reasoning_effort="none", messages=[...]) # BUG: r.choices[0].message.reasoning_content is NOT None ``` Workaround that works today: ```python r = completion(model="volcengine/...", extra_body={"thinking": {"type": "disabled"}}, ...) ``` ## Fix - Add `reasoning_effort` to VolcEngine's `get_supported_openai_params`. - In `map_openai_params`, translate `reasoning_effort` → Volcengine native `thinking.type`: - `none` / `minimal` → `disabled` - `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` → `enabled` - `auto` → `auto` - Explicit `thinking=` always overrides `reasoning_effort` (precedence rule). - Reuses the existing validation / `extra_body` block from #14569 — no duplicate logic. ## Tests Added `test_reasoning_effort_mapping` in `tests/test_litellm/llms/volcengine/test_volcengine.py` covering: - Param exposure (in supported list) - `none` / `minimal` → disabled - `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` → enabled - `auto` → auto - Precedence: explicit `thinking=` over `reasoning_effort=` - End-to-end via `get_optional_params` Existing `test_thinking_parameter_handling` continues to pass unchanged. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signals.title: fix(bedrock): recalculate total_tokens after cache-token inflation in _transform_usage
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes a bug in `AmazonConverseConfig._transform_usage` where `total_tokens` was read from Bedrock's raw `totalTokens` field **before** cache-token inflation, causing `total_tokens` to be understated whenever `cacheReadInputTokens` or `cacheWriteInputTokens` are present. ## Root cause `_transform_usage` inflates `input_tokens` by adding cache tokens: ```python if "cacheReadInputTokens" in usage: cache_read_input_tokens = usage["cacheReadInputTokens"] input_tokens += cache_read_input_tokens # input_tokens grows here if "cacheWriteInputTokens" in usage: cache_creation_input_tokens = usage["cacheWriteInputTokens"] input_tokens += cache_creation_input_tokens # and here ``` But `total_tokens` was set **before** this block: ```python total_tokens = usage["totalTokens"] # ← BUG: snapshot taken before inflation ``` Bedrock's native `totalTokens` = `inputTokens + outputTokens` (non-cached only), so it misses the cache tokens that were just added to `input_tokens`. This violates the invariant `total_tokens == prompt_tokens + completion_tokens` that the rest of litellm relies on. ## Concrete example | Field | Before fix | After fix | |---|---|---| | Bedrock `inputTokens` | 100 | 100 | | Bedrock `cacheReadInputTokens` | 30 | 30 | | Bedrock `outputTokens` | 50 | 50 | | `usage.prompt_tokens` | 130 | 130 | | `usage.completion_tokens` | 50 | 50 | | `usage.total_tokens` | **150 ← WRONG** | **180 ← correct** | ## Fix Removed the early `total_tokens = usage["totalTokens"]` assignment and added a recalculation **after** the inflation block: ```python # Recalculate total_tokens AFTER inflating input_tokens with cache tokens, # so that total_tokens == prompt_tokens + completion_tokens. # Bedrock's native "totalTokens" only covers inputTokens + outputTokens # (i.e. non-cached tokens), so it would be too low whenever cache tokens # are present. Mirroring what the Anthropic transformation already does # (see litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py). total_tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens ``` This matches the pattern already used in `litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py` (line ~2242). ## Impact - Affects any Bedrock request that uses prompt caching (Claude 3.x on Bedrock). - `total_tokens` reported in `response.usage` and passed to callbacks/logging integrations is too low, causing incorrect cost tracking, analytics dashboards, and rate-limit accounting. - Cost calculation itself is unaffected (uses `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens` separately).

signals.title: fix(tests): normalize Google OAuth JWT in VCR matcher to stop cassette overflow
signals.text: ## Summary Two Vertex image-gen tests (`TestVertexImageGeneration::test_basic_image_generation`, `TestVertexAIGeminiImageGeneration::test_basic_image_generation`) show up as `[VCR MISS:OVERFLOW]` in the `image_gen_testing` CircleCI job and hit the live Vertex API on every CI run. The VCR diagnostic log pinpoints the cause: each run POSTs a freshly minted service-account JWT to `oauth2.googleapis.com/token`. The JWT's `iat`/`exp` claims (and the resulting RSA signature) change every run, so the `safe_body` matcher misses, vcrpy appends a new episode instead of replaying, and the cassette grows until `MAX_EPISODES_PER_CASSETTE=50` refuses the save. Fix: normalize Google OAuth JWT request bodies in `_before_record_request`. Drop volatile JWT claims (`iat`, `exp`, `jti`, `nbf`) and replace the signature with a fixed placeholder before matching, so byte-identical bodies compare equal across runs. Different scopes / issuers still produce distinct normalized bodies, so meaningful auth differences aren't collapsed. ## Files - `tests/_vcr_conftest_common.py` — add `_normalize_jwt`, `_is_google_oauth_token_request`, `_normalize_google_oauth_jwt`; wire into `_before_record_request`. - `tests/llm_translation/test_vcr_filters.py` — 13 new unit tests covering the helper directly (volatile claim stripping, idempotency, content-length rewriting, scope-distinguishability, malformed-JWT and non-OAuth bypass paths, `accounts.google.com` host). ## Test plan - [x] `uv run pytest tests/llm_translation/test_vcr_filters.py tests/llm_translation/test_vcr_classification.py` — 77 passed locally - [x] `uv run ruff check` / `uv run black .` clean - [ ] Re-run the `image_gen_testing` CircleCI job and confirm the `CASSETTE OVERFLOW` section is empty - [ ] Confirm cassette episode count for the two Vertex tests drops from 51/52 back to 1 <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Medium risk because it changes authorization behavior for team/key management writes and alters VCR request-body normalization, which could affect who can configure pass-through routing and how tests match recorded cassettes. > > **Overview** > **Security/permissions:** Moves `_check_passthrough_routes_caller_permission` into shared `common_utils` and applies it to `team` create/update flows, blocking non-`PROXY_ADMIN` callers from setting `allowed_passthrough_routes` (including `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes`) with clearer entity-specific error messages. > > **Test/VCR stability:** Expands the VCR plumbing to (a) pin httpx multipart boundaries, (b) canonicalize/materialize iterable request bodies, (c) normalize Google OAuth token POSTs by stripping volatile JWT claims and replacing signatures, and (d) emit per-worker diagnostic logs surfaced in pytest terminal summaries; updates audio/image tests to use fresh byte payloads and adds unit tests covering JWT normalization and team passthrough-route blocking. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit acb55ab0116061ba6652f02ca2611f274ff20cfd. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix: use >= in _team_max_budget_check (matches all other budget checks)
signals.text: ## Summary `_team_max_budget_check` used strict `>` comparison while every other budget enforcement check in `auth_checks.py` uses `>=`. This means a team at exactly its budget limit is not blocked on the next request. **The bug:** ```python # line ~2870 — was if math.isfinite(team_object.max_budget) and spend > team_object.max_budget: # fixed if math.isfinite(team_object.max_budget) and spend >= team_object.max_budget: ``` **Inconsistency table before this fix:** | Check | Operator | |---|---| | `_virtual_key_max_budget_check` | `>=` | | team member budget check | `>=` | | org budget check (`_org_max_budget_check`) | `>=` | | tag budget check | `>` (separate issue) | | **`_team_max_budget_check`** | **`>` ← was wrong** | **Observable impact:** - A team with `max_budget=10.0` and `spend=10.0` passes the check (`10.0 > 10.0` is `False`) and the next request is allowed through. - Setting `max_budget=0` as a hard "no spend" block does nothing for teams (`0 > 0` is `False`), but correctly blocks keys (`0 >= 0` is `True`). ## Changes Single character change in `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py`. ## Test plan - [ ] Existing budget tests pass - [ ] A team with `spend == max_budget` is blocked on next request - [ ] A team with `spend < max_budget` is still allowed through - [ ] `max_budget=0` correctly blocks teams Fixes #28020

signals.title: fix(vertex): remove spurious vertexai SDK guard from VertexAIPartnerModels.count_tokens
signals.text: ## Summary `/v1/messages/count_tokens` for Vertex AI Claude models fails with HTTP 500 on any proxy deployment that does not have `google-cloud-aiplatform` (the Gemini SDK) installed, even though the actual token counting works fine without it. **Root cause:** `VertexAIPartnerModels.count_tokens()` opens with an `import vertexai` guard copied from other methods in the class. The guard raises `VertexAIError` if the SDK is absent. But `count_tokens` never actually calls any `vertexai.*` API — it delegates immediately to `VertexAIPartnerModelsTokenCounter.handle_count_tokens_request()`, which uses plain HTTPS via `httpx` to hit Vertex's publisher-specific count-tokens endpoint. **Before:** ```python async def count_tokens(self, model, messages, ...): try: import vertexai # raises if google-cloud-aiplatform not installed except Exception as e: raise VertexAIError(status_code=400, message=f"vertexai import failed ...") if not (hasattr(vertexai, "preview") or ...): raise VertexAIError(...) # also never needed try: from litellm.llms.vertex_ai.vertex_ai_partner_models.count_tokens.handler import ( VertexAIPartnerModelsTokenCounter, ) result = await VertexAIPartnerModelsTokenCounter().handle_count_tokens_request(...) ``` **After:** Remove the `import vertexai` block entirely — the `VertexAIPartnerModelsTokenCounter` handles its own HTTP auth without the SDK. ## Impact - All other Vertex AI Claude routes (`/v1/messages`, streaming, tool calls, vision) already work without `google-cloud-aiplatform` because they use the same HTTP path. - `count_tokens` was the only exception, due to the copy-pasted guard. - No behavioral change for deployments that do have `google-cloud-aiplatform` installed. ## Test plan - [ ] `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` for a `vertex_ai` Claude model returns token count without `google-cloud-aiplatform` installed - [ ] `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` continues to work when `google-cloud-aiplatform` is installed - [ ] All existing Vertex AI tests pass Fixes #28084
signals.author: VANDRANKI

signals.title: fix(responses): forward timeout to completion-transformation path in responses()
signals.text: ## Summary The `responses()` function (Responses API) silently ignores the `timeout` parameter for non-native providers (Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex AI). **Root cause:** Two code paths handle provider dispatch inside `responses()`: 1. **Native path** (line ~1159) — calls `base_llm_http_handler.response_api_handler(...)` and explicitly passes `timeout=timeout or request_timeout`. 2. **Completion-transformation path** (line ~1109) — calls `litellm_completion_transformation_handler.response_api_handler(...)` and omits `timeout` entirely. Anthropic, Bedrock, and Vertex AI all go through this path. **Before:** ```python # completion-transformation path return litellm_completion_transformation_handler.response_api_handler( model=model, input=input, ... extra_headers=extra_headers, extra_body=extra_body, # timeout missing ← bug **kwargs, ) ``` **After:** ```python return litellm_completion_transformation_handler.response_api_handler( ... timeout=timeout or request_timeout, # matches native path **kwargs, ) ``` ## Test plan - [ ] `responses(model="claude-sonnet-4-5", ..., timeout=5.0)` raises `Timeout` when the upstream is slow (Anthropic path) - [ ] Same for Bedrock and Vertex AI Claude models - [ ] Native-path providers (OpenAI) unaffected - [ ] No regression in existing Responses API tests Fixes #28132

signals.title: fix(guardrails): classify GuardrailRaisedException as guardrail_intervened, not guardrail_failed_to_respond
signals.text: ## Summary When `generic_guardrail_api` blocks a request (returns `{"action": "BLOCKED"}`), it raises `GuardrailRaisedException`. The `log_guardrail_information` decorator calls `_is_guardrail_intervention(e)` to decide whether to log the block as `guardrail_intervened` or `guardrail_failed_to_respond`. Because `GuardrailRaisedException` is not checked, every block is misclassified as an API failure. **Downstream effect:** The Guardrails Monitor dashboard shows 0 blocked requests and a 100% pass rate even while the guardrail is actively blocking. **Root cause:** ```python # before @staticmethod def _is_guardrail_intervention(e: Exception) -> bool: if isinstance(e, ModifyResponseException): return True if HTTPException is not None and isinstance(e, HTTPException) and e.status_code == 400: return True return False # GuardrailRaisedException falls through → logged as failed_to_respond ``` **Fix:** add `GuardrailRaisedException` check: ```python from litellm.exceptions import GuardrailRaisedException if isinstance(e, GuardrailRaisedException): return True ``` ## Changes `litellm/integrations/custom_guardrail.py` — one `isinstance` guard added to `_is_guardrail_intervention`. ## Test plan - [ ] `generic_guardrail_api` block → logged as `guardrail_intervened` - [ ] `generic_guardrail_api` timeout/connection error → still logged as `guardrail_failed_to_respond` - [ ] `HTTPException(400)` path unchanged - [ ] Existing guardrail tests pass Fixes #28163
signals.author: VANDRANKI

signals.title: fix(auth): union proxy models with team models in get_key_models when all-proxy-models sentinel present
signals.text: ## Summary `GET /v1/models` silently drops team-specific models for keys bound to a team whose ACL contains the `"all-proxy-models"` sentinel alongside named models. **Root cause — inconsistency between `get_key_models` and `get_team_models`:** ```python # get_key_models — REPLACES (bug) if SpecialModelNames.all_proxy_models.value in all_models: all_models = list(proxy_model_list) # team-specific models lost # get_team_models — UNIONS (correct) if SpecialModelNames.all_proxy_models.value in all_models_set: all_models_set.update(proxy_model_list) # keeps team models + adds proxy-wide ``` **How the sentinel ends up in a team's ACL:** a team created without specifying `models` gets `models=[]`, and `add_new_models_to_team` injects `"all-proxy-models"` because it treats an empty list as "all access". Named models added later coexist with the sentinel, but `get_key_models` then discards them when resolving `/v1/models`. **Fix:** compute the union in `get_key_models`, consistent with `get_team_models`: ```python if SpecialModelNames.all_proxy_models.value in all_models: merged = set(all_models) | set(proxy_model_list) merged.discard(SpecialModelNames.all_proxy_models.value) all_models = list(merged) ``` ## Test plan - [ ] Team key with `all-proxy-models` sentinel + named models → `/v1/models` returns union - [ ] Team key with only `all-proxy-models` sentinel → `/v1/models` returns proxy-wide list (unchanged) - [ ] Key without sentinel → unaffected - [ ] Existing model ACL tests pass Fixes #28173
signals.author: VANDRANKI

signals.title: fix(anthropic-messages): wire cache_control_injection_points into /v1/messages
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Customer report (Slack): `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0` + Claude Code → proxy `/v1/messages` produced `cache_creation_input_tokens=0` and `cache_read_input_tokens=0` despite a `cache_control_injection_points` config that works on `/v1/chat/completions`: ```yaml - model_name: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0 cache_control_injection_points: - location: message role: system ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes ### Root cause `cache_control_injection_points` fires through `litellm_logging_obj.async_get_chat_completion_prompt` inside `litellm.completion`, so it works on `/v1/chat/completions`. The native Anthropic `/v1/messages` handler (`litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/handler.py`) forwards Anthropic-format payloads directly to `base_llm_http_handler.anthropic_messages_handler` without ever invoking the prompt-management hook — model-config caching is silently dropped for any Claude Code customer pointing `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at the proxy and routed to `anthropic/*` or `bedrock/*claude*` deployments. Secondary issue in the customer config: `role: system` on `/v1/messages` matches nothing because the system prompt is a top-level `system` parameter, not an entry in `messages` (unlike OpenAI). ### Fix 1. **Schema extension** in `litellm/types/integrations/anthropic_cache_control_hook.py` — add `location: "system"` and `location: "tools"`. The big Claude Code wins (long cached system prompt, cached tool list) were inexpressible before this. 2. **Anthropic-Messages-shaped processing** in `AnthropicCacheControlHook` — new `apply_to_anthropic_messages_request(messages, system, tools, non_default_params)` writes `cache_control` at the **block** level (Anthropic rejects message-level `cache_control` on `/v1/messages`). The OpenAI-shaped `_safe_insert_cache_control_in_message` helper is unchanged so the chat/completions path keeps working. 3. **Auto-translation of the customer's exact config** — when `{location: message, role: system}` is requested AND no message has `role: system` AND a top-level `system` prompt exists, treat it as `{location: system}`. The customer's unmodified YAML now produces cache hits on `/v1/messages`. 4. **Wiring in `anthropic_messages_handler`** — call the new entrypoint right before `base_llm_http_handler.anthropic_messages_handler`, mutating `messages` / `system` / `tools`, popping `cache_control_injection_points` from kwargs so it does not leak as an unknown field to upstream. The OpenAI-shaped chat/completions adapter branch and the OpenAI Responses API branch are unchanged — both still go through `litellm.acompletion` / `litellm.responses`, where the existing hook handles the OpenAI-format case. ### Files - `litellm/types/integrations/anthropic_cache_control_hook.py` — add `CacheControlSystemInjectionPoint`, `CacheControlToolsInjectionPoint` - `litellm/integrations/anthropic_cache_control_hook.py` — add `apply_to_anthropic_messages_request` + three block-level helpers - `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/handler.py` — invoke the hook on the native Anthropic path - `tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_anthropic_cache_control_hook_messages.py` — 21 new tests ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added testing in `tests/test_litellm/` — 21 new tests in `tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_anthropic_cache_control_hook_messages.py` - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` (130 passed across the new file + existing `test_anthropic_cache_control_hook.py` + the full anthropic experimental_pass_through messages suite) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible — single concern (wire one hook into one handler); no router, proxy, or DB changes ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Unit + integration tests for both layers (helper logic + wiring through `anthropic_messages_handler`): ``` signals.title: fix(caching): guard disconnect() against None async_redis_conn_pool in cluster mode
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #31206 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproduce before the fix: ```python import asyncio from unittest.mock import patch async def repro(): with patch("asyncio.get_running_loop", side_effect=RuntimeError): from litellm.caching.redis_cache import RedisCache cache = RedisCache(host="localhost", port=6379, password="x") cache.async_redis_conn_pool = None # what get_redis_connection_pool returns for cluster await cache.disconnect() # AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'disconnect' asyncio.run(repro()) ``` After the fix the call returns cleanly with no exception. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `get_redis_connection_pool()` returns `None` when `REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES` is set because the cluster client manages its own internal connection pool. `RedisCache.__init__` assigns that `None` directly to `self.async_redis_conn_pool`. `disconnect()` then called `self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(...)` unconditionally, raising `AttributeError` and crashing proxy shutdown on every Redis Cluster deployment. The fix is a single early-return guard at the top of `disconnect()`: if `async_redis_conn_pool` is `None` there is nothing to disconnect, so we return immediately. A regression test in `tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py` covers this path.

signals.title: fix(streaming): backfill response.completed output from output_item.done events
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #25429. Related to #26179. Supersedes #30934 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) (201 pre-existing failures in prisma/database, vertex AI, and MCP semantic filter tests; none in touched files — 324 tests across `tests/test_litellm/responses/` and `tests/test_litellm/llms/chatgpt/` pass cleanly) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## CI (LiteLLM team) > **CI status guideline:** > > - 50-55 passing tests: main is stable with minor issues. > - 45-49 passing tests: acceptable but needs attention > - <= 40 passing tests: unstable; be careful with your merges and assess the risk. - [ ] **Branch creation CI run** Link: - [ ] **CI run for the last commit** Link: - [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run** Links: ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The `chatgpt/` provider routes through chatgpt.com's Codex backend, which sends `response.completed` with `output: []`. The actual assistant content arrives via preceding `response.output_item.done` SSE events. Without accumulation, the chat-completions bridge receives an empty output list and raises: ``` ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: [] ``` The fix teaches `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator._process_chunk` to accumulate `response.output_item.done` payloads as they stream in and backfill them into the `response.completed` chunk before it is stored as `completed_response`. Items are serialized to plain dicts via `model_dump()` so the downstream `_handle_raw_dict_response_item` callback in the transformation layer can process them. The existing `_recover_output_items_from_raw_sse` fallback in `LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler.transform_response` is preserved as a second layer if the streaming path is ever bypassed. **Before:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []. Received Model Group=gpt-5.4\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` **After:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"id":"chatcmpl-764df91c-940a-47ea-be8c-d2aff173b8f4","created":1782409329,"model":"gpt-5.4","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"hello","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":5,"prompt_tokens":1635,"total_tokens":1640,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator` accumulates `response.output_item.done` items into `_streamed_output_items` during streaming. A secondary `_streamed_text_only_items` dict catches providers that emit `response.output_text.done` without a preceding `response.output_item.done`. At `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`, if `output` is empty and either dict is non-empty, the merged items are sorted by `output_index` and backfilled onto the response object. Items are serialized via `model_dump()` when they are Pydantic instances and passed through unchanged when they are already plain dicts; both the serialization and the assignment sit inside a `try/except` so any failure degrades to a logged warning rather than crashing the stream. `FallbackResponsesStreamWrapper` (router.py) and `MCPEnhancedStreamingIterator` (mcp_streaming_iterator.py) both bypass `super().__init__()` and are updated to mirror the two new instance attributes. Twelve regression tests are added to `tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator_output_recovery.py`, covering: the core backfill, multi-item index ordering, authoritative output preservation, `response.incomplete` backfill, `response.failed` no-backfill, `output_text.done` fallback, `output_item.done` precedence, replace-in-place content slots, gap padding, absent `output_index` sequential fallback, exception swallowing, and the dict-type contract required by the downstream transformation layer. The bulk of the line-count change in `streaming_iterator.py` is ruff reformatting of pre-existing code required to pass `ruff format`; the logical additions are confined to the accumulation block in `_process_chunk` and the two new instance attributes in `__init__`.

signals.title: feat(voyage): add voyage-multimodal-3.5 model and extra multimodal params
signals.text: ## Relevant issues Supersedes #18285, which was opened against the wrong base and ballooned to 300+ files; this is a clean re-do against `litellm_internal_staging` ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The multimodal config and routing already exist on `litellm_internal_staging`, so this change is small: register `voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5` and surface the extra params the multimodal API accepts. Local verification with real litellm calls (no mocks in the routing/cost path) follows; the only thing not exercised here is the billed network call to Voyage, which needs a `VOYAGE_API_KEY` ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python - <<'PY' import litellm litellm.model_cost = litellm.get_model_cost_map(url="") litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear() info = litellm.get_model_info("voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5") print({k: info[k] for k in ("litellm_provider","mode","input_cost_per_token","max_input_tokens","max_tokens")}) from litellm.utils import get_optional_params_embeddings, ProviderConfigManager print(get_optional_params_embeddings(model="voyage-multimodal-3.5", custom_llm_provider="voyage", dimensions=512, encoding_format="base64", input_type="document", truncation=False, drop_params=True)) cfg = ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_embedding_config(model="voyage-multimodal-3.5", provider=litellm.LlmProviders.VOYAGE) print(type(cfg).__name__) PY {'litellm_provider': 'voyage', 'mode': 'embedding', 'input_cost_per_token': 1.2e-07, 'max_input_tokens': 32000, 'max_tokens': 32000} {'encoding_format': 'base64', 'output_dimension': 512, 'input_type': 'document', 'truncation': False} VoyageMultimodalEmbeddingConfig ``` Live end-to-end against the real API (run with a Voyage key set): ``` VOYAGE_API_KEY=*** python - <<'PY' from litellm import embedding r = embedding( model="voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5", input=[{"content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "a photo of a cat"}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4d/Cat_November_2010-1a.jpg"}, ]}], input_type="document", ) print(r.model, len(r.data[0]["embedding"]), r.usage) PY ``` ## Type New Feature ## Changes Adds `voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5` to both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the packaged backup, priced at the published $0.12 per million text tokens with a 32k context window. The multimodal routing on `litellm_internal_staging` already matches any `*multimodal*` model, so no wiring changes were needed for the model to resolve to `VoyageMultimodalEmbeddingConfig` Extends `VoyageMultimodalEmbeddingConfig` to map `encoding_format`, `input_type` and `truncation` in addition to `dimensions`, matching the parameters the Voyage multimodal embeddings API documents. The existing request/response transformation, API-key validation and `data:image/...` base64 normalization are left untouched Tests live in the already-mapped `tests/test_litellm/llms/voyage/test_voyage_multimodal_embedding.py`: the supported-params and mapping assertions were updated for the new params, and a registration test was added that fails if the `voyage-multimodal-3.5` entry is missing from the cost map
