signals.title: feat: add EmpirioLabs models to model_prices_and_context_window.json
signals.text: ## What Adds price and context-window metadata for EmpirioLabs models to `model_prices_and_context_window.json`, so `litellm.get_model_info("empiriolabs/...")` and the Proxy's cost tracking work out of the box for the `empiriolabs` provider (registered in `litellm/llms/openai_like/providers.json`, docs at https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/empiriolabs). 84 entries: 80 chat, 3 embedding, 1 rerank. Keys are prefixed `empiriolabs/<model id>`, matching the model strings the provider already routes. ## Details - Per-token costs are in USD, sourced from the public catalog at `https://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1/models`. - Chat models that price per message rather than per token use `input_cost_per_request` (same field the Perplexity online entries use). - Models with context-tiered pricing list their standard (base context) rate. - Capability flags (`supports_function_calling`, `supports_vision`, `supports_reasoning`, `supports_web_search`, `supports_system_messages`, `supports_prompt_caching`, `supports_response_schema`) are set from each model's published capabilities. - Image, video, audio and 3D generation are async media endpoints that the per-token cost map does not meter, so they are out of scope here. ## Test `python -c "import json; json.load(open('model_prices_and_context_window.json'))"` parses clean. Every entry was generated from and checked against the live `/v1/models` catalog.

signals.title: fix(pricing): add the azure gpt-realtime-2 family and price realtime image input per token
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Three azure realtime models have no cost map entry - Realtime image input bills at the text rate, not its own - The openai-direct `gpt-realtime-2` entry is stale How it solves it: - Add `azure/gpt-realtime-2`, `-2.1` and `-2.1-mini` - Move the image rate onto the field the calculator reads - Reconcile `gpt-realtime-2` to its published limits and rate ## User Flow Before: a developer sending a photo into a realtime session is charged the text rate for it, so their spend understates what the vendor charges 1. They open a WebSocket to `wss://litellm-domain/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` 2. They send a `conversation.item.create` carrying an `input_image` content part and ask about it 3. The model describes the image, and the session reports back `input_token_details` with `image_tokens: 194` 4. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and the request's input cost is $0.00020940, which is those 194 tokens charged at the $0.60/1M text rate 5. Anyone on `azure/gpt-realtime-2`, `-2.1` or `-2.1-mini` gets no spend row at all, because the model resolves to no entry After: image tokens are charged at the image rate, and the three new models are priced 1. They open a WebSocket to `wss://litellm-domain/v1/realtime?model=gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` 2. They send a `conversation.item.create` carrying an `input_image` content part and ask about it 3. The model describes the image, and the session reports back `input_token_details` with `image_tokens: 194` 4. The same request now shows an input cost of $0.00024820, the 194 tokens at the $0.80/1M image rate 5. `azure/gpt-realtime-2`, `-2.1` and `-2.1-mini` resolve and bill ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix **The image rate was on a field nothing reads.** These entries carry image input cost as `input_cost_per_image`, which is the per-image field used by generation models. The token calculator reads `input_cost_per_image_token`, so image tokens fell through to `input_cost_per_token` and were charged the text rate. Same usage, same entry, only the field name changed: ``` input_cost_per_image = 8e-07 -> input cost $0.00020940 (image at the text rate) input_cost_per_image_token = 8e-07 -> input cost $0.00024820 (image at its own rate) ``` Confirmed on a real realtime session against a live gateway. Azure does accept image input on this API, and the session reported the split itself: ``` input_token_details: {"text_tokens": 145, "audio_tokens": 0, "image_tokens": 194, "cached_tokens": 128, "cached_tokens_details": {"text_tokens": 128}} ``` Reading the resulting spend row back, the input cost reconciles to the reported split exactly, at the rate each modality should pay: ``` mode reported split billed input expected text 128 cached $0.00000768 $0.00000768 EXACT image 17 text + 128 cached + 194 image $0.00024220 $0.00024220 EXACT audio 62 text + 64 cached + 39 audio $0.00046560 $0.00046560 EXACT ``` The image row is the one that moves: before this change it billed $0.00020940 for the same tokens. Text and audio are unchanged, so nothing that was already correct shifted. This adds up faster than a single photo suggests. A realtime session has no video content type, so a camera feed is sent as a sequence of image parts: four consecutive frames reported 776 image tokens, 194 apiece. At the text rate that stream is billed at roughly three quarters of what it should be, and it scales with frame rate. **Rates come from Azure's meters, not OpenAI's price card.** Azure prices its OpenAI models independently, so the values were checked against the retail prices API for the Global tier, per 1M tokens: ``` gpt-realtime-2 Text inp 4.00 Text opt 24.00 Image inp 5.00 Text cd inp 0.40 gpt-realtime-2.1 Text inp 4.00 Text opt 24.00 Image inp 5.00 Audio inp 32.00 / opt 64.00 gpt-realtime-2.1-mini Text inp 0.60 Text opt 2.40 Image inp 0.80 Audio inp 10.00 / opt 20.00 ``` The Data Zone meters are exactly 1.1x Global on every dimension, which is the expected relationship and a signal the rows are live rather than stale. These agree with OpenAI's published realtime rates, but the meters are what an `azure/` key should follow. **Resolution check** on the updated map: ``` azure/gpt-realtime-2 image 5e-06 out 2.4e-05 in 32000 / out 4096 azure/gpt-realtime-2.1 image 5e-06 out 2.4e-05 in 32000 / out 4096 azure/gpt-realtime-2.1-mini image 8e-07 out 2.4e-06 in 32000 / out 4096 azure/gpt-realtime-2025-08-28 image 5e-06 out 1.6e-05 azure/gpt-realtime-1.5-2026-02-23 image 5e-06 out 1.6e-05 azure/gpt-realtime-mini-2025-10-06 image 8e-07 out 2.4e-06 gpt-realtime-2 out 2.4e-05 in 128000 / out 32000 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Adds `azure/gpt-realtime-2`, `azure/gpt-realtime-2.1` and `azure/gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` to both cost map files. Renames `input_cost_per_image` to `input_cost_per_image_token` on the six `azure/gpt-realtime` entries, so image tokens are priced at the image rate instead of falling back to text. The values were already correct. Carries forward the `gpt-realtime-2` reconciliation from review: 32k context / 4096 output / $16 output to 128k / 32000 / $24, agreeing with the azure entry and both vendors' published rate. The azure entries use Azure's 32000 input / 4096 output request limits while the openai-direct entries keep 128000 / 32000. Azure's Realtime API caps a single response at 4096 even though the context window is 128k, so the two providers legitimately differ; this is the correction made earlier in this PR's review and it supersedes the 128k/32000 figures an earlier revision of this description quoted for the azure entries. Rebuilt on `litellm_internal_staging`. This branch previously targeted `litellm_oss_daily_2026_07_10` and no daily branch has been cut since `2026_07_20`. Rebuilding also picks up `mode: realtime`, which staging had since corrected on the sibling entries. No new test, per the cost-map convention; the existing cost suite is the verification. ## Caveats (if any) - `openai/gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` still carries max_output_tokens 4096 - The bare `gpt-realtime*` entries keep the inert per-image field - Both left out to keep this PR to the azure family ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(exceptions): distinguish non-retryable insufficient_quota from transient RateLimitError
signals.text: ## Relevant issues <!-- e.g., "Fixes #000" --> ## Linear ticket <!-- if you are an internal contributor, add "Resolves " followed by the Linear ticket e.g., "Resolves LIT-1234" to link the Linear ticket to the GitHub PR. If you don't have one, leave the section blank rather than guessing --> ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [X] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [X] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The reproduction uses a dedicated OpenAI project with a $1/month hard budget cap, burned to the cap with real `litellm.completion` calls, so both captures below are live API responses — no mocks, no monkeypatching. The raw provider rejection, captured with a direct curl against `https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions`: ``` { "error": { "message": "You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors.", "type": "insufficient_quota", "param": null, "code": "insufficient_quota" } } HTTP_STATUS: 429 ``` **Before (merge-base `3d63edaa6d2ed5f74d7762a07b058e678226907b`)** — the quota error surfaces as a plain `RateLimitError` with `type: throttling_error`, indistinguishable from a transient 429: ``` commit: 3d63edaa6d2ed5f74d7762a07b058e678226907b type(exc).__name__: RateLimitError isinstance(exc, litellm.RateLimitError): True exc.status_code: 429 exc.code: 429 exc.type: throttling_error --- str(exc) verbatim --- litellm.RateLimitError: RateLimitError: OpenAIException - You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors. ``` **After (PR head `7fc261308e654c150b298b786223822112797318`)** — the same probe on the same exhausted key now raises `InsufficientQuotaError` with `code`/`type == insufficient_quota`, and it is **still caught by `except litellm.RateLimitError`** (backwards compatibility, demonstrated live): ``` commit: 7fc261308e654c150b298b786223822112797318 type(exc).__name__: InsufficientQuotaError isinstance(exc, litellm.RateLimitError): True exc.status_code: 429 exc.code: insufficient_quota exc.type: insufficient_quota --- str(exc) verbatim --- litellm.InsufficientQuotaError: litellm.RateLimitError: RateLimitError: OpenAIException - You exceeded your current quota, please check your plan and billing details. For more information on this error, read the docs: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/error-codes/api-errors. ``` Probe command, identical for both captures except the checked-out commit: ```python import litellm try: litellm.completion(model="gpt-5.6", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK."}], max_tokens=16, api_key=REPRO_KEY, num_retries=0) except Exception as exc: print(type(exc).__name__, isinstance(exc, litellm.RateLimitError), getattr(exc, "code", None)) raise ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes **What / why:** When an OpenAI key has no remaining quota (`code: "insufficient_quota"` — a billing state), LiteLLM mapped it to the same `litellm.RateLimitError` used for transient rate-limit 429s, because the mapping matches the `429` token in the error string before the error code is consulted. Retry policies key on `RateLimitError` as retryable, so callers retry a condition that retrying cannot fix (see #14547, #12497 for users hitting this in the wild). This adds an `InsufficientQuotaError(RateLimitError)` subtype and detects the quota case in `_map_openai_exception` **before** the generic rate-limit branch. It carries `code`/`type == "insufficient_quota"` so callers can also branch on the attribute. **Backwards compatible:** existing `except RateLimitError` handlers still catch it (it subclasses `RateLimitError`); retry policies that want to skip billing errors can now exclude the subtype. **Scope, deliberately narrow:** detection keys on OpenAI's `insufficient_quota` code only. Other providers' "quota" 429s (e.g. Vertex's refilling per-minute quotas) are untouched — those are genuinely transient and should stay retryable. Happy to extend to other providers' billing-state codes with maintainer input. **Tests:** mocked tests added in `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_exception_mapping_utils.py` — quota string → `InsufficientQuotaError`; isinstance `RateLimitError` (backwards compat); transient 429 still maps to plain `RateLimitError`; attributes set. File passes 64/64. **Disclosure:** built with AI assistance (my two-agent Claude workflow — Claude Code implemented against my written spec). The issue analysis, scope decisions, and line-by-line review are mine.

signals.title: fix(proxy): retry startup general_settings read on transient DB transport error
signals.text: ### Summary On proxy startup the first Prisma read of `general_settings` (the `store_model_in_db` lookup) can hit a transient `httpx.ReadError`. That leaves the connection in a bad state and uvicorn exits, so the UI never comes up. ### Fix Route that startup read through the existing `call_with_db_reconnect_retry` helper, the same one every other startup DB read already uses, so a transient transport blip triggers one reconnect and retry. Also normalize a string-valued `param_value` (Prisma can return the JSON column as a string) so the DB override is not silently skipped. Adds a regression test that injects a real `httpx.ReadError` on the first read and asserts the reconnect and retry path. Fixes #32412

signals.title: fix: duplicate message_start in anthropic responses stream wrapper
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: four self-hosted vLLM backends behind openai/ deployments, Claude Code pointed at the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint, which routes through the anthropic -> responses bridge for openai-provider models Before the fix, every streamed request emits `message_start` twice with the same message id, which the Anthropic SDK stream parser in Claude Code rejects as an event-order violation: ``` $ curl -s -N http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -d '{"model": "my-model", "max_tokens": 2000, "stream": true, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK and nothing else."}]}' \ | grep -oE "event: [a-z_]+" | sort | uniq -c 62 event: content_block_delta 1 event: content_block_start 1 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 2 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` After the fix, the same command produces a protocol-correct sequence: ``` 1097 event: content_block_delta 2 event: content_block_start 2 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 1 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` (the two content_block start/stop pairs are the thinking block and the text block; Claude Code streams these sessions without errors after the fix) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper.__anext__` pre-emits `message_start` before consuming the upstream stream, and the `response.created` handler in `_process_event` appended another one without checking `_sent_message_start`. Every streamed request through the wrapper emitted `message_start` twice. This guards the `response.created` handler with the existing flag Added a regression test that drives the wrapper with a `response.created`-first event stream and asserts exactly one `message_start` is emitted **Follow-up commit:** while looking at the same wrapper's handling of providers that skip `response.output_item.added`, found that `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` had no fallback for that case. `response.output_text.delta` already synthesizes a `content_block_start` when no block is registered for the item_id; the reasoning delta handler instead fell back to whatever `_current_block_index` happened to be open, which is not necessarily a thinking block, and emitted a `thinking_delta` into it regardless. Strict Anthropic SSE clients reject a `thinking_delta` aimed at a block of a different declared type. Mirrored the existing text-delta fallback for the reasoning case, with a regression test covering both the synthesis and that it never reuses an already-open non-thinking block.

signals.title: fix: omit empty tools array in responses to chat completion transformation
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: self-hosted vLLM backend behind an openai/ deployment with `use_chat_completions_api: true`, hitting the proxy's `/v1/responses` endpoint with a request that carries no tools Before the fix, the bridge sends `tools: []` to the backend and vLLM rejects the request (the error also bounces through every configured fallback since it reproduces on each deployment): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "my-model", "max_output_tokens": 200, "input": [{"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Say OK and nothing else."}]}]}' {"error": {"message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - 1 validation error: {'type': 'value_error', 'loc': ('body',), 'msg': 'Value error, `tools` must not be an empty array. Either provide at least one tool or omit the field entirely.', ... ``` After the fix, the same command returns a normal response: ``` {"id":"resp_N2PG_...","created_at":1784410664,"error":null, ...} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `transform_responses_api_request_to_chat_completion_request` converts an absent `tools` param into `[]` via `responses_api_request.get("tools") or []`, and the final request dict only filters `None` values, so the empty array reaches the backend. Strict OpenAI-compatible backends such as vLLM reject empty tool arrays outright. This maps the empty result back to `None` so the existing None-filter drops the key Added a regression test asserting that a responses request without tools produces a chat completion request with no `tools` key

signals.title: fix: count anthropic image content blocks in token_counter instead of raising
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: router with `enable_pre_call_checks: true` and vision-capable vLLM backends, Claude Code sending screenshots to the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint Before the fix, every image-bearing anthropic messages request logs this router error and silently skips pre-call context-window filtering (the initial deployment list is returned unfiltered): ``` LiteLLM Router:ERROR: router.py - litellm.router.py::_pre_call_checks: failed to count tokens. Returning initial list of deployments. Got - Error getting number of tokens from content list: Invalid content item type: image. Expected str or dict with 'type' field (text, image_url, tool_use, tool_result, thinking, tool_reference)., default_token_count=None ``` After the fix, the same request counts tokens normally and the usage is tracked (no router error logged): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -d '{"model": "my-model", "max_tokens": 300, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "What color? One word."}, {"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png", "data": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="}}]}]}' {..., "usage": {"input_tokens": 82, "output_tokens": 300}, ...} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_count_content_list` handles openai `image_url` blocks but raised `Invalid content item type` on anthropic-format `image` blocks (`{"type": "image", "source": ...}`). The raise disables router pre-call checks for any anthropic messages traffic containing images and breaks token accounting on that path. This counts the flat `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TOKEN_COUNT` for such blocks, matching the `image_url` fallback behavior, since a base64 source has no URL or detail field to inspect. Same failure shape as the `tool_reference` handling that already landed for tool-search traffic Added a regression test asserting an anthropic image block increases the count by at least `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TOKEN_COUNT` instead of raising

signals.title: fix: content_block_delta type mismatch when reasoning and content arrive in one chunk
signals.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: self-hosted vLLM backend with a reasoning-capable Qwen model behind an `openai/` deployment, Claude Code pointed at the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint Captured live from the failing deployment before the fix. The vLLM reasoning parser flushed the tail of `reasoning_content` bundled with the first character of the answer in one streaming chunk. `AnthropicStreamWrapper` opened the new content block as `text` (block-type detection prefers content) but emitted a `thinking_delta` into it (delta emission prefers reasoning), producing this SSE sequence: ``` content_block_stop {"index": 1} content_block_start {"index": 2, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}} content_block_delta {"index": 2, "delta": {"type": "thinking_delta", "thinking": "\n"}} ``` Claude Code (a strict Anthropic SSE client) rejects this as "Content block is not a thinking block". Because the corrupted assistant turn gets replayed as conversation history, every subsequent turn in the same context fails the same way until the context is cleared. After the fix, hitting the same backend with a prompt that forces a reasoning/answer transition, and reducing the captured event stream to (index -> declared block type) then checking every delta against its block's declared type: ``` $ curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "my-reasoning-model", "max_tokens": 1500, "stream": true, "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]}' \ | grep -oE "event: [a-z_]+" | sort | uniq -c 462 event: content_block_delta 3 event: content_block_start 3 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 1 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` block types opened: `{0: "text", 1: "thinking", 2: "text"}` (empty leading text block, then thinking, then the answer), zero delta/block-type mismatches across all 462 deltas ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_CombinedChunkSplitter` previously only split a chunk that combined response content with a `finish_reason` (needed for fake-streamed providers like Vertex AI Gemma `:predict`, which collapse the whole response into one chunk). It did not split a chunk that combined `reasoning_content`/`thinking_blocks` with `content` in the same delta, which some vLLM reasoning parsers do at the reasoning/answer boundary. That combined shape hit two functions that disagree on which payload is dominant: `_should_start_new_content_block` (content-block-type detection) checks `content` before `reasoning_content` and picks `text`, while `translate_streaming_openai_response_to_anthropic` (delta emission) checks `reasoning_content` first and picks `thinking_delta`. The mismatch means a `thinking_delta` lands on a block the client was told is `text`. Generalized `_CombinedChunkSplitter` to split on any combination of {reasoning, content/tool_calls, finish_reason} rather than only {content, finish_reason}, so each downstream chunk carries exactly one payload and both functions agree on its type. Existing content+finish_reason behavior is unchanged; a chunk carrying reasoning+content+finish_reason now splits into three single-payload chunks instead of two. Added a regression test (`test_streaming_iterator_reasoning_content_chunk.py`) that replays the captured chunk shape (reasoning tail bundled with content) through the full `AnthropicStreamWrapper` and asserts no delta ever targets a block of the wrong declared type, and that both payloads survive as separate deltas. Updated the existing combined-chunk splitter test that asserted the old (incorrect) two-way split behavior for a reasoning+content+finish chunk to assert the corrected three-way split.
signals.author: streber42

signals.title: fix: include cache_write_tokens in cost calculation for cached-input requests
signals.text: ## Summary Fixes #33772 OpenAI models that report **cache-write** tokens (`cache_write_tokens`) were being mis-priced because LiteLLM's cost path only recognized Anthropic's field name (`cache_creation_tokens`). This caused `response_cost` to be **understated** for any request that writes to the prompt cache -- cache-write tokens were billed at the plain input rate (or zero) instead of the correct 1.25x cache-creation rate. The error compounded across **three separate places** in the cost path, all of which are fixed here. ## Root Cause Analysis ### Pricing Model Background OpenAI's prompt caching has two distinct token categories: - **Cache-read tokens** (`cached_tokens`): tokens served from an existing cache entry, priced at a discount (e.g., 0.1x input) - **Cache-write tokens** (`cache_write_tokens`): tokens written to the cache for the first time, priced at a premium (e.g., 1.25x input) Anthropic uses the field name `cache_creation_tokens` for the same concept as OpenAI's `cache_write_tokens`. LiteLLM's cost engine was only reading the Anthropic field name, so OpenAI cache-write tokens were invisible to the pricing logic. ### Place 1: `_parse_prompt_tokens_details` drops `cache_write_tokens` **File:** `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` The function `_parse_prompt_tokens_details` only read `cache_creation_tokens` (Anthropic's field) from `usage.prompt_tokens_details`. OpenAI reports cache writes under `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` (chat completions) / `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` (responses API), so the cache-write token count arrived as `0` and those tokens were billed at the plain input rate instead of the 1.25x cache-write rate. ### Place 2: Tiered cache-creation cost keys not registered **Files:** `litellm/utils.py`, `litellm/types/utils.py` `get_model_info` copies a fixed set of cost keys onto `ModelInfoBase`, but omitted: - `cache_creation_input_token_cost_priority` - `cache_creation_input_token_cost_flex` - `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_272k_tokens` Even when these keys were defined in the model config, they were silently discarded. The `ModelInfoBase` TypedDict and `_CACHE_PRICING_FIELDS` tuple also lacked these fields. This meant cache-write cost could not vary by service tier (priority/flex) or long-context (>272k) tier. ### Place 3: Responses API usage translation drops the cache-write split **File:** `litellm/responses/utils.py` `ResponseAPILoggingUtils._transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage` builds a `PromptTokensDetailsWrapper` from the Responses API usage but did not map `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` onto the chat-shaped `cache_creation_tokens`. So even after fixing Place 1, requests routed through the Responses API (`/v1/responses`) still lost their cache-write tokens before cost was computed. ## Fix ### Fix 1: Read `cache_write_tokens` with fallback to `cache_creation_tokens` In `_parse_prompt_tokens_details`, the code now reads `cache_write_tokens` first (OpenAI's field), falling back to `cache_creation_tokens` (Anthropic's field). This ensures cache-write tokens are recognized regardless of which provider reports them. ### Fix 2: Register tiered cache-creation cost keys - Added `cache_creation_input_token_cost_priority`, `cache_creation_input_token_cost_flex`, and `cache_creation_input_token_cost_above_272k_tokens` to: - `_CACHE_PRICING_FIELDS` tuple in `litellm/utils.py` - The `ModelInfoBase` constructor call in `get_model_info` - The `ModelInfoBase` TypedDict in `litellm/types/utils.py` This mirrors the existing tiered `cache_read_input_token_cost_*` keys and allows cache-write pricing to vary by service tier and context-length threshold. ### Fix 3: Carry `cache_write_tokens` through Responses API transform In `_transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage`: - **Dict branch**: Maps `cache_write_tokens` -> `cache_creation_tokens` before constructing `PromptTokensDetailsWrapper` - **Object branch**: Reads `cache_write_tokens` via `getattr` and passes it as `cache_creation_tokens` This ensures cost is computed identically regardless of whether a request went through `/chat/completions` or `/responses`. ## Files Changed | File | Change | |------|--------| | `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py` | Read `cache_write_tokens` with fallback to `cache_creation_tokens` in `_parse_prompt_tokens_details` | | `litellm/utils.py` | Add tiered cache-creation keys to `_CACHE_PRICING_FIELDS` and `get_model_info` | | `litellm/types/utils.py` | Add tiered cache-creation fields to `ModelInfoBase` TypedDict | | `litellm/responses/utils.py` | Map `cache_write_tokens` -> `cache_creation_tokens` in Responses API usage transform | ## Verification - Existing `cache_read_tokens` pricing is unchanged (the fix only adds a new field read with fallback) - Existing `cache_creation_tokens` (Anthropic) path is preserved as the fallback - Edge cases handled: if `cache_write_tokens` is `0`, `None`, or missing, the code gracefully falls back to `cache_creation_tokens` or defaults to `0` - The tiered key registration mirrors the existing pattern for `cache_read_input_token_cost_priority` / `_flex` / `_above_272k_tokens` - Both dict and object branches of the Responses API transform are covered ## Impact After this fix, `response_cost` for OpenAI models with prompt caching enabled will correctly reflect: - Cache-write tokens priced at the model's `cache_creation_input_token_cost` rate (typically 1.25x input) - Tiered pricing for priority/flex service tiers and >272k context windows - Consistent pricing across both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses` API paths

signals.title: fix(batches): don't crash logging when a completed batch has no output file
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - All-error batches finish with an error file only, no output file - Polling such a batch crashed the gateway's success logging - None of those polls ever reached the spend logs How it solves it: - Treat a batch with no output file as an empty result - Record zero cost and usage instead of raising ## User Flow Before: every status poll of the all-error batch vanishes from the gateway's spend records, and the gateway console prints a file-retrieval error each time 1. They upload their batch input with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (purpose=batch, target_model_names=gpt-5.5), every JSONL line asking for an out-of-range temperature, and get back a long gateway file id 2. They create the batch with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches using that input_file_id and get back a batch id with "status": "validating" 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} with their virtual key until the response shows "status": "completed" with "output_file_id": null, a real "error_file_id", and request_counts 0 completed / 3 failed 4. They open GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?api_key=<their virtual key> and find rows for the upload and the batch creation but none for any status poll, while the console printed "ValueError: Output file id is None cannot retrieve file content" on every poll After: every status poll is recorded at zero spend and the console stays clean 1. They upload their batch input with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (purpose=batch, target_model_names=gpt-5.5), every JSONL line asking for an out-of-range temperature, and get back a long gateway file id 2. They create the batch with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches using that input_file_id and get back a batch id with "status": "validating" 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} with their virtual key until the response shows "status": "completed" with "output_file_id": null, a real "error_file_id", and request_counts 0 completed / 3 failed 4. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?api_key=<their virtual key> now lists a $0.00 batch-retrieve row for each distinct batch state they polled, including the final completed one, and no error appears in the console ## Relevant issues Fixes #33987 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-4852 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live e2e against real OpenAI batches, all request lines carrying an out-of-range `"temperature": 42` so every line fails provider-side. Both legs ran the identical setup and differ only in the commit the proxy was booted from: fresh Postgres DB, config with `gpt-5.5` (`openai/gpt-5.5`) plus a `files_settings` entry for the plain-provider flow, `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_ENABLED=false` (the OSS shape from #33987, no enterprise cost poller), and a user-bound virtual key **Before, merge base `add095b494cc75440543a240618a88174ea4a445` (proxy port 25200): polls never reach the spend logs** Managed flow (upload with `target_model_names=gpt-5.5`, then create and poll): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:25200/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names=gpt-5.5 -F file=@all_error.jsonl $ curl -s http://localhost:25200/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -d '{"input_file_id":"<unified id>","endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","completion_window":"24h"}' $ curl -s http://localhost:25200/v1/batches/<unified batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" # repeated until terminal {"id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDpkMGI3...", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29u...", "request_counts": {"completed": 0, "failed": 3, "total": 3}} $ curl -s "http://localhost:25200/spend/logs?api_key=$KEY_A" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-master-before" [{"call_type": "acreate_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:47:04.432000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_file", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:55.295000Z"}] ``` 3 polls made, zero `aretrieve_batch` rows. Plain-provider flow (`POST /v1/files?provider=openai`, raw ids) behaves the same: ``` $ curl -s "http://localhost:25200/v1/batches/batch_6a82210c6cb88190804d7ce1fcf18390?provider=openai" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_B" {"id": "batch_6a82210c6cb88190804d7ce1fcf18390", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "file-GvMrtsJxCK3qgtrSgtGJB9", "request_counts": {"completed": 0, "failed": 3, "total": 3}} $ curl -s "http://localhost:25200/spend/logs?api_key=$KEY_B" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-master-before" [{"call_type": "acreate_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:43:55.945000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_file", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:43:47.250000Z"}, {"call_type": "", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T00:34:28.796000Z"}] ``` (the empty-call_type row is from an earlier rejected 403 poll, hours before this run; see observations below) Every one of the 5 polls across both flows produced a `LoggingWorker error: ... ValueError: Output file id is None cannot retrieve file content` traceback in the proxy console, 1:1 with the polls, at any batch status, not just completed **After, PR head `f91e698adbd00b88c3114a276b8a3d0095302ffc` (proxy port 52847): every poll is accounted at $0.00** Same commands, same flows. Managed flow, 6 polls to the same terminal shape: ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:52847/v1/batches/<unified batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" # final poll {"id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDpkMGI3...", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29u...", "request_counts": {"completed": 0, "failed": 3, "total": 3}} $ curl -s "http://localhost:52847/spend/logs?api_key=$KEY_A" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-master-after" [{"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:49:25.338000Z"}, {"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:48:24.724000Z"}, {"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:47:54.473000Z"}, {"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:53.997000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:43.203000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_file", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:36.830000Z"}] ``` Plain-provider flow, 5 polls: ``` $ curl -s "http://localhost:52847/v1/batches/batch_6a8221ca2c588190b4375348ceb759dd?provider=openai" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_B" {"id": "batch_6a8221ca2c588190b4375348ceb759dd", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "file-3rGHqXkyX5g5CQnmfN7sas", "request_counts": {"completed": 0, "failed": 3, "total": 3}} $ curl -s "http://localhost:52847/spend/logs?api_key=$KEY_B" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-master-after" [{"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:49:14.579000Z"}, {"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:48:14.053000Z"}, {"call_type": "aretrieve_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:47:13.494000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:47:05.839000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_file", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:58.840000Z"}] ``` Zero "Output file id is None" occurrences and zero tracebacks in the proxy console across all 11 after-leg polls. Row counts read 4 of 6 and 3 of 5 because the spend log keys retrieve rows on a hash of the response, so consecutive polls observing an identical batch state dedup to one row; that behavior predates this PR, and the row for the completed-observing poll, the one the bug erased, is present in both flows Observed during QA, all pre-existing and untouched by this PR unless noted: - Crash fired on every poll status, this PR fixes all (broader than issue narrative) - Virtual keys without an attached user 403 on managed batches - Spend rows dedup identical consecutive poll states by response hash - All-failed OpenAI batches finish "completed", never "failed" - Plain-provider file upload requires a files_settings config block - Rejected 403 polls still write empty-call_type spend rows ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signals.title: fix(openrouter): preserve shared session when streaming
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Native OpenRouter async streams discard supplied shared HTTP sessions How it solves it: - Propagates `shared_session` through the streaming HTTP handler chain ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix With `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set, I ran the same live OpenRouter streaming request at each commit with an `aiohttp` trace attached to the caller-supplied session ```bash uv run python - <<'PY' import asyncio import subprocess import aiohttp import litellm async def main() -> None: requests = 0 async def count_request(*args: object) -> None: nonlocal requests requests += 1 trace = aiohttp.TraceConfig() trace.on_request_start.append(count_request) async with aiohttp.ClientSession(trace_configs=[trace]) as session: response = await litellm.acompletion( model="openrouter/openai/gpt-5.2", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply only OK"}], max_tokens=4, stream=True, shared_session=session, ) chunks = sum([1 async for _ in response]) commit = subprocess.check_output(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], text=True).strip() print(f"commit={commit}") print(f"shared_session_requests={requests}") print(f"stream_chunks={chunks}") asyncio.run(main()) PY ``` Before: ```text commit=9ab3847c0b2132221aecf858a3ac5c62697359a9 shared_session_requests=0 stream_chunks=3 ``` After: ```text commit=42934718bb5f7566e22d766d4d967e156a69d3bc shared_session_requests=1 stream_chunks=3 ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `shared_session` now reaches the async streaming HTTP client factory, matching the existing non-streaming path The mapped handler test covers the native OpenRouter streaming path and fails if session propagation regresses ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(router): apply order fallback before deployment affinity
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Session affinity can repin explicit order fallbacks. - Retries can select an earlier deployment order again. How it solves it: - Prefilter explicit target orders before affinity callbacks. - Add regression coverage for pinned order-one sessions. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in PR merge, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This bug is in the in-process deployment-selection pipeline and requires no provider request. On base commit `abf18f8`, affinity narrows the candidates to the cached order-1 deployment before `_target_order=2` is applied. Because no order-2 candidate remains, the order helper returns the pinned deployment unchanged. On fix commit `39a58ba`, the explicit target order narrows candidates first, so the stale order-1 pin cannot match. ```console $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_router_order_fallback.py -q ............... [100%] 15 passed ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `async_get_healthy_deployments` now consumes and applies an explicit `_target_order` immediately after health, cooldown, and blocked-deployment filtering. This makes the fallback order a hard retry constraint before `DeploymentAffinityCheck` runs. The existing final order filter remains in place for normal selection, preserving routing-plugin and default-order behavior. The regression test primes session affinity to order 1, verifies an ordinary selection remains pinned there, then verifies an order-2 fallback selects the order-2 deployment. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(anthropic/adapter): stop translate_anthropic_tools_to_openai mutating the caller's input_schema
signals.text: ## Title fix(anthropic/adapter): stop `translate_anthropic_tools_to_openai` mutating the caller's `input_schema` ## Relevant issues Fixes #34510 ## What's broken `translate_anthropic_tools_to_openai` aliases the caller's `input_schema` into `function_chunk["parameters"]`, then the trailing kwargs loop mutates it in place: ```python if "input_schema" in tool: function_chunk["parameters"] = tool["input_schema"] # aliases the source dict ... for k, v in tool.items(): if k not in mapped_tool_params: function_chunk.setdefault("parameters", {}).update({k: v}) # mutates it ``` Extra top-level tool keys (e.g. `display_width_px` / `display_height_px` on a `computer` tool) get merged back into the caller's original `input_schema`. Callers reuse the same tool list across passes: the pass-through guardrail translates the tools in a pre-call hook, then the request is translated again for the real call. On the second pass the schema is already polluted with non-schema keys, and providers that validate the tool `parameters` JSON schema can reject the request or silently receive a corrupted schema. Nothing raises. ## Reproduction (no credentials, pure translation logic) ```python tool = { "name": "computer", "type": "computer_20241022", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"action": {"type": "string"}}}, "display_width_px": 1024, "display_height_px": 768, } adapter.translate_anthropic_tools_to_openai([tool]) ``` ``` before: tool["input_schema"] gains display_width_px / display_height_px # leaked in after: tool["input_schema"] unchanged ``` ## Fix Shallow-copy the schema before assigning, so the kwargs loop updates a fresh dict instead of the caller's: ```python function_chunk["parameters"] = dict(tool["input_schema"] or {}) ``` The translated OpenAI `parameters` still carry the schema plus the intended vendor kwargs; only the leak back into the source is removed. `translate_anthropic_output_format_to_openai` in this same file already copies its schema for the same reason, so this brings the tool path in line with that in-file precedent. Scope note: the tool-level `type` leak into `parameters` was already fixed on `main` (#30557, `type` is now in `mapped_tool_params`). This covers the remaining aliasing/in-place-mutation half. #29669 proposed the copy bundled with the type change but is open and conflicting against an older base, so this isolates the still-unfixed copy against current `main`. ## Testing Added `test_translate_anthropic_tools_to_openai_does_not_mutate_input_schema` next to the #30557 test. It asserts the source tool and its schema are untouched, that the translated parameters still carry both the schema and the vendor kwargs, and that re-translating the reused tool keeps the source clean (the double-translation scenario from the issue). I confirmed it fails on the pre-fix source and passes with the change (reverted only `transformation.py` and the new test went red, restored it and it passed). The two neighbouring tool tests still pass. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix

signals.title: fix(dashscope): select one pricing tier from request input size
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - DashScope cost tracking applies graduated, income-tax-style slicing to `tiered_pricing`, but Alibaba Model Studio picks one tier from a request's total input tokens and bills every token in that request at that tier's rates. Large Qwen requests are logged well under what the provider actually charges - Each token category was tiered independently from zero, so completion tokens selected their own tier and cached input selected a tier from the cached count alone rather than from the request's input size - The proxy's budget reservation path already uses the request-size model via `select_tier_for_input`, so reservation estimates and post-response spend disagreed with each other on the same request How it solves it: - Resolve the tier once in `dashscope/cost_calculator.py` from `usage.prompt_tokens` using `select_tier_for_input`, the selector budget reservation already uses, and apply that one tier's rates to plain input, cached input, completion and reasoning tokens ## Relevant issues Fixes #34729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have DashScope credentials, so this is the repro script from the issue rather than a live proxy run. It makes no provider call; the token counts are synthetic and the rates come straight out of `model_prices_and_context_window.json`. ``` python - <<'PY' from litellm.llms.dashscope.cost_calculator import cost_per_token from litellm.types.utils import Usage from litellm.utils import get_model_info from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.tiered_pricing import ( select_tier_for_input, tier_rate, ) model = "qwen-flash" input_tokens = 300_000 output_tokens = 2_000 usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=input_tokens, completion_tokens=output_tokens, total_tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, ) actual_input, actual_output = cost_per_token(model, usage) model_info = get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider="dashscope") tier = select_tier_for_input(model_info["tiered_pricing"], input_tokens) expected_input = input_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "input_cost_per_token") expected_output = output_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "output_cost_per_token") print({ "actual_total": actual_input + actual_output, "request_tier_total": expected_input + expected_output, }) PY ``` Before, on `24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c`: ``` {'actual_total': 0.024599999999999997, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` After: ``` {'actual_total': 0.079, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` `qwen-flash` declares `[0, 256000]` at $0.05/M input and `[256000, 1000000]` at $0.25/M input. A 300,000-token request sits in the second tier, so Model Studio charges all 300,000 input tokens at $0.25/M and the 2,000 completion tokens at that tier's $2/M. The old result charged the first 256,000 input tokens at the cheap rate and put the completion tokens in tier 1 entirely, which is 69% under. Reverting only `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` and keeping the new tests gives the failures below, so the regression coverage is genuinely pinned to this fix: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py -q --tb=line E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0246, 0.079, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:96: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.012800249999999999, (256001 * 2.5e-07), rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:127: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.2488, 0.3, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:281: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0015999999999999999, 0.002, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:259: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0474, 0.07379999999999999, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:172: assert False FAILED ...::test_dashscope_cached_tokens_count_toward_tier_selection FAILED ...::test_dashscope_input_above_first_tier_bills_whole_request_at_that_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_output_tokens_do_not_select_their_own_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tier_boundary_is_inclusive_of_range_end FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_string_costs_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_with_caching 7 failed, 3 passed in 1.39s ``` With the fix restored: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/ tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/ -q 193 passed in 23.14s $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py -q 80 passed in 4.55s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` now resolves the tier once per request instead of running four independent graduated calculations. `_calculate_prompt_cost` and `_calculate_completion_cost` take the selected tier rather than the whole `tiered_pricing` list, and read their rates with `tier_rate`, which keeps the existing fallbacks (cached input falls back to the tier's input rate, reasoning falls back to the tier's output rate) and the existing string-cost coercion for YAML-parsed rates. The flat-pricing path for models with no `tiered_pricing` is untouched, as is `calculate_tiered_cost` itself for any caller that wants graduated behaviour. A follow-up commit converts the three annotations the fix touches to PEP 604 / PEP 585 form (`dict | None`, `list[dict] | None`), which keeps the strict-rule budget from moving; the file drops from 8 strict violations to 2. The existing tests in `test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` asserted the graduated numbers, so they are updated to the request-size expectations. Five cases were added or reworked to cover what the issue asked for: an above-first-tier request billed wholly at that tier, the tier boundary being inclusive of `range_end` (256,000 stays in tier 1, 256,001 moves up), output tokens not selecting their own tier, cached tokens counting toward tier selection, and input beyond the highest declared range falling back to the last tier. The two string-valued-rate regressions from the earlier YAML coercion fix are kept, with expectations recomputed under the new model. ## QA runbook Point a deployment at a DashScope Qwen model with `tiered_pricing` in the cost map (`qwen-flash` or `qwen3-coder-plus`), send one request whose input is comfortably above the first tier's `range_end` and one below it, then compare `spend` on the two `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` rows against the Model Studio console for the same requests. The large request should now be priced entirely at the higher tier rather than partly at the cheap one, and it should match the budget reservation estimate for that request rather than falling short of it. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(proxy): add project-level ITPM and OTPM quotas
signals.text: ## Problem this solves: - Projects cannot enforce separate input and output TPM quotas How it solves it: - Stores model ITPM and OTPM maps in project metadata - Reserves and reconciles input and output tokens independently - Handles Responses, multimodal inputs, caching, and cancellation safely ## Relevant issues - Builds on #31952 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Local functional validation I validated the project-level ITPM and OTPM enforcement through a locally running LiteLLM proxy using a deterministic mock model ### Environment The proxy was started from branch `feature/bedrock-mantle-quota-project-itr1` with PostgreSQL-backed virtual keys and the following mock deployment: ```yaml - model_name: mock-gpt-4o litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o api_key: fake-key mock_response: "This is a mock response for testing rate limits." ``` The mock response avoids external provider calls while exercising the complete proxy authentication, project metadata, pre-call reservation, rate-limit response, and reconciliation paths ### Project quota configuration The OSS `/project/update` endpoint is Enterprise-gated, so I populated the existing local project record using the same metadata representation produced by the management endpoint: ```sql UPDATE "LiteLLM_ProjectTable" SET metadata = '{ "model_itpm_limit": {"mock-gpt-4o": 50}, "model_otpm_limit": {"mock-gpt-4o": 50} }'::jsonb, models = ARRAY['mock-gpt-4o'] WHERE project_id = 'test-itpm-project-001' RETURNING project_id, metadata, models; ``` The database returned: ```text project_id | metadata | models -----------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------- test-itpm-project-001 | {"model_itpm_limit":{"mock-gpt-4o":50},"model_otpm_limit":{"mock-gpt-4o":50}} | {mock-gpt-4o} ``` I then generated a virtual key associated with `test-itpm-project-001` and used that key for the following requests ### Candidate-aware OTPM rejection This request asks for two completion candidates with a maximum of 30 output tokens each: ```bash curl -i http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LOCAL_PROJECT_KEY}" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "mock-gpt-4o", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "max_tokens": 30, "n": 2 }' ``` The pre-call reservation is `30 × 2 = 60` output tokens, which exceeds the project OTPM limit of 50 Observed response: ```text HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests retry-after: 60 rate_limit_type: tokens x-litellm-response-cost: 0 { "error": { "message": "Rate limit exceeded for model_per_project_otpm: test-itpm-project-001:mock-gpt-4o. Limit type: tokens. Current limit: 50, Remaining: 50", "type": "throttling_error", "param": null, "code": "429" } } ``` The `model_per_project_otpm` descriptor rejected the request before provider dispatch, and the remaining quota stayed at 50 because the rejected reservation was not applied ### Under-limit request I then sent a single-candidate request with a maximum of 20 output tokens: ```bash curl -i http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${LOCAL_PROJECT_KEY}" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "mock-gpt-4o", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], "max_tokens": 20 }' ``` Observed response: ```text HTTP/1.1 200 OK x-litellm-model-group: mock-gpt-4o x-ratelimit-model_per_project_itpm-remaining-tokens: 42 x-ratelimit-model_per_project_itpm-limit-tokens: 50 x-ratelimit-model_per_project_otpm-remaining-tokens: 30 x-ratelimit-model_per_project_otpm-limit-tokens: 50 { "model": "mock-gpt-4o", "object": "chat.completion", "choices": [ { "finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": { "content": "This is a mock response for testing rate limits.", "role": "assistant" } } ], "usage": { "completion_tokens": 20, "prompt_tokens": 10, "total_tokens": 30 } } ``` This confirms that project ITPM and OTPM limits are loaded from project metadata, exposed through independent rate-limit headers, and enforced using separate token counters It also confirms that multiple completion candidates reserve `max_tokens × candidate_count`, over-limit reservations are rejected atomically, and an under-limit request succeeds and reports its input and output quota state This validation covers the proxy-level project quota behavior with a deterministic mock response and does not validate Bedrock credentials or live AWS service quotas ## Type New Feature ## Changes - Adds `model_itpm_limit` and `model_otpm_limit` to project create and update requests - Stores both maps in existing project metadata without a database migration - Adds independent project ITPM and OTPM rate-limit descriptors - Reserves estimated input and output usage before provider dispatch - Reconciles reservations against actual usage after completion - Excludes cached prompt-read tokens from project ITPM accounting - Preserves reservations when stream cancellation leaves usage unknown - Enforces project quotas for every Responses WebSocket `response.create` frame - Reconciles aggregate-only usage without retaining inflated reservations - Uses endpoint-specific input fields and output cap parameters - Conservatively handles Responses file references and chained responses - Regenerates dashboard API types with numeric quota map values ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including edge cases and the reported real-world quota paths Docs PR https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm-docs/pull/638

signals.title: fix(guardrails): send image parts to bedrock ApplyGuardrail
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock guardrail never saw image input - IMAGE modality guardrails scanned only neighbouring text - Masking could drop image parts from the request How it solves it: - Send image content items in the ApplyGuardrail INPUT payload - Decode inline/remote images via existing `BedrockImageProcessor` - Skip formats ApplyGuardrail rejects instead of failing the call ## Relevant issues Fixes #35332 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I could not capture live proof here: this sandbox's network allowlist blocks AWS, so `bedrock-runtime.*.amazonaws.com` is unreachable and no ApplyGuardrail call can be made. What follows is the runbook that reproduces the miss and the fix against a real guardrail; the reporter's own numbers in #35332 (`textCharacters {total: 67}`, `imageUnits: 0` for a request carrying a 2,296-char base64 image) are the "before" side of it. Prerequisites: a Bedrock guardrail with both TEXT and IMAGE modalities enabled on its content policy, and an image the guardrail flags (the reporter used a scam-SMS screenshot flagged `MISCONDUCT / HIGH`) ```bash # 1. config cat > /tmp/guardrail_config.yaml <<'YAML' model_list: - model_name: claude litellm_params: model: bedrock/anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 guardrails: - guardrail_name: bedrock-image litellm_params: guardrail: bedrock mode: pre_call guardrailIdentifier: <your-guardrail-id> guardrailVersion: DRAFT YAML # 2. run the proxy (before: on litellm_internal_staging, after: on this branch) python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/guardrail_config.yaml --detailed_debug 2>&1 | tee litellm.log # 3. send the flagged image IMG=$(base64 -w0 scam-sms.png) curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"claude\",\"guardrails\":[\"bedrock-image\"],\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"what does this say?\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"data:image/png;base64,$IMG\"}}]}]}" # 4. what the guardrail actually got grep -i 'imageUnits\|textCharacters\|GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED' litellm.log ``` Before, step 4 shows `imageUnits: 0` and the request returns 200 with a model answer; after, the image counts as an image unit and the flagged screenshot returns `GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED` (HTTP 400 from the proxy) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_create_bedrock_input_content_request` walked every message through `get_content_items_for_message`, which keeps list items only when they carry a `text` key. An OpenAI image part (`{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {...}}`) has no such key, so it fell through both branches and never reached ApplyGuardrail, while the text part sitting next to it in the same message was scanned; `BedrockContentItem` had no `image` field to put it in either. Input assembly now builds content items per part rather than per extracted text block: ```python async def _build_input_content_item(self, item: object) -> Optional[BedrockContentItem]: if isinstance(item, str): return BedrockContentItem(text=BedrockTextContent(text=item)) part = cast(Mapping[str, object], item) text = part.get("text") if isinstance(text, str): return BedrockContentItem(text=BedrockTextContent(text=text)) image_url = self._get_image_url(item=part) return await self._build_image_content_item(image_url=image_url) if image_url else None ``` Images go through `BedrockImageProcessor.process_image_async`, the same decoder the Converse path uses, so inline base64 data URIs and remote urls both work and the fetches for a multi-image message run concurrently. That is what makes `convert_to_bedrock_format` (and its two callers) async. ApplyGuardrail takes png and jpeg only, unlike Converse; anything else (gif, webp, an unreachable url) is left out with a warning rather than sent and turned into a validation error that would fail the whole scan. One adjacent fix: `_mask_content_list` rebuilt message content from the parts it recognised and silently discarded the rest, so a masked request lost its image before reaching the model. Unrecognised parts are now carried through untouched. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(ui): make Inception selectable in the Add Model provider dropdown
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Inception cannot be selected in the Admin UI Add Model form - Backend fully supports it; the provider metadata file omits it - So mercury-2 cannot be onboarded from the dashboard How it solves it: - Add Inception to `provider_create_fields.json`, which drives the dropdown - Add the matching `Providers` and `provider_map` members for display name and logo - Convert `getPlaceholder` to a lookup map to stay under the complexity ceiling ## Relevant issues Fixes #35209 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at commit `2dd0a66b`, against a live proxy on localhost:4000 and the dashboard dev server, using a real Inception API key against the real api.inceptionlabs.ai endpoint and costing real $ `local_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: mercury-2 litellm_params: model: inception/mercury-2 api_key: os.environ/INCEPTION_API_KEY ``` 1. Before, on the base branch: filtering the provider dropdown for "incep" returns "No data", even though `GET /public/providers` already lists `inception` and the cost map already has `inception/mercury-2` 2. After: the same filter now matches Inception 3. Selecting it fills the provider field, and the model dropdown offers `inception/mercury-2` alongside the INCEPTION wildcard, so onboarding mercury-2 is a one-click flow 4. The endpoint that backs the dropdown now serves the provider: ``` $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/public/providers/fields | \ python -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print([(e['provider'],e['provider_display_name']) for e in d if e['provider']=='INCEPTION'])" [('INCEPTION', 'Inception')] ``` 5. Real chat completion routed through the proxy to Inception: ``` $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "mercury-2", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "In one sentence, what is a diffusion language model?"}]}' { "id": "chatcmpl-65efa4fa-a581-48d9-aac6-d9428ec8c22a", "model": "mercury-2", "object": "chat.completion", "choices": [ { "finish_reason": "stop", "index": 0, "message": { "content": "A diffusion language model is a type of generative model that produces text by iteratively denoising a random latent representation, allowing many tokens to be generated in parallel rather than one-by-one.", "role": "assistant" } } ], "usage": {"completion_tokens": 39, "prompt_tokens": 11, "total_tokens": 91, "cached_input_tokens": 3} } ``` 6. Spend is attributed to the `inception` provider off the existing cost-map entry: ``` $ curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/spend/logs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_MASTER_KEY" { "model": "inception/mercury-2", "custom_llm_provider": "inception", "spend": 3.35e-05, "prompt_tokens": 11, "completion_tokens": 39 } ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes `inception` is already a member of `LlmProviders`, so `GET /public/providers` returns it, and the provider ships both chat and completion transformations under `litellm/llms/inception/` along with an `inception/mercury-2` entry in the model cost map. What was missing was the Admin UI The Add Model provider dropdown is not built from the frontend `Providers` enum. `AddModelForm` renders its options entirely from `useProviderFields()`, which fetches `/public/providers/fields`, and that endpoint serves `litellm/proxy/public_endpoints/provider_create_fields.json` verbatim. A provider absent from that file simply cannot be picked, which is what made Inception unselectable. The entry is added with `api_key` required and `api_base` optional, matching how the other openai-compatible providers that ship a default `api_base` are described The `Select` uses `providerInfo.provider` as the option value, and that key flows into `ProviderLogo` and `getProviderModels`. So `Providers` and `provider_map` need the matching `INCEPTION` member as well, otherwise the option renders with the raw slug as its label and the model dropdown cannot resolve the `inception` models. Inception has no bundled logo asset, so it joins the known logoless set alongside the other providers that render without one `getPlaceholder` was already sitting exactly at the eslint `complexity` ceiling of 20, so adding one more `else if` branch pushed it to 21 and introduced a fresh lint warning. Rather than spend the budget headroom, the chain is now a `providerPlaceholders` lookup keyed by the enum value with the existing `gpt-3.5-turbo` fallback. Behaviour is unchanged and the existing `getPlaceholder` tests cover it One note on diff size: `ruff format` reflows a number of pre-existing lines in `test_public_endpoints.py`. That file was already non-conforming on the base branch, and the diff-scoped format check covers any file a PR touches, so the reformat comes along with the two tests added there ## QA runbook ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
