signal.title: [Bug]: Bedrock GPT-5.6 entries use mode responses and a smaller context than OpenAI/Azure
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Rescoped on 2026-08-16 after re-validating against `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. The missing long-context pricing is fixed; the metadata mismatch is not The three Bedrock GPT-5.6 entries still declare `"mode": "responses"` and `"supported_endpoints": ["/v1/responses"]`, while the 16 OpenAI and Azure entries for the same models declare `"mode": "chat"` with `["/v1/chat/completions", "/v1/batch", "/v1/responses"]`. `max_input_tokens` is also 1000000 on Bedrock against 1050000 everywhere else ``` bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol mode=responses max_input_tokens=1000000 endpoints=['/v1/responses'] gpt-5.6-sol mode=chat max_input_tokens=1050000 endpoints=['/v1/chat/completions', '/v1/batch', '/v1/responses'] ``` The practical effect is that these models do not present as chat models on Bedrock, so anything keying off `mode` or `supported_endpoints` (model discovery, the chat-completions surface, UI filtering) treats them differently from the identical model on other providers One caveat for whoever fixes this: the `mode` value is load-bearing, not cosmetic. `mantle_supports_responses` in `litellm/llms/bedrock_mantle/common_utils.py` gates native Responses routing on `/v1/responses` being in `supported_endpoints` or `mode == "responses"`, and `mantle_base_segment` uses the `use_openai_responses_path` flag to put gpt-5.x on the `/openai/v1` base. The chat config's own docstring says that base serves both `/responses` and `/chat/completions`. So the safe change is flipping `mode` to `"chat"` and adding `/v1/chat/completions` to `supported_endpoints` while keeping `/v1/responses` and `use_openai_responses_path`, which preserves the gate Also note the entries live under the `bedrock_mantle/` prefix rather than `bedrock/`, and there is no `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6` matching OpenAI's unsuffixed `gpt-5.6` ### What changed since this issue was filed Commit `ef305fe4ab` ([#36698](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/36698)) added the 1M context window and the above-272k tiers to all three Bedrock entries, so the original "no costs above 272k" complaint is resolved. The remaining price delta against base OpenAI is a uniform 1.1x (5.5e-06 vs 5e-06 input on sol, and so on), matching the uplift the `azure/us/*` and `azure/eu/*` entries already use, so I no longer believe the prices themselves are wrong ### Steps to Reproduce N/A ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? _No response_ ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? Rescoped on 2026-08-16 after re-validating against `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. The team-policy half of this report was fixed by [#36102](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/36102) and has been removed; see the note at the bottom The pre-call `_PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter` swallows every non-`HTTPException` and returns normally, so this enforcement layer silently disappears whenever it cannot read spend: ```python except HTTPException as e: raise e except Exception as e: verbose_logger.exception( "litellm.proxy.hooks.max_budget_limiter.py::async_pre_call_hook(): Exception occured - %s", e ) ``` `get_current_spend` reaches the dual cache and, on a miss, the database. A Redis outage, a cache client error, or any runtime error inside that call therefore turns the hook into a no-op with no signal to the caller and no distinguishing metric. The failure looks identical to a request that was checked and allowed `common_checks` and budget reservation normally still enforce, so this is not a claim that every request bypasses all budget controls. The defect is that a registered defense-in-depth hook reports success when it could not evaluate anything, which matters exactly in the infrastructure-degraded conditions it exists to cover, and for any path relying on this hook rather than the central check ### Steps to Reproduce No LLM call is needed: ```python from types import SimpleNamespace from unittest.mock import AsyncMock, patch from litellm.proxy.hooks.max_budget_limiter import _PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter auth = SimpleNamespace( user_max_budget=10.0, user_id="user-1", user_spend=20.0, team_id=None, budget_reservation=None, ) with patch( "litellm.proxy.proxy_server.get_current_spend", new=AsyncMock(side_effect=RuntimeError("cache down")), ): await _PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter().async_pre_call_hook( user_api_key_dict=auth, cache=None, data={"model": "gpt-4o"}, call_type="completion", ) ``` Observed: the exception is logged and the hook returns normally, admitting a user who is already at twice their budget ### Expected behavior Infrastructure failures should follow an explicit policy rather than an unconditional broad swallow. Reusing the existing `fail_closed_budget_enforcement` setting would be consistent with the reservation path, which already consults it when a counter write fails. At minimum the fail-open should be narrowed to expected exception types and should emit a metric so operators can see that enforcement degraded A regression should cover a raising spend lookup with the fail-closed setting both on and off. `tests/test_litellm/proxy/hooks/test_max_budget_limiter.py` has no test that makes `get_current_spend` raise ### What changed since this issue was filed The original first half reported that the hook returned early for every request with a non-null `team_id`, ignoring the central team-key policy. Commit `527dc0a8bb` ([#36102](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/36102)) replaced `skip_user_budget_on_team_key` with the inverted opt-in `apply_user_budget_to_team_keys`, and the hook now gates on the same setting as `common_checks` and budget reservation. Regression coverage exists for the flag both on and off. That half is resolved ### Relevant log output ```shell litellm.proxy.hooks.max_budget_limiter.py::async_pre_call_hook(): Exception occured - cache down # request hook still completes successfully ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? Re-validated on `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. Originally filed against `65ca095d4d15a82372e53a547a2390a69f7e1797` ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: spend-log batches are dropped when a non-transport database write fails
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? Rescoped on 2026-08-16 after re-validating against `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. The transport-failure half of the original report is fixed; the non-transport half is not, and is now deliberate. Details of what changed are at the bottom Spend-log batches are detached from the in-memory queue before their database write succeeds. `update_spend_logs_job` pops up to `MAX_LOGS_PER_INTERVAL` rows through `dequeue_spend_logs` and hands the detached list to `ProxyUpdateSpend.update_spend_logs`. Inside the retry loop, anything that fails `PrismaDBExceptionHandler.is_database_transport_error` is re-raised immediately, with no requeue and no dead-letter: ```python except Exception as e: if not PrismaDBExceptionHandler.is_database_transport_error(e): raise ... if i >= n_retry_times: await enqueue_spend_logs(prisma_client, logs_to_process, at_head=True) raise ``` `is_database_transport_error` matches only connection-typed errors and PrismaError messages containing connection keywords. A batch-level failure that is not connection-shaped therefore destroys the whole batch on the first attempt. Realistic triggers are a deadlock or serialization failure under concurrent writers, an engine-internal error, a statement timeout on an oversized batch, and a transiently missing table or column during a rolling migration. All of these are recoverable on a later attempt, but none of them look like a transport error The result is missing rows in `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` for requests that completed and that may already have updated entity spend counters, so audit history, per-request cost reporting, and billing built from spend logs are silently incomplete. Nothing surfaces the loss beyond a log line The poison-row isolation from [#31705](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/31705) covers the case this drop is designed for, namely individual rows the database will keep rejecting. It operates per row, so a batch-level rejection bypasses it entirely and takes every row in the batch with it Expected behavior is that a batch-level non-transport failure is not treated as successful persistence. A bounded retry count per batch, or a dead-letter buffer with a metric, would keep the queue from wedging on a genuinely permanent rejection while still not discarding recoverable ones. The current binary choice between "requeue forever" and "drop silently" is what makes this lossy ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Put two known rows in `prisma_client.spend_log_transactions` 2. Make the batch write raise a non-transport error, for example a deadlock or a plain `RuntimeError` 3. Call `update_spend_logs_job` 4. Inspect `prisma_client.spend_log_transactions` 5. Observe both rows are gone even though no insert succeeded ```python prisma.spend_log_transactions = [ {"request_id": "r1"}, {"request_id": "r2"}, ] with patch( "litellm.proxy.utils._create_spend_logs_with_poison_isolation", AsyncMock(side_effect=RuntimeError("deadlock detected")), ): with pytest.raises(RuntimeError): await ProxyUpdateSpend.update_spend_logs( n_retry_times=0, prisma_client=prisma, db_writer_client=None, proxy_logging_obj=proxy_logging, ) assert prisma.spend_log_transactions == [] # current behavior ``` Note that `test_update_spend_logs_does_not_requeue_non_transport_failures` in `tests/test_litellm/proxy/utils/prisma_and_spend/test_proxy_update_spend.py` currently asserts exactly this behavior, so any fix has to replace that test rather than just add one ### What changed since this issue was filed Commit `6e7984e537` ([#36716](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/36716)) fixed the transport-error path. `update_spend_logs` now calls `enqueue_spend_logs(..., at_head=True)` before re-raising once retries are exhausted, `update_spend_logs_job` requeues at head on `asyncio.CancelledError`, the "do not put the logs back" comment is gone, and the queue is byte-bounded through the `enqueue_spend_logs` / `dequeue_spend_logs` pair. Regression coverage is in `test_proxy_update_spend.py`. The original text of this issue, which framed the loss as happening after connection retries are exhausted, no longer applies and has been rewritten Related issue [#27704](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/27704) reports one real startup condition that causes spend-log writes to fail ### Relevant log output ```shell [Non-Blocking]LiteLLM Prisma Client Exception - update spend logs: deadlock detected db_failure_raised=True db_queue_after=0 ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? Re-validated on `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e986`. Originally filed against v1.94.0 at `3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74` ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: Pass-through endpoints from raw config dicts skip centralized common checks
signal.text: ### Summary A pass-through endpoint supplied as a raw dictionary with no `auth` key still requires a valid LiteLLM key, but it silently skips the centralized common checks that an `auth: true` endpoint gets. Three call sites read the same `auth` field with two different defaults This report has been rescoped. It originally claimed such an endpoint was completely unauthenticated. That is not true at HEAD, and I have removed the open-proxy framing. `create_pass_through_route()` puts `user_api_key_dict: UserAPIKeyAuth = Depends(user_api_key_auth)` in the generated handler's own signature, independent of the route-level `dependencies` list, and `check_api_key_for_custom_headers_or_pass_through_endpoints()` reads `endpoint.get("auth", True) is not True`. Both landed in `148485c2a2`, which closed GHSA-7h34-mmrh-6g58. I verified by registering the raw dict below against a `FastAPI` app: route-level `dependencies` is empty, but the resolved `route.dependant.dependencies` still contains `user_api_key_auth` ### Current behavior `_register_pass_through_endpoint()` accepts either a `PassThroughGenericEndpoint` or a raw dictionary. For a Pydantic object, `model_dump()` materializes the default `auth=True`. For a raw dictionary, the registration code reads the field with no default: ~~~python auth: Final[bool | str | None] = endpoint_data.get("auth") dependencies = None auth_enforced: Final = auth is not None and str(auth).lower() == "true" if auth_enforced: dependencies = [Depends(user_api_key_auth)] if path not in LiteLLMRoutes.openai_routes.value: LiteLLMRoutes.openai_routes.value.append(path) ~~~ So `auth` omitted from a raw config gives `auth_enforced=False`, and the path is never appended to `LiteLLMRoutes.openai_routes`. `_run_centralized_common_checks()` then early-returns for that route, using a third reading of the same field that also has no default: ~~~python if isinstance(endpoint, dict) and endpoint.get("path", "") == route and endpoint.get("auth") is not True: return ~~~ The net effect is a key-authenticated endpoint that never runs model-access checks, key/team/user budget checks, or route guardrails, because the proxy classifies it as an explicitly-unauthenticated forwarder ### Reproduction ~~~yaml general_settings: pass_through_endpoints: - path: /internal/provider target: https://upstream.example.test # auth is omitted ~~~ An unauthenticated call is rejected, which is correct and is the part that changed since this issue was filed: ~~~bash curl -i http://localhost:4000/internal/provider # 401 ~~~ A call with a valid key belonging to a fully exhausted budget succeeds anyway, because the centralized checks were skipped. Compare against the same config with `auth: true`, where the request is rejected on budget ### Impact Model-access restrictions, budget enforcement, and guardrails are silently inert on any pass-through endpoint configured as a raw dict without an explicit `auth: true`. Authentication itself is intact, so this is a policy-enforcement gap rather than an exposure ### Expected behavior Read the field consistently. Either normalize every endpoint through `PassThroughGenericEndpoint` before registration, or default the two remaining raw-dict reads to `True` so all three call sites agree: - `pass_through_endpoints.py`, `_register_pass_through_endpoint`: `endpoint_data.get("auth", True)` - `user_api_key_auth.py`, `_run_centralized_common_checks`: `endpoint.get("auth", True) is not True` `tests/test_litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/test_passthrough_auth_default.py` already covers the authentication default from the GHSA fix, so the new regression only needs to assert that a raw dict without `auth` reaches `_run_centralized_common_checks` Related issues [#32202](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/32202) and [#26399](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/26399) discuss other pass-through security boundaries and do not duplicate this default mismatch ### Source - `litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/pass_through_endpoints.py`, `_register_pass_through_endpoint` - `litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py`, `_run_centralized_common_checks` and `check_api_key_for_custom_headers_or_pass_through_endpoints` - `litellm/proxy/_types.py`, `PassThroughGenericEndpoint.auth`

signal.title: [Security]: Cached proxy-admin keys bypass blocked-key checks
signal.text: ### Summary A cached key whose role is `PROXY_ADMIN` returns from `user_api_key_auth()` before the normal `blocked` check. A stale local cache entry on another worker can therefore continue to authenticate after the key has been blocked in the database ### Current behavior After loading a cached `UserAPIKeyAuth`, the proxy has a privileged early return for proxy-admin keys. That path checks expiration and updates request context, but it does not check `valid_token.blocked` The ordinary non-admin path checks `valid_token.blocked` later `block_key()` updates the database and attempts to delete the key from the local cache and the shared cache. The invalidation is not guaranteed to synchronously remove a stale entry from every worker. A worker that still serves the old cached admin object reaches the privileged early return and never consults the database ### Reproduction Use two proxy workers with a shared database and cache: 1. Authenticate an admin key through worker B so its local cache contains `blocked=False` 2. Block the key through the management API or directly in the database 3. Make another request with the same key through worker B before its local cache refreshes 4. Observe that the request passes the admin early-return path, while a normal key would reach the blocked-key check A focused test can construct a cached `UserAPIKeyAuth(user_role=PROXY_ADMIN, blocked=False)`, make the shared cache miss or stale, and assert that `user_api_key_auth()` does not authorize the key after an authoritative blocked record is present ### Impact Blocking an admin key is not an immediate revocation guarantee across workers. The stale key can continue to access management and model routes for the cache lifetime or until invalidation succeeds ### Expected behavior Run the blocked-key check before any privileged early return. For proxy-admin keys, either revalidate the blocked state against the database on every request or use a revocation version or generation that can be checked across workers without trusting the stale object Add a multi-worker cache invalidation test that blocks a warmed admin key and verifies the next request is rejected ### Source - `litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py`, cached `PROXY_ADMIN` early return - `litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py`, normal blocked-key check - `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py`, `_delete_cache_key_object`

signal.title: [Bug]: New DB deployments are dropped during router upsert when no existing deployment is found
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? Database-backed deployments are dropped from a proxy pod's in-memory router when they are loaded for the first time through `Router.upsert_deployment()` This affects startup and periodic database reloads. Static configuration deployments remain available, while database deployments disappear from model-list endpoints and cannot receive traffic. Model creation can persist the row successfully and then return an internal error because the new deployment is not live in the pod after reload The regression was introduced by commit [300e710bc34](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/300e710bc34). `upsert_deployment()` calls `get_deployment()`, which returns `None` for a deployment that is new to the current router. It then unconditionally passes that value to `_unregister_pre_routing_strategy_for_deployment()`, where `deployment.litellm_params` is dereferenced With `ignore_invalid_deployments=True`, the resulting `AttributeError` is caught and the deployment is silently dropped Expected behavior: a previously unseen database deployment is added to the router, indexed by model ID, and returned by model-list endpoints ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run the following against a version containing commit `300e710bc34` ```python from litellm import Router from litellm.types.router import Deployment, LiteLLM_Params, ModelInfo router = Router(model_list=[], ignore_invalid_deployments=True) deployment = Deployment( model_name="database-model", litellm_params=LiteLLM_Params(model="openai/gpt-4o"), model_info=ModelInfo(id="database-model-1", db_model=True), ) result = router.upsert_deployment(deployment=deployment) print(result) print(router.get_model_list()) ``` 2. Observe that `result` is `None` and the router model list remains empty 3. Set `ignore_invalid_deployments=False` to observe the underlying `AttributeError` A minimal fix is to call the unregister helper only when `_deployment_on_router is not None` A focused regression test should start with an empty router, upsert a new database deployment, and assert that the deployment is returned, retrievable by model ID, and present in the model list ### Relevant log output ```shell Error upserting deployment database-model (id=database-model-1): 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'litellm_params'. Dropping it and continuing with other deployments ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? `litellm_internal_staging` containing commit `300e710bc34` ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: Nullable DailyTagSpend conflict columns cause duplicate inserts and database CPU exhaustion
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? `LiteLLM_DailyTagSpend` can accumulate many physical rows for the same logical spend key when `custom_llm_provider` is `NULL`. The repeated inserts increase table/index size and can make daily-spend flushes consume most of the PostgreSQL CPU. Spend reporting also becomes fragmented across duplicate rows. I expected repeated daily tag-spend updates for the same `(tag, date, api_key, model, custom_llm_provider, mcp_namespaced_tool_name, endpoint)` key to update one row. The current implementation does not enforce that behavior when a conflict column is nullable: 1. The Prisma schema makes `tag`, `model`, `custom_llm_provider`, `mcp_namespaced_tool_name`, and `endpoint` nullable, then includes all of them in a normal composite unique constraint: [`schema.prisma#L878-L900`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74/litellm/proxy/schema.prisma#L878-L900). 2. PostgreSQL treats `NULL` values as distinct in a normal unique constraint, so the constraint permits multiple otherwise-identical rows when any conflict column is `NULL`. 3. `_update_daily_spend` also constructs inconsistent upsert values. The `where` selector converts a missing provider to `""`, while the create payload preserves `None`: [`db_spend_update_writer.py#L1513-L1539`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74/litellm/proxy/db/db_spend_update_writer.py#L1513-L1539). ```python # where "custom_llm_provider": transaction.get("custom_llm_provider") or "", # create "custom_llm_provider": transaction.get("custom_llm_provider"), ``` The selector therefore looks for an empty string while a create writes `NULL`. The next flush does not select that row, and PostgreSQL's unique constraint does not reject another `NULL`, so another row can be inserted. The same generic function writes the user, team, organization, end-user, agent, and tag daily-spend tables, whose composite constraints also contain nullable columns. `DailyTagSpend` was the table where the operational impact was observed, but the invariant should be reviewed for all six tables. In one anonymized PostgreSQL 16 deployment running LiteLLM 1.94.0: - `LiteLLM_DailyTagSpend` reached approximately 5.15 million rows and 3.47 GB including indexes. - A one-day sample found 1,647 duplicate physical rows across six logical keys. - The largest logical-key group contained approximately 804 physical rows. - Daily tag-spend upserts dominated database execution count and drove sustained high CPU. - The deployment had 28 proxy workers. Each worker initializes the scheduler, which amplifies pressure when many flushes are active, although locking can limit simultaneous execution. The current upstream code at commit [`3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74) still contains the schema and create/lookup mismatch. The writer also issues as many as 100 individual Prisma upserts per batch ([`db_spend_update_writer.py#L1472-L1500`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74/litellm/proxy/db/db_spend_update_writer.py#L1472-L1500), [`#L1587-L1593`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74/litellm/proxy/db/db_spend_update_writer.py#L1587-L1593)). That is not the correctness bug, but it magnifies the database cost once duplicate-producing keys are flushed repeatedly. Possible fixes: - Choose one canonical representation for every conflict-key field and use it consistently in the aggregation key, `where`, and `create` payloads. - Backfill/deduplicate existing rows, then enforce the chosen invariant at the database layer, for example with non-null canonical values or a PostgreSQL `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` unique constraint where supported. - Add a PostgreSQL integration test that performs the same upsert twice with each nullable conflict field set to `None` and asserts that only one physical row exists and its counters were incremented. Mock-only tests cannot detect PostgreSQL's `NULL` uniqueness behavior. - Consider a set-based upsert per batch to reduce query execution count independently of the correctness fix. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Use PostgreSQL with the current `LiteLLM_DailyTagSpend` schema. 2. Process the same daily tag-spend transaction more than once with `custom_llm_provider=None` and all other logical-key values unchanged. This can be exercised through `_update_daily_spend` using `entity_type="tag"`; the current test suite already permits `None` in this field but only mocks the Prisma table call. 3. Alternatively, the database behavior can be demonstrated directly with the equivalent conflict key: ```sql CREATE TEMP TABLE daily_tag_spend_repro ( tag text, spend_date text NOT NULL, api_key text NOT NULL, model text, custom_llm_provider text, mcp_namespaced_tool_name text, endpoint text, api_requests bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, UNIQUE ( tag, spend_date, api_key, model, custom_llm_provider, mcp_namespaced_tool_name, endpoint ) ); INSERT INTO daily_tag_spend_repro (tag, spend_date, api_key, model, custom_llm_provider, mcp_namespaced_tool_name, endpoint, api_requests) VALUES ('repro-tag', '2026-01-01', 'repro-key', 'repro-model', NULL, '', '', 1) ON CONFLICT ( tag, spend_date, api_key, model, custom_llm_provider, mcp_namespaced_tool_name, endpoint ) DO UPDATE SET api_requests = daily_tag_spend_repro.api_requests + 1; -- Run the same INSERT a second time, then inspect the result. SELECT tag, spend_date, api_key, model, custom_llm_provider, mcp_namespaced_tool_name, endpoint, COUNT(*) AS physical_rows, SUM(api_requests) AS requests FROM daily_tag_spend_repro GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7; ``` 4. Observe `physical_rows = 2` and two rows with `api_requests = 1`, instead of one row with `api_requests = 2`. 5. On a LiteLLM database, duplicate logical keys can be detected with: ```sql SELECT tag, date, api_key, model, custom_llm_provider, mcp_namespaced_tool_name, endpoint, COUNT(*) AS physical_rows FROM "LiteLLM_DailyTagSpend" GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY physical_rows DESC; ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell No application error is required. The upserts succeed as inserts because PostgreSQL considers NULL conflict-key values distinct. ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.94.0; also verified in upstream commit 3f9b71c1a45e870d1789ee105bd59b9274bb0d74 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: [Bug]: DashScope tiered pricing uses graduated slices instead of the request-size tier
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I searched open and closed issues before filing - [x] #30738 concerns string coercion inside DashScope tier data and #21249 concerns missing flat prices during budget enforcement, so neither covers this pricing-model mismatch ### What happened? The DashScope cost calculator applies graduated, income-tax-style slicing to `tiered_pricing`, while Alibaba Model Studio selects one tier from the total input-token count and bills all input and output tokens at that tier's unit prices The proxy budget reservation code already implements the request-size model through `select_tier_for_input`, so reservation estimates and post-response spend accounting also disagree with each other This can materially understate logged spend and weaken budget enforcement for large Qwen requests. Cached input is especially inconsistent because the current calculator tiers the cached-token count independently from zero instead of selecting a rate from the request's total input size Alibaba's current pricing rule is documented here: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing The relevant rule says the unit price is selected by total input tokens in one request and all tokens in that request use the corresponding tier All token counts in the reproduction are synthetic and no provider request is made ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Check out commit `24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c` 2. Run this script from the repository root ```python from litellm.llms.dashscope.cost_calculator import cost_per_token from litellm.types.utils import Usage from litellm.utils import get_model_info from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.tiered_pricing import ( select_tier_for_input, tier_rate, ) model = "qwen-flash" input_tokens = 300_000 output_tokens = 2_000 usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=input_tokens, completion_tokens=output_tokens, total_tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, ) actual_input, actual_output = cost_per_token(model, usage) model_info = get_model_info( model=model, custom_llm_provider="dashscope", ) tier = select_tier_for_input( model_info["tiered_pricing"], input_tokens, ) expected_input = input_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "input_cost_per_token") expected_output = output_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "output_cost_per_token") print( { "actual_input": actual_input, "actual_output": actual_output, "actual_total": actual_input + actual_output, "request_tier_input": expected_input, "request_tier_output": expected_output, "request_tier_total": expected_input + expected_output, } ) ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell { 'actual_input': 0.023799999999999998, 'actual_output': 0.0007999999999999999, 'actual_total': 0.024599999999999997, 'request_tier_input': 0.075, 'request_tier_output': 0.004, 'request_tier_total': 0.079 } ``` For the current `qwen-flash` map, the two tiers are: ```python [ { "range": [0, 256000], "input_cost_per_token": 5e-08, "output_cost_per_token": 4e-07, }, { "range": [256000, 1000000], "input_cost_per_token": 2.5e-07, "output_cost_per_token": 2e-06, }, ] ``` A 300,000-input-token request selects the second tier. The current result instead charges the first 256,000 input tokens at the lower rate, the remaining 44,000 at the higher rate, and the 2,000 output tokens at the first tier because completion tokens are tiered independently ### Current-code analysis DashScope prompt cost calls `calculate_tiered_cost` separately for text input and cached input https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c/litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py#L45-L68 Completion and reasoning tokens are also passed independently to the graduated helper https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c/litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py#L77-L100 The shared helper explicitly implements graduated slicing https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c/litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/tiered_pricing.py#L28-L95 The same module separately documents and implements Alibaba's all-or-nothing request-size tier selection https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c/litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/tiered_pricing.py#L102-L132 Budget reservation uses the request-size selector signal.title: [Bug]: Project updates leave blocked, model, and budget auth state stale
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I searched open and closed issues before filing - [x] [#25553](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/25553) is related cache-coherence work for virtual keys but does not cover project objects or `/project/update` ### What happened? The enterprise `POST /project/update` endpoint updates the project row and its budget or object-permission rows, then returns without refreshing or invalidating `project_id:{project_id}` Authentication resolves projects through that cache key first. `_run_project_checks` then trusts the cached `blocked`, `models`, and budget values. A warmed project can therefore continue using its previous authorization state after an admin blocks it, restricts its models, or lowers its budget The stale direction also affects availability. Unblocking a project or widening its model access can continue to reject requests until the management-object cache expires ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Create an enterprise project with `blocked=False` and attach a key 2. Send one LLM request to warm `project_id:{project_id}` 3. Call `POST /project/update` with `blocked=True` 4. Confirm the database row is blocked 5. Send another request before the management-object cache expires 6. Observe that `get_project_object` returns the cached unblocked project and the request is admitted The same sequence can be repeated by replacing `blocked` with a restrictive `models` update or a lower budget ### Expected behavior After every successful project mutation, update or invalidate `project_id:{project_id}` and any cached included budget or permission data before returning Regression coverage should warm the project cache, mutate blocked, models, and budget independently, and assert that the next auth check observes each change ### Relevant code - [Project update returns after the DB write](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/b1fd20f4cdc8f7a9b4e0c886a277465aedb05ec8/enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/management_endpoints/project_endpoints.py#L650-L681) - [Cache-first project lookup](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/b1fd20f4cdc8f7a9b4e0c886a277465aedb05ec8/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py#L4221-L4270) - [Project auth checks](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/b1fd20f4cdc8f7a9b4e0c886a277465aedb05ec8/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py#L280-L350) ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.96.0, commit `b1fd20f4cdc8f7a9b4e0c886a277465aedb05ec8`

signal.title: [Feature]: Support Langfuse Python SDK v4
signal.text: ## Feature Request Support the Langfuse Python SDK v4 in LiteLLM's Langfuse callback integration. ## Current State `pyproject.toml` pins `langfuse = "^2.45.0"`, which means LiteLLM is locked to the v2 SDK. The Langfuse v3 SDK has been available for some time, and **Langfuse Python SDK v4.0.0 was released on March 10, 2026** with additional breaking changes. Relevant file: [`litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse.py`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/main/litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse.py) ## Why This Matters Self-hosted Langfuse users running the latest server (`langfuse/langfuse:3`) already require workarounds to use LiteLLM with v3 SDK semantics. When Langfuse publishes a `langfuse/langfuse:4` server image, the mismatch will become a hard blocker — the server will expect v4 SDK payloads while LiteLLM sends v2-era requests. ## What Needs to Change 1. **`pyproject.toml`**: Update `langfuse = "^2.45.0"` to allow v4 (`langfuse >= 4.0.0`) 2. **`litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse.py`**: Migrate API call sites to v4 SDK (import paths, client init, `generation` → `span` patterns, flush semantics) 3. **`litellm/integrations/langfuse/langfuse_prompt_management.py`**: Update prompt management client init and fetch calls per v4 API ## Migration Reference Langfuse has published a v3 → v4 migration guide: https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/sdk/upgrade-path/python-v3-to-v4 Key breaking changes in v4: - New client initialization pattern - Updated tracing/generation API - Changed flush/shutdown semantics ## No Existing Tracking Searched open issues and PRs — no existing tracking for this as of 2026-03-19. ## Expected Behavior After this change, `pip install litellm` should work out-of-the-box with `langfuse>=4.0.0`, with no manual dependency overrides required.

signal.title: feat(elevenlabs): add WebSocket streaming-input TTS endpoint
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - ElevenLabs supports low-latency TTS via WebSocket when text arrives incrementally (e.g. from an LLM stream), but LiteLLM only exposed the batch HTTP endpoint - Developers piping LLM output to ElevenLabs had to buffer the entire text first, adding hundreds of ms of latency How it solves it: - Adds a proxy WebSocket route WS /v1/audio/speech/stream-input that connects upstream to wss://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voice_id}/stream-input - Proxy handles auth (LiteLLM key in, xi-api-key out), BOS message on connect, and per-character cost tracking on session close - Regenerates schema.d.ts to include the new WebSocket endpoint stubs ## User Flow Before: a developer who wants to pipe LLM tokens directly to ElevenLabs TTS must buffer the full response 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with the complete text once the LLM finishes 2. They wait for ElevenLabs to process the full text before receiving any audio 3. Total latency = LLM completion time + ElevenLabs processing time After: the same developer can start streaming audio while the LLM is still generating 1. They open WS wss://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech/stream-input?model=elevenlabs/eleven_multilingual_v2&voice=alloy with their LiteLLM API key in the Authorization header 2. As each LLM token arrives they send {"text": "token "} over the WebSocket 3. ElevenLabs begins returning audio chunks (JSON with base64 audio field) before the LLM has finished 4. They send {"text": ""} when the LLM stream ends; the server replies with {"isFinal": true} and closes ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is a new feature. To verify end-to-end: 1. Start the proxy: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug` 2. Connect a WebSocket client (requires `wscat` or equivalent): ``` wscat -c "ws://localhost:4000/v1/audio/speech/stream-input?model=elevenlabs/eleven_multilingual_v2&voice=alloy" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer <litellm-key>" ``` 3. Send: `{"text": "Hello, how are you doing today? "}` 4. Send: `{"text": ""}` to close 5. Observe JSON frames with `{"audio": "<base64>"}` arriving, followed by `{"isFinal": true}` Requires ELEVENLABS_API_KEY set in the proxy environment. ## Type New Feature

signal.title: feat(voyage): add voyage-multimodal-3.5 model and extra multimodal params
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Supersedes #18285, which was opened against the wrong base and ballooned to 300+ files; this is a clean re-do against `litellm_internal_staging` ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The multimodal config and routing already exist on `litellm_internal_staging`, so this change is small: register `voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5` and surface the extra params the multimodal API accepts. Local verification with real litellm calls (no mocks in the routing/cost path) follows; the only thing not exercised here is the billed network call to Voyage, which needs a `VOYAGE_API_KEY` ``` $ LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True python - <<'PY' import litellm litellm.model_cost = litellm.get_model_cost_map(url="") litellm.get_model_info.cache_clear() info = litellm.get_model_info("voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5") print({k: info[k] for k in ("litellm_provider","mode","input_cost_per_token","max_input_tokens","max_tokens")}) from litellm.utils import get_optional_params_embeddings, ProviderConfigManager print(get_optional_params_embeddings(model="voyage-multimodal-3.5", custom_llm_provider="voyage", dimensions=512, encoding_format="base64", input_type="document", truncation=False, drop_params=True)) cfg = ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_embedding_config(model="voyage-multimodal-3.5", provider=litellm.LlmProviders.VOYAGE) print(type(cfg).__name__) PY {'litellm_provider': 'voyage', 'mode': 'embedding', 'input_cost_per_token': 1.2e-07, 'max_input_tokens': 32000, 'max_tokens': 32000} {'encoding_format': 'base64', 'output_dimension': 512, 'input_type': 'document', 'truncation': False} VoyageMultimodalEmbeddingConfig ``` Live end-to-end against the real API (run with a Voyage key set): ``` VOYAGE_API_KEY=*** python - <<'PY' from litellm import embedding r = embedding( model="voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5", input=[{"content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "a photo of a cat"}, {"type": "image_url", "image_url": "https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4d/Cat_November_2010-1a.jpg"}, ]}], input_type="document", ) print(r.model, len(r.data[0]["embedding"]), r.usage) PY ``` ## Type New Feature ## Changes Adds `voyage/voyage-multimodal-3.5` to both `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and the packaged backup, priced at the published $0.12 per million text tokens with a 32k context window. The multimodal routing on `litellm_internal_staging` already matches any `*multimodal*` model, so no wiring changes were needed for the model to resolve to `VoyageMultimodalEmbeddingConfig` Extends `VoyageMultimodalEmbeddingConfig` to map `encoding_format`, `input_type` and `truncation` in addition to `dimensions`, matching the parameters the Voyage multimodal embeddings API documents. The existing request/response transformation, API-key validation and `data:image/...` base64 normalization are left untouched Tests live in the already-mapped `tests/test_litellm/llms/voyage/test_voyage_multimodal_embedding.py`: the supported-params and mapping assertions were updated for the new params, and a registration test was added that fails if the `voyage-multimodal-3.5` entry is missing from the cost map

signal.title: fix(streaming): backfill response.completed output from output_item.done events
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #25429. Related to #26179. Supersedes #30934 ## Linear ticket N/A ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) (201 pre-existing failures in prisma/database, vertex AI, and MCP semantic filter tests; none in touched files — 324 tests across `tests/test_litellm/responses/` and `tests/test_litellm/llms/chatgpt/` pass cleanly) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## CI (LiteLLM team) > **CI status guideline:** > > - 50-55 passing tests: main is stable with minor issues. > - 45-49 passing tests: acceptable but needs attention > - <= 40 passing tests: unstable; be careful with your merges and assess the risk. - [ ] **Branch creation CI run** Link: - [ ] **CI run for the last commit** Link: - [ ] **Merge / cherry-pick CI run** Links: ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The `chatgpt/` provider routes through chatgpt.com's Codex backend, which sends `response.completed` with `output: []`. The actual assistant content arrives via preceding `response.output_item.done` SSE events. Without accumulation, the chat-completions bridge receives an empty output list and raises: ``` ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: [] ``` The fix teaches `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator._process_chunk` to accumulate `response.output_item.done` payloads as they stream in and backfill them into the `response.completed` chunk before it is stored as `completed_response`. Items are serialized to plain dicts via `model_dump()` so the downstream `_handle_raw_dict_response_item` callback in the transformation layer can process them. The existing `_recover_output_items_from_raw_sse` fallback in `LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler.transform_response` is preserved as a second layer if the streaming path is ever bypassed. **Before:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"error":{"message":"litellm.APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []. Received Model Group=gpt-5.4\nAvailable Model Group Fallbacks=None","type":null,"param":null,"code":"500"}} ``` **After:** ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \ -d '{"model":"gpt-5.4","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: hello"}],"stream":false}' {"id":"chatcmpl-764df91c-940a-47ea-be8c-d2aff173b8f4","created":1782409329,"model":"gpt-5.4","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"hello","role":"assistant"}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":5,"prompt_tokens":1635,"total_tokens":1640,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0},"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":0}}} ``` ## Type Bug Fix ## Changes `BaseResponsesAPIStreamingIterator` accumulates `response.output_item.done` items into `_streamed_output_items` during streaming. A secondary `_streamed_text_only_items` dict catches providers that emit `response.output_text.done` without a preceding `response.output_item.done`. At `response.completed` or `response.incomplete`, if `output` is empty and either dict is non-empty, the merged items are sorted by `output_index` and backfilled onto the response object. Items are serialized via `model_dump()` when they are Pydantic instances and passed through unchanged when they are already plain dicts; both the serialization and the assignment sit inside a `try/except` so any failure degrades to a logged warning rather than crashing the stream. `FallbackResponsesStreamWrapper` (router.py) and `MCPEnhancedStreamingIterator` (mcp_streaming_iterator.py) both bypass `super().__init__()` and are updated to mirror the two new instance attributes. Twelve regression tests are added to `tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator_output_recovery.py`, covering: the core backfill, multi-item index ordering, authoritative output preservation, `response.incomplete` backfill, `response.failed` no-backfill, `output_text.done` fallback, `output_item.done` precedence, replace-in-place content slots, gap padding, absent `output_index` sequential fallback, exception swallowing, and the dict-type contract required by the downstream transformation layer. The bulk of the line-count change in `streaming_iterator.py` is ruff reformatting of pre-existing code required to pass `ruff format`; the logical additions are confined to the accumulation block in `_process_chunk` and the two new instance attributes in `__init__`.

signal.title: [Bug]: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 returns empty final Responses output, and completion() bridge fails with "Unknown items in responses API response: []"
signal.text:
### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? Using `litellm==1.83.4` with `model="chatgpt/gpt-5.4"` and ChatGPT subscription auth, I can consistently reproduce two related issues: 1. `litellm.responses(..., stream=False)` returns a response with: - `status="completed"` - `output == []` - `output_text == ""` 2. `litellm.responses(..., stream=True)` emits `OutputTextDeltaEvent` text correctly, but the final `ResponseCompletedEvent.response` is still empty: - completed status is `"completed"` - completed response `output == []` 3. `litellm.completion(...)` on the same model then fails in the chat-completions bridge with: `litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []` Expected behavior: - non-stream Responses calls should return non-empty `output` / `output_text` - streamed Responses calls should preserve the final assembled output in `ResponseCompletedEvent.response` - `completion()` should not fail when the upstream request clearly produced text deltas This looks like a LiteLLM bug in either: - final Responses output assembly for the `chatgpt/*` provider, and/or - the completion bridge's handling of empty `response.output` ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Authenticate with ChatGPT subscription / device flow so `chatgpt/gpt-5.4` is available. 2. Save and run this repro script: ```python import argparse import importlib.metadata import traceback from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass from typing import Optional from litellm import completion, responses from litellm.types.llms.openai import ( OutputTextDeltaEvent, ResponseCompletedEvent, ResponsesAPIResponse, ResponsesAPIStreamingResponse, ) @dataclass class NonStreamResult: ok: bool error_type: Optional[str] error_message: Optional[str] status: Optional[str] output_len: Optional[int] output_text_len: Optional[int] @dataclass class StreamResult: ok: bool error_type: Optional[str] error_message: Optional[str] delta_text_len: Optional[int] completed_status: Optional[str] completed_output_len: Optional[int] @dataclass class CompletionResult: ok: bool error_type: Optional[str] error_message: Optional[str] def build_input(prompt: str) -> list[dict]: return [ { "role": "user", "content": [ { "type": "input_text", "text": prompt, } ], } ] def run_non_stream(model: str, prompt: str) -> NonStreamResult: try: resp: ResponsesAPIResponse = responses( model=model, instructions="You are concise.", input=build_input(prompt), temperature=1.0, stream=False, ) output_text = resp.output_text or "" return NonStreamResult( ok=True, error_type=None, error_message=None, status=resp.status, output_len=len(resp.output), output_text_len=len(output_text), ) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 return NonStreamResult( ok=False, error_type=type(exc).__name__, error_message=str(exc), status=None, output_len=None, output_text_len=None, ) def run_stream(model: str, prompt: str) -> StreamResult: try: stream: ResponsesAPIStreamingResponse = responses( model=model, instructions="You are concise.", input=build_input(prompt), temperature=1.0, stream=True, ) deltas: list[str] = [] completed_response: ResponsesAPIResponse | None = None for chunk in stream: if isinstance(chunk, OutputTextDeltaEvent): if chunk.delta: deltas.append(chunk.delta) continue if isinstance(chunk, ResponseCompletedEvent): completed_response = chunk.response return StreamResult( ok=True, error_type=None, error_message=None, delta_text_len=len("".join(deltas).strip()), completed_status=completed_response.status if completed_response else None, completed_output_len=len(completed_response.output) if completed_response else None, ) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 return StreamResult( ok=False, error_type=type(exc).__name__, error_message=str(exc), delta_text_len=None, completed_status=None, completed_output_len=None, ) def run_completion_bridge(model: str, prompt: str) -> CompletionResult: try: _ = completion( model=model, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], temperature=1.0, ) return CompletionResult(ok=True, error_type=None, error_message=None) except Exception as exc: # noqa: BLE001 return CompletionResult( ok=False, error_type=type(exc).__name__, error_message=str(exc), ) def main() -> int: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser( description=( "Reproduce LiteLLM chatgpt/* bridge issue where non-stream responses can be empty " "while stream delta contains text, and completion() fails in bridge transformation." ) ) parser.add_argument("--model", default="chatgpt/gpt-5.4") parser.add_argument("--prompt", default="Reply with exactly: OK") args = parser.parse_args() print("litellm_version:", importlib.metadata.version("litellm")) print("model:", args.model) non_stream = run_non_stream(args.model, args.prompt) stream = run_stream(args.model, args.prompt) bridge = run_completion_bridge(args.model, args.prompt) print("
non_stream:", asdict(non_stream)) print("stream:", asdict(stream)) print("completion_bridge:", asdict(bridge)) bridge_msg = bridge.error_message or "" bug_signature = ( non_stream.ok and stream.ok and non_stream.status == "completed" and (non_stream.output_len or 0) == 0 and (non_stream.output_text_len or 0) == 0 and (stream.delta_text_len or 0) > 0 ) bridge_signature = "Unknown items in responses API response: []" in bridge_msg print("
reproduced_non_stream_empty_vs_stream_delta:", bug_signature) print("reproduced_completion_bridge_error:", bridge_signature) if bug_signature or bridge_signature: print("
BUG REPRODUCED") return 0 print("
BUG NOT REPRODUCED (or blocked by auth/network/model differences)") return 1 if __name__ == "__main__": try: raise SystemExit(main()) except KeyboardInterrupt: print("Interrupted") raise except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 print("Unexpected fatal error:") traceback.print_exc() raise ``` 3. Observe ```text litellm_version: 1.83.4 model: chatgpt/gpt-5.4 .venv\Lib\site-packages\pydantic\main.py:464: UserWarning: Pydantic serializer warnings: PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue(Expected `ResponseAPIUsage` - serialized value may not be as expected [field_name='usage', input_value={'completion_tokens': 5, ..., 'video_tokens': None}}, input_type=dict]) return self.__pydantic_serializer__.to_python( Give Feedback / Get Help: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/new LiteLLM.Info: If you need to debug this error, use `litellm._turn_on_debug()'. non_stream: {'ok': True, 'error_type': None, 'error_message': None, 'status': 'completed', 'output_len': 0, 'output_text_len': 0} stream: {'ok': True, 'error_type': None, 'error_message': None, 'delta_text_len': 2, 'completed_status': 'completed', 'completed_output_len': 0} completion_bridge: {'ok': False, 'error_type': 'APIConnectionError', 'error_message': 'litellm.APIConnectionError: APIConnectionError: ChatgptException - Unknown items in responses API response: []'} reproduced_non_stream_empty_vs_stream_delta: True reproduced_completion_bridge_error: True BUG REPRODUCED ``` ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.83.4 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(logging): preserve uvicorn color_message args during secret redaction
signal.text: ## TLDR fixes #37121 Problem this solves: - Proxy startup can print literal `%s://%s:%d` instead of the real URL - Only shows in a real TTY (colors on), so it's easy to miss in CI/Docker How it solves it: - Preserve record.args long enough to also substitute uvicorn's color_message - Redaction filter now fixes up color_message before clearing args ## User Flow Before: an admin starting the proxy in an interactive terminal can't tell what port it's listening on 1. They run `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000` directly in a terminal (no piping) 2. The startup banner prints `INFO: Uvicorn running on %s://%s:%d (Press CTRL+C to quit)` 3. They have to already know the port from their own `--port` flag; the log line is useless After: the same startup banner shows the real address 1. They run the same command in the same terminal 2. The startup banner prints `INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix before: after: Reproduced by running the real proxy (`python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml`) under a real TTY, at the merge base before this fix: ``` INFO: Started server process [%d] INFO: Uvicorn running on %s://%s:%d (Press CTRL+C to quit) ``` With this fix applied, the same startup path prints: ``` INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 (Press CTRL+C to quit) ``` Regression test `tests/test_litellm/test_secret_redaction.py::test_filter_preserves_uvicorn_color_message_args` drives uvicorn's actual `DefaultFormatter` in color mode and fails without the fix, reproducing this exact output. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only reproduces when stderr is a real TTY (colors on); piping through `tee` or running without a TTY (e.g. most Docker/CI setups) masks it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): register WebSocket passthrough for OpenAI prefixes
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - WebSocket upgrades under /openai and /openai_passthrough always returned 403 - client.realtime.connect() and client.responses.connect() could not pass through the proxy How it solves it: - registers catch-all WebSocket routes for both OpenAI prefixes - injects the provider key and forwards the client query string - decodes upstream frames as utf-8 so real sessions survive - negotiates the client's WebSocket subprotocol like the native realtime route - refuses model-restricted keys at connect, keeping model ACLs intact ## User Flow Before: you cannot open any OpenAI WebSocket session through the proxy's OpenAI passthrough prefixes 1. You point the OpenAI SDK at the proxy with your LiteLLM key, base_url `http://<proxy>/openai/v1` or `http://<proxy>/openai_passthrough/v1` 2. You call `client.realtime.connect(model="gpt-realtime-2.1-mini")` against `/openai_passthrough/v1/realtime` and the upgrade is rejected with HTTP 403 3. You call `client.responses.connect()` against `/openai/v1/responses` or `/openai_passthrough/v1/responses` and that upgrade is also rejected with HTTP 403 After: the same SDK calls open live WebSocket sessions through both prefixes 1. You point the OpenAI SDK at the proxy exactly as before 2. `client.realtime.connect(model="gpt-realtime-2.1-mini")` upgrades, `session.created` arrives, and your realtime conversation streams back with token usage 3. `client.responses.connect()` upgrades on either prefix and `response.create` returns real model output over the socket 4. A browser client that authenticates via `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` values (`openai-insecure-api-key.<key>`, `openai-beta.realtime-v1`) gets its first offered subprotocol echoed back in the handshake, so spec-compliant browsers keep the connection open instead of aborting it 5. If your key is restricted to specific models, both connects are refused at the handshake with HTTP 403, so a restricted key cannot reach arbitrary models over these WebSocket routes; the native `/openai/v1/realtime` route keeps serving that key's allowed models ## Relevant issues Fixes #36088 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5396 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy booted from the repo with a one-model config (`gpt-realtime-2.1-mini` + master key), real OpenAI API calls costing real $. Clients are the plain OpenAI Python SDK (2.33.0) pointed at the proxy, plus a raw `websockets` client that mimics a browser's subprotocol handshake <details> <summary>realtime_qa.py (OpenAI SDK realtime client used below)</summary> ```python import asyncio, os, sys from openai import AsyncOpenAI PORT, PREFIX = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] MODEL = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "gpt-realtime-2.1-mini" async def main() -> None: client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_PROXY_KEY"], base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/{PREFIX}/v1") async with client.realtime.connect(model=MODEL) as conn: await conn.session.update(session={"type": "realtime", "output_modalities": ["text"]}) await conn.conversation.item.create(item={"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Reply with exactly: WS PASSTHROUGH OK"}]}) await conn.response.create() async for event in conn: print("event:", event.type) if event.type == "response.output_text.done": print(" model said:", event.text) if event.type == "response.done": print(" status:", event.response.status) print(" usage:", event.response.usage) break asyncio.run(main()) ``` </details> <details> <summary>responses_qa.py (OpenAI SDK responses.connect client used below)</summary> ```python import asyncio, os, sys from openai import AsyncOpenAI PORT, PREFIX = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2] MODEL = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else "gpt-5.6" async def main() -> None: client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key=os.environ["LITELLM_PROXY_KEY"], base_url=f"http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}/{PREFIX}/v1") async with client.responses.connect() as conn: await conn.send({"type": "response.create", "model": MODEL, "input": "Reply with exactly: WS RESPONSES OK"}) while True: event = await conn.recv() print("event:", event.type) if event.type == "response.output_text.done": print(" model said:", event.text) if event.type in ("response.completed", "response.failed", "response.incomplete"): print(" status:", event.response.status) print(" model:", event.response.model) print(" usage:", event.response.usage) break asyncio.run(main()) ``` </details> <details> <summary>subproto_qa.py (browser-style client: auth via Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, no Authorization header)</summary> ```python import asyncio, json, sys import websockets PORT, PREFIX, KEY = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3] MODEL = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "gpt-realtime-2.1-mini" async def main() -> None: url = f"ws://localhost:{PORT}/{PREFIX}/v1/realtime?model={MODEL}" offered = ["realtime", f"openai-insecure-api-key.{KEY}", "openai-beta.realtime-v1"] async with websockets.connect(url, subprotocols=offered) as ws: print("SELECTED_SUBPROTOCOL:", ws.subprotocol) first = json.loads(await ws.recv()) print("FIRST_EVENT:", first.get("type")) await ws.send(json.dumps({"type": "response.create", "response": {"instructions": "Say hola in one word", "output_modalities": ["text"]}})) async for raw in ws: event = json.loads(raw) if event.get("type") == "response.done": response = event.get("response", {}) print("RESPONSE_DONE status:", response.get("status"), "total_tokens:", response.get("usage", {}).get("total_tokens")) break print("BROWSER SUBPROTO OK") asyncio.run(main()) ``` </details> ### Before, at merge base 4e5495e1bd (proxy on port 28517) ```console $ python realtime_qa.py 28517 openai_passthrough websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403 $ python responses_qa.py 28517 openai websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403 $ python responses_qa.py 28517 openai_passthrough websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403 ``` Control on the same proxy: the native realtime bridge works, so only the passthrough surfaces were broken ```console $ python realtime_qa.py 28517 openai event: response.done status: completed usage: ... input_tokens=132 ... output_tokens=23, total_tokens=155 ``` ### After, at 5965648547 (proxy on port 29226) ```console $ python realtime_qa.py 29226 openai_passthrough event: response.output_text.done model said: WS PASSTHROUGH OK event: response.done status: completed usage: ... input_tokens=132 ... output_tokens=24, total_tokens=156 $ python responses_qa.py 29226 openai event: response.output_text.done model said: WS RESPONSES OK event: response.completed status: completed model: gpt-5.6-sol usage: ... input_tokens=15 ... output_tokens=9, total_tokens=24 $ python responses_qa.py 29226 openai_passthrough event: response.output_text.done model said: WS RESPONSES OK event: response.completed status: completed model: gpt-5.6-sol usage: ... total_tokens=24 ``` ### Subprotocol negotiation for browser clients At a258b2b130 (before this fix) the route accepted the socket without selecting any subprotocol even when the client offered some; RFC 6455 requires such clients (all browsers) to fail the connection. After the fix the first offered subprotocol is echoed, mirroring the native `/openai/v1/realtime` route, and the whole session runs authenticated purely by the `openai-insecure-api-key.` subprotocol ```console $ python subproto_qa.py 22160 openai_passthrough $LITELLM_KEY # at a258b2b130 SELECTED_SUBPROTOCOL: None FIRST_EVENT: session.created $ python subproto_qa.py 29226 openai_passthrough $LITELLM_KEY # at 5965648547 SELECTED_SUBPROTOCOL: realtime FIRST_EVENT: session.created RESPONSE_DONE status: completed total_tokens: 61 BROWSER SUBPROTO OK $ python subproto_qa.py 29226 openai $LITELLM_KEY # at 5965648547 SELECTED_SUBPROTOCOL: realtime FIRST_EVENT: session.created RESPONSE_DONE status: completed total_tokens: 52 BROWSER SUBPROTO OK ``` ### Model ACL enforcement, at 5965648547 (same proxy, DB-backed) A key restricted to one model is refused at the handshake on both WebSocket surfaces, in both auth styles, and still works on the native realtime route with its allowed model ```console $ curl -s http://127.0.0.1:29226/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ -d '{"models": ["gpt-realtime-2.1-mini"]}' # -> sk-MS_WO... $ LITELLM_PROXY_KEY=sk-MS_WO... python realtime_qa.py 29226 openai_passthrough websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403 $ python subproto_qa.py 29226 openai_passthrough sk-MS_WO... websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403 $ LITELLM_PROXY_KEY=sk-MS_WO... python realtime_qa.py 29226 openai event: response.done status: completed usage: ... input_tokens=132 ... output_tokens=28, total_tokens=160 ``` ### Missing provider credential, at 5965648547 (proxy on port 22245, no OPENAI_API_KEY configured) The handshake is refused cleanly with no server-side traceback, instead of the previous close-then-raise that left an ASGI ValueError in the logs ```console $ python subproto_qa.py 22245 openai_passthrough $LITELLM_KEY websockets.exceptions.InvalidStatus: server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 403 $ grep -c "Traceback" qa_proxy_nokey2.log; grep -c "ValueError" qa_proxy_nokey2.log 0 0 ``` Caveats: - native /openai/v1/realtime route is untouched; it shadows the catch-all - model-restricted keys are refused on these WebSocket routes - first offered subprotocol is echoed, same as the native route - /vertex_ai/live model-ACL parity is a separate follow-up ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Registers a catch-all `@router.websocket` route for the `/openai` and `/openai_passthrough` prefixes in `llm_passthrough_endpoints.py`. The handler authenticates through `user_api_key_auth_websocket`, injects the configured OpenAI key upstream, preserves the client's query string, and hands off to the shared `websocket_passthrough_request` forwarder The shared forwarder previously decoded the upstream's first frame as ascii, which crashed on any non-ascii byte in OpenAI's `session.created` payload; it now decodes utf-8. Keys restricted to specific models are refused at connect with close code 1008 so these routes cannot be used to sidestep model ACLs, matching the enforcement the HTTP passthrough applies to request bodies. The logged endpoint now reflects the actual request path instead of hardcoding `/openai/` The route accepts the socket itself, echoing the client's first offered `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` exactly like the native `/openai/v1/realtime` route, so browser clients that carry auth in subprotocols survive the handshake. The URL join helper moved from a private static method to a module-level `_join_url_paths` so the route does not reach into another class's private API. When no OpenAI credential is configured the route closes with 1011 and returns instead of raising after the close, matching the Vertex live path Unit tests cover route registration, query and auth forwarding, subprotocol selection, the restricted-key refusal, the unrestricted-key allow list, the credential-missing clean close, and a regression test that fails on the old ascii decode ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix: apply secret filter to Uvicorn log
signal.text: ## TLDR <!-- Fill in the bullets below and keep each one short and concrete: one line per bullet, roughly 10 words max This section must be extremely human parsable, comprehensible, and readable: its target audience is humans, not AI agents --> Problem this solves: - default JSON Uvicorn logs leak sensitive data through API requests, example: leaking sk-keys through [`GET /key/info`](https://www.litellm.org/#/key%20management/info_key_fn_key_info_get) How it solves it: - trivially applies the secret filter in the default `logging` configuration; - it DOES NOT apply it to user-supplied configuration. ## User Flow <!-- Two ordered lists, Before and After, walking the same end user through the same task, written strictly from that user's seat Read the linked issue, ticket, or customer thread first so the flow reflects the real application and the routes its users actually hit; don't invent a generic scenario Lead each list with one plain sentence saying where the flow fails (Before) or succeeds (After), then number the steps Every step is something the user does or observes: the HTTP method and full URL they hit, what they sent, and what visibly came back (status code, error text, the shape of an ID). UI steps name the page URL and what is on screen No LiteLLM internals: never name functions, files, DB tables, config classes, hooks, callbacks, or code paths. "The upload hands back an ID that looks like OpenAI's own `file-abc123` instead of the scrambled one the gateway returned" is right, "no managed-file row was registered" is wrong Keep the two lists step-for-step identical until they diverge, so the changed step is obvious If the bug had a security or authorization consequence, end each list with what another user could or could no longer do Regenerate this section whenever new commits change the PR's behavior, so it never describes an older revision Example: Before: a developer whose app streams chat completions gets no token counts back, so their cost dashboard reads zero 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` and no `stream_options` 2. The last SSE chunk arrives with `"usage": null`, so their app records 0 prompt and 0 completion tokens 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request logged at $0 spend After: the same request comes back with real token counts, so the dashboard shows real spend 1. The proxy admin sets `always_include_stream_usage: true` and restarts the proxy 2. The developer sends the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` and no `stream_options` 3. The last SSE chunk now carries a `usage` object with real prompt and completion token counts 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows that request at non-zero spend --> ## Relevant issues None to my best knowledge. ## Linear ticket <!-- if you are an internal contributor, add "Resolves " followed by the Linear ticket e.g., "Resolves LIT-1234" to link the Linear ticket to the GitHub PR. signal.title: fix: count anthropic image content blocks in token_counter instead of raising
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: router with `enable_pre_call_checks: true` and vision-capable vLLM backends, Claude Code sending screenshots to the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint Before the fix, every image-bearing anthropic messages request logs this router error and silently skips pre-call context-window filtering (the initial deployment list is returned unfiltered): ``` LiteLLM Router:ERROR: router.py - litellm.router.py::_pre_call_checks: failed to count tokens. Returning initial list of deployments. Got - Error getting number of tokens from content list: Invalid content item type: image. Expected str or dict with 'type' field (text, image_url, tool_use, tool_result, thinking, tool_reference)., default_token_count=None ``` After the fix, the same request counts tokens normally and the usage is tracked (no router error logged): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -d '{"model": "my-model", "max_tokens": 300, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [ {"type": "text", "text": "What color? One word."}, {"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/png", "data": "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mP8z8BQDwAEhQGAhKmMIQAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="}}]}]}' {..., "usage": {"input_tokens": 82, "output_tokens": 300}, ...} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_count_content_list` handles openai `image_url` blocks but raised `Invalid content item type` on anthropic-format `image` blocks (`{"type": "image", "source": ...}`). The raise disables router pre-call checks for any anthropic messages traffic containing images and breaks token accounting on that path. This counts the flat `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TOKEN_COUNT` for such blocks, matching the `image_url` fallback behavior, since a base64 source has no URL or detail field to inspect. Same failure shape as the `tool_reference` handling that already landed for tool-search traffic Added a regression test asserting an anthropic image block increases the count by at least `DEFAULT_IMAGE_TOKEN_COUNT` instead of raising

signal.title: fix: duplicate message_start in anthropic responses stream wrapper
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: four self-hosted vLLM backends behind openai/ deployments, Claude Code pointed at the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint, which routes through the anthropic -> responses bridge for openai-provider models Before the fix, every streamed request emits `message_start` twice with the same message id, which the Anthropic SDK stream parser in Claude Code rejects as an event-order violation: ``` $ curl -s -N http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -d '{"model": "my-model", "max_tokens": 2000, "stream": true, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say OK and nothing else."}]}' \ | grep -oE "event: [a-z_]+" | sort | uniq -c 62 event: content_block_delta 1 event: content_block_start 1 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 2 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` After the fix, the same command produces a protocol-correct sequence: ``` 1097 event: content_block_delta 2 event: content_block_start 2 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 1 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` (the two content_block start/stop pairs are the thinking block and the text block; Claude Code streams these sessions without errors after the fix) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper.__anext__` pre-emits `message_start` before consuming the upstream stream, and the `response.created` handler in `_process_event` appended another one without checking `_sent_message_start`. Every streamed request through the wrapper emitted `message_start` twice. This guards the `response.created` handler with the existing flag Added a regression test that drives the wrapper with a `response.created`-first event stream and asserts exactly one `message_start` is emitted **Follow-up commit:** while looking at the same wrapper's handling of providers that skip `response.output_item.added`, found that `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` had no fallback for that case. `response.output_text.delta` already synthesizes a `content_block_start` when no block is registered for the item_id; the reasoning delta handler instead fell back to whatever `_current_block_index` happened to be open, which is not necessarily a thinking block, and emitted a `thinking_delta` into it regardless. Strict Anthropic SSE clients reject a `thinking_delta` aimed at a block of a different declared type. Mirrored the existing text-delta fallback for the reasoning case, with a regression test covering both the synthesis and that it never reuses an already-open non-thinking block.
