signal.title: fix(agent-shin): give contributors 24 hours of grace before auto-close
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Agent Shin auto-closed items 2 hours after warning - Two hours is too short for an OSS contributor - Every comment hardcoded "2 hours" in prose How it solves it: - `GRACE_PERIOD_SECONDS` goes from 7200 to 86400 - New `GRACE_PERIOD_LABEL` renders the window everywhere - Tests assert the constant, not the literal ## User Flow Before: an external contributor opens a PR with a thin description, gets warned, and finds it closed before their workday is over 1. They open a PR on `BerriAI/litellm` with no QA proof 2. Agent Shin comments "If the description isn't updated in the next **2 hours**, I'll auto-close this PR" 3. Two hours later, the next sweep closes the PR, so a contributor in another timezone wakes up to a closed PR they never had a chance to fix 4. They have to open a fresh PR or comment `@agent-shin reconsider` to get back into the queue After: the same contributor gets a full day to react before the close 1. They open the same PR with no QA proof 2. Agent Shin comments "If the description isn't updated in the next **24 hours**, I'll auto-close this PR" 3. They update the description the next morning, and the sweep that runs after the warning sees it passing and leaves the PR open 4. If they do nothing for a day, the close comment says the grace period (24 hours) has elapsed, with the same recovery paths as before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This change only affects the GitHub triage bot's own comments, so there is no proxy endpoint to curl. The proof renders the real comment bodies the bot posts, at the merge base and at this PR's tip. Shared setup: ```bash cat > /tmp/render.py <<'EOF' import sys sys.path.insert(0, ".github/scripts") import agent_shin_shared as s, close_low_quality_prs as c, triage_with_llm as t print("GRACE_PERIOD_SECONDS =", s.GRACE_PERIOD_SECONDS) warn = c.format_grace_warning_comment(score=2, threshold=4) close = c.format_close_comment(score=2, threshold=4) issue = t.format_grace_warning_issue_comment({"verdict": "fail", "missing": ["QA proof"], "explanation": "thin"}) for label, body in (("greptile warn", warn), ("greptile close", close), ("issue warn", issue)): for line in body.splitlines(): if "auto-close" in line or "grace period (" in line: print(f"[{label}] {line[:160]}") EOF ``` ### Before (973329e986) 1. `python3 /tmp/render.py` ``` GRACE_PERIOD_SECONDS = 7200 [greptile warn] If the score isn't lifted in the next **2 hours**, I'll auto-close this PR. signal.title: fix(proxy): route blocked models through healthy fallbacks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Fully blocked primary deployments reject requests before configured fallbacks run. - Healthy fallback deployments therefore cannot recover availability. How it solves it: - Preserve the blocked-model error when no fallback deployment is available. - Let the Router fallback chain run when a fallback remains unblocked. - Add mocked regression coverage for recovery and rejection behavior. ## User Flow Before: a client receives `Model is blocked` even though its configured fallback is healthy. 1. The operator blocks every deployment behind the alias's primary model group. 2. The client sends `POST https://<proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "DeepSeek-Flash"`. 3. The gateway immediately returns a `Model is blocked` permission error. 4. The client receives no completion because the configured fallback is never attempted. After: the same client request uses the healthy configured fallback. 1. The operator blocks every deployment behind the alias's primary model group. 2. The client sends `POST https://<proxy-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `model: "DeepSeek-Flash"`. 3. The gateway sees that a configured fallback still has an unblocked deployment. 4. The client receives the completion from that fallback; fully blocked models without a usable fallback still return `Model is blocked`. ## Relevant issues Fixes #36665 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix No live provider proof was captured in this environment. The regression tests use mocked deployments, as required for tests under `tests/test_litellm/`; a maintainer should run the live proxy scenario before merging. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Live provider end-to-end verification requires a configured proxy and provider credentials. ## Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(batches): don't crash logging when a completed batch has no output file
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - All-error batches finish with an error file only, no output file - Polling such a batch crashed the gateway's success logging - None of those polls ever reached the spend logs How it solves it: - Treat a batch with no output file as an empty result - Record zero cost and usage instead of raising ## User Flow Before: every status poll of the all-error batch vanishes from the gateway's spend records, and the gateway console prints a file-retrieval error each time 1. They upload their batch input with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (purpose=batch, target_model_names=gpt-5.5), every JSONL line asking for an out-of-range temperature, and get back a long gateway file id 2. They create the batch with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches using that input_file_id and get back a batch id with "status": "validating" 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} with their virtual key until the response shows "status": "completed" with "output_file_id": null, a real "error_file_id", and request_counts 0 completed / 3 failed 4. They open GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?api_key=<their virtual key> and find rows for the upload and the batch creation but none for any status poll, while the console printed "ValueError: Output file id is None cannot retrieve file content" on every poll After: every status poll is recorded at zero spend and the console stays clean 1. They upload their batch input with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (purpose=batch, target_model_names=gpt-5.5), every JSONL line asking for an out-of-range temperature, and get back a long gateway file id 2. Both legs ran the identical setup and differ only in the commit the proxy was booted from: fresh Postgres DB, config with `gpt-5.5` (`openai/gpt-5.5`) plus a `files_settings` entry for the plain-provider flow, `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_ENABLED=false` (the OSS shape from #33987, no enterprise cost poller), and a user-bound virtual key **Before, merge base `add095b494cc75440543a240618a88174ea4a445` (proxy port 25200): polls never reach the spend logs** Managed flow (upload with `target_model_names=gpt-5.5`, then create and poll): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:25200/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names=gpt-5.5 -F file=@all_error.jsonl $ curl -s http://localhost:25200/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" -d '{"input_file_id":"<unified id>","endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","completion_window":"24h"}' $ curl -s http://localhost:25200/v1/batches/<unified batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_A" # repeated until terminal {"id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDpkMGI3...", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29u...", "request_counts": {"completed": 0, "failed": 3, "total": 3}} $ curl -s "http://localhost:25200/spend/logs?api_key=$KEY_A" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-master-before" [{"call_type": "acreate_batch", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:47:04.432000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_file", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:55.295000Z"}] ``` 3 polls made, zero `aretrieve_batch` rows. "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDpkMGI3...", "status": "completed", "output_file_id": null, "error_file_id": "bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTphcHBsaWNhdGlvbi9qc29u...", "request_counts": {"completed": 0, "failed": "2026-08-16T20:46:43.203000Z"}, {"call_type": "acreate_file", "spend": 0.0, "startTime": "2026-08-16T20:46:36.830000Z"}] ``` Plain-provider flow, 5 polls: ``` $ curl -s signal.title: fix: content_block_delta type mismatch when reasoning and content arrive in one chunk
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: self-hosted vLLM backend with a reasoning-capable Qwen model behind an `openai/` deployment, Claude Code pointed at the proxy's `/v1/messages` endpoint Captured live from the failing deployment before the fix. The vLLM reasoning parser flushed the tail of `reasoning_content` bundled with the first character of the answer in one streaming chunk. `AnthropicStreamWrapper` opened the new content block as `text` (block-type detection prefers content) but emitted a `thinking_delta` into it (delta emission prefers reasoning), producing this SSE sequence: ``` content_block_stop {"index": 1} content_block_start {"index": 2, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}} content_block_delta {"index": 2, "delta": {"type": "thinking_delta", "thinking": "\n"}} ``` Claude Code (a strict Anthropic SSE client) rejects this as "Content block is not a thinking block". Because the corrupted assistant turn gets replayed as conversation history, every subsequent turn in the same context fails the same way until the context is cleared. After the fix, hitting the same backend with a prompt that forces a reasoning/answer transition, and reducing the captured event stream to (index -> declared block type) then checking every delta against its block's declared type: ``` $ curl -sN http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "my-reasoning-model", "max_tokens": 1500, "stream": true, "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "..."}]}' \ | grep -oE "event: [a-z_]+" | sort | uniq -c 462 event: content_block_delta 3 event: content_block_start 3 event: content_block_stop 1 event: message_delta 1 event: message_start 1 event: message_stop ``` block types opened: `{0: "text", 1: "thinking", 2: "text"}` (empty leading text block, then thinking, then the answer), zero delta/block-type mismatches across all 462 deltas ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_CombinedChunkSplitter` previously only split a chunk that combined response content with a `finish_reason` (needed for fake-streamed providers like Vertex AI Gemma `:predict`, which collapse the whole response into one chunk). It did not split a chunk that combined `reasoning_content`/`thinking_blocks` with `content` in the same delta, which some vLLM reasoning parsers do at the reasoning/answer boundary. That combined shape hit two functions that disagree on which payload is dominant: `_should_start_new_content_block` (content-block-type detection) checks `content` before `reasoning_content` and picks `text`, while `translate_streaming_openai_response_to_anthropic` (delta emission) checks `reasoning_content` first and picks `thinking_delta`. The mismatch means a `thinking_delta` lands on a block the client was told is `text`. Generalized `_CombinedChunkSplitter` to split on any combination of {reasoning, content/tool_calls, finish_reason} rather than only {content, finish_reason}, so each downstream chunk carries exactly one payload and both functions agree on its type. Existing content+finish_reason behavior is unchanged; a chunk carrying reasoning+content+finish_reason now splits into three single-payload chunks instead of two. Added a regression test (`test_streaming_iterator_reasoning_content_chunk.py`) that replays the captured chunk shape (reasoning tail bundled with content) through the full `AnthropicStreamWrapper` and asserts no delta ever targets a block of the wrong declared type, and that both payloads survive as separate deltas. Updated the existing combined-chunk splitter test that asserted the old (incorrect) two-way split behavior for a reasoning+content+finish chunk to assert the corrected three-way split.

signal.title: fix: omit empty tools array in responses to chat completion transformation
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Proxy config: self-hosted vLLM backend behind an openai/ deployment with `use_chat_completions_api: true`, hitting the proxy's `/v1/responses` endpoint with a request that carries no tools Before the fix, the bridge sends `tools: []` to the backend and vLLM rejects the request (the error also bounces through every configured fallback since it reproduces on each deployment): ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "my-model", "max_output_tokens": 200, "input": [{"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Say OK and nothing else."}]}]}' {"error": {"message": "litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - 1 validation error: {'type': 'value_error', 'loc': ('body',), 'msg': 'Value error, `tools` must not be an empty array. Either provide at least one tool or omit the field entirely.', ... ``` After the fix, the same command returns a normal response: ``` {"id":"resp_N2PG_...","created_at":1784410664,"error":null, ...} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `transform_responses_api_request_to_chat_completion_request` converts an absent `tools` param into `[]` via `responses_api_request.get("tools") or []`, and the final request dict only filters `None` values, so the empty array reaches the backend. Strict OpenAI-compatible backends such as vLLM reject empty tool arrays outright. This maps the empty result back to `None` so the existing None-filter drops the key Added a regression test asserting that a responses request without tools produces a chat completion request with no `tools` key

signal.title: fix(bedrock): report uploaded size in the FileObject returned by managed batch uploads
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Bedrock managed batch uploads return `bytes: 0` - Client-side checks on `FileObject.bytes` fail How it solves it: - Report the size of the body uploaded to S3 - Response `Content-Length` on PutObject is always 0 ## User Flow Before: a developer uploading a Bedrock batch input file gets back a file object claiming the file is empty, so their `bytes > 0` guard rejects a perfectly good upload 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with `purpose=batch`, `target_model_names=bedrock-batch-haiku` and a 22180 byte JSONL file 2. They get back a 200 with a managed file id and `"bytes": 0` 3. The object really is in S3 at the expected key with a non-zero size, so the response contradicts the storage 4. Their validation on `bytes > 0` fails and they never get to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches After: the same upload reports the size of the object that was stored 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files 2. They get back a 200 with `"bytes": 21679`, matching the object stored in S3 3. Their `bytes > 0` check passes and they continue to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches, which accepts the file and starts a real batch job The uploaded size is the Bedrock-shaped JSONL that the gateway writes, so it can differ slightly from the file on the caller's disk. It always matches what is in the bucket ## Relevant issues Fixes #36388 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5400 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proof against real AWS (S3 + Bedrock, account `litellm-dev`), replacing the earlier simulated-S3 proof from the Devin environment. Same config on both legs: a `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` deployment named `bedrock-batch-haiku` with `s3_bucket_name: litellm-kms-qa-35148`, `s3_encryption_key_id`, `aws_batch_role_arn`, and `model_info.mode: batch`; a 100-record JSONL of 22180 bytes on disk Before, at 3840970613: ``` $ wc -c < batch_input.jsonl 22180 $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:24817/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -F "purpose=batch" -F "target_model_names=bedrock-batch-haiku" \ -F "file=@batch_input.jsonl;type=application/jsonl" {"id":"bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTph...", "bytes":0, "created_at":1786839989, "filename":"litellm-bedrock-files-us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1-0-564ac031-....jsonl", "object":"file", "purpose":"batch", "status":"uploaded"} $ aws s3api head-object --bucket litellm-kms-qa-35148 \ --key litellm-bedrock-files-us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1-0-564ac031-....jsonl \ --query '{ContentLength:ContentLength,SSE:ServerSideEncryption}' {"ContentLength": 21679, "SSE": "aws:kms"} ``` The bucket holds a 21679 byte object while the API reported `bytes: 0` After, at 904ff9efa7: ``` $ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:24923/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ -F "purpose=batch" -F "target_model_names=bedrock-batch-haiku" \ -F "file=@batch_input.jsonl;type=application/jsonl" signal.title: [Bug]: compression_savings_spend and prompt_caching_savings_spend always $0 with cost-based-routing and multiple deployments per model_name
signal.text: # [Bug]: `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` always $0 when using `cost-based-routing` with multiple deployments per model_name ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? When using `routing_strategy: cost-based-routing` with multiple deployments sharing the same `model_name` (each at a different provider/price point), the daily spend rollup fields `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` are always recorded as `$0.00`, even though compression is actively removing tokens from requests. The root cause is that `compute_savings_spend()` in `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/savings.py` calls `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` which uses `litellm.get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider=custom_llm_provider)` to look up the model's pricing. But for multi-deployment setups the backend model name (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `custom_llm_provider="openrouter"`) is **not** in `litellm.model_cost` — because `shared_backend_model_info()` in `litellm/types/utils.py` explicitly strips all pricing fields from the shared backend key: ```python SHARED_BACKEND_MODEL_INFO_FIELDS = frozenset( ModelInfoBase.__required_keys__ | ModelInfoBase.__optional_keys__ ) - frozenset(CustomPricingLiteLLMParams.model_fields) # <-- removes ALL cost fields def shared_backend_model_info(model_info: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]: return {k: v for k, v in model_info.items() if k in SHARED_BACKEND_MODEL_INFO_FIELDS} ``` So when `_create_deployment()` registers the shared backend key: ```python _backend_alias_cost = {_model_name: _shared_model_info} litellm.register_model(model_cost=_backend_alias_cost) ``` The registered entry contains only `{"litellm_provider": "openrouter", "mode": "chat"}` — no pricing. Subsequent `get_model_info()` calls for that model+provider combination fail with "This model isn't mapped yet", and `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` gracefully returns `(0.0, 0.0)`. The per-deployment pricing IS correctly stored under the deployment's unique `model_info.id` hash, but `compute_savings_spend()` never looks it up by that ID — it only has `model` and `custom_llm_provider` available from the spend log payload. ## What did you expect to happen? `compression_savings_spend` and `prompt_caching_savings_spend` should reflect the actual dollar savings using the deployment's configured pricing, even when multiple deployments share a `model_name` with different prices. ## Steps to Reproduce **Config (minimal):** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY input_cost_per_token: 0.0000004225 output_cost_per_token: 0.000000845 model_info: cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.000000035 - model_name: deepseek-v4-pro litellm_params: model: openai/deepseek-v4-pro api_key: os.environ/ZEN_API_KEY api_base: https://example.com/zen input_cost_per_token: 0.00000174 output_cost_per_token: 0.00000384 model_info: cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.000000174 router_settings: routing_strategy: cost-based-routing ``` Two deployments, same `model_name`, different providers and prices. Cost-based-routing picks the cheaper OpenRouter deployment. The spend log records `model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with `custom_llm_provider=openrouter`. **Verification inside the running container:** ```python import litellm # The shared backend key has NO pricing: print(litellm.model_cost.get("openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro")) # → None (not registered at all, because shared_backend_model_info stripped the cost fields) # get_model_info fails for the backend model+provider combo: litellm.get_model_info(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", custom_llm_provider="openrouter") # → raises: "This model isn't mapped yet" # So compute_savings_spend returns (0.0, 0.0): from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.savings import compute_savings_spend result = compute_savings_spend( model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", custom_llm_provider="openrouter", compression_saved_tokens=100000, cache_read_input_tokens=500000, ) print(result) # SavingsSpend(compression=0.0, prompt_caching=0.0) # Expected: SavingsSpend(compression=0.04225, prompt_caching=0.000203625) # (100k * $0.4225/M = $0.04225 compression, 500k * ($0.4225 - $0.035)/M = $0.000203625 caching) ``` **Observable effect:** - Headroom `/stats` endpoint shows compression is actively working (6.7M tokens removed across 457 requests) - But `/user/daily/activity` shows `compression_savings_spend: 0.0` for all days after switching to multi-deployment cost-based routing **Before/After comparison from our daily activity data:** ``` 2026-08-11 saved_tokens=430430 comp_savings_spend=$0.09 ← single deployment per model_name 2026-08-12 saved_tokens=2256791 comp_savings_spend=$2.34 ← last day with old config 2026-08-13 saved_tokens=0 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ← switched to multi-deployment 2026-08-14 saved_tokens=3939121 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ← compression works, pricing broken 2026-08-16 saved_tokens=543419 comp_savings_spend=$0.00 ``` ## Suggested fix `compute_savings_spend()` receives the `model` and `custom_llm_provider` from the spend log payload but not the `router_model_id` (deployment ID). Two possible approaches: **Option A (minimal):** Thread the deployment's `model_info.id` into `compute_savings_spend()` and look up pricing via `litellm.model_cost[model_info_id]` first, falling back to `get_model_info()` only when the ID lookup misses. **Option B (more robust):** Thread the deployment's actual `input_cost_per_token` / `cache_read_input_token_cost` values directly into `compute_savings_spend()` from `litellm_params` / `metadata.model_info`, similar to how `custom_cost_per_token` is already passed in the response-cost path. This removes the dependency on the global `litellm.model_cost` dict entirely for savings calculation. ## Relevant log output No errors are logged — `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` catches the exception from `get_model_info()` and degrades silently: ```python except Exception as e: verbose_proxy_logger.debug( "savings: no model info for provider=%s model=%s (%s)", custom_llm_provider, model, e ) return 0.0, 0.0 ``` Setting `LITELLM_LOG=DEBUG` surfaces: ``` savings: no model info for provider=openrouter model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro (This model isn't mapped yet...) ``` ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy, Cost Tracking ## What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.95.0 (Docker image `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.95.0`)

signal.title: feat: add Levo AI Gateway guardrail integration
signal.text: ## Title feat: add Levo AI Gateway guardrail integration ## Relevant issues None — new provider integration. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/litellm/` directory — `tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_levo.py` (13 tests) - [x] I have added a screenshot / evidence of my new test passing locally (see below) - [x] `make test-unit` — guardrails suite: 2850 passed - [x] `make lint` — exit 0 ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Adds `guardrail: levo`, backed by a self-hosted [Levo AI Gateway](https://docs.levo.ai/install-ai-gateway/ai-gateway-docker). The gateway runs Levo's policy engine — PII and secret detection, prompt-injection heuristics, CEL-based access control, MCP tool policies — and answers allow / block / rewrite. ```yaml guardrails: - guardrail_name: "levo" litellm_params: guardrail: levo api_base: http://levo-gateway:8080 api_key: os.environ/LEVO_GUARDRAIL_API_KEY mode: [pre_call, post_call] default_on: true ``` The gateway already speaks the Basic Guardrail API, so this subclasses `GenericGuardrailAPI` and reuses its wire contract rather than duplicating it. ### Why a separate integration rather than `generic_guardrail_api` **Streamed responses are buffered until moderated by default.** `generic_guardrail_api` never sets `streaming_buffer_until_moderated`, so a response-side finding on a streaming call lands *after* the client already holds the content. Verified against a running gateway — same image, same prompt, completion containing PII, only the guardrail type changed: ``` generic_guardrail_api : 19 content chunks emitted, PII reached the client guardrail: levo : 0 content chunks, 400 before any output ``` Repeated 3× for stability. Clean streamed responses are unaffected and still deliver content (3 chunks, `"Hello."`). Operators who need time-to-first-token more than response-side enforcement can opt out with `buffer_streaming_until_moderated: false`. ### One implementation note worth flagging `apply_guardrail` is overridden in the class body even though it only delegates to the parent. The proxy selects the unified guardrail path with: ```python has_apply_guardrail = "apply_guardrail" in type(callback).__dict__ ``` That inspects the class's own attributes and does not see inherited methods. Without the override, the guardrail is constructed, registered, and even consulted via `should_run_guardrail` — but never invoked, so **every request passes unscanned while the guardrail reports healthy**. I hit this while developing; a test asserts the override stays present, since the failure mode is silent. Might be worth a note in the guardrail authoring docs — any subclass-based integration will hit it. ## Testing ``` $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/test_levo.py -q 13 passed, 1 warning in 1.43s $ make lint OK: every strict rule is within its codebase ceiling OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling OK: every rule is within its basedpyright limit or no higher than base exit 0 $ uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/guardrails -q 2850 passed, 1 xfailed ``` (One unrelated pre-existing failure in `test_model_armor_credentials_handling` — confirmed identical with this branch stashed.) Tests cover registry membership, config-model wiring, endpoint path construction, the `x-api-key` header, initializer validation, `optional_params` flattening as the UI submits it, streaming defaults and their opt-out, and the `__dict__` regression above. Integration-tested end to end against a real gateway: benign 200, secret blocked 400, PII masked, response-side PII blocked 400, streamed PII blocked with zero chunks leaked. ## Notes - Levo already ships an OTLP observability integration at `litellm/integrations/levo/`. This is separate and complementary — that one exports traces, this one enforces policy. - File set follows the existing provider-integration layout: plugin, types, enum entry, tests, logo, and the three guardrail-garden UI registries.

signal.title: feat(proxy): weekly/monthly cost savings report emails
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Auto router users only see estimated savings on the cost optimization tab, with no periodic export - No way to get a recurring summary of auto-router, compression, and caching savings How it solves it: - Adds scheduled weekly/monthly emails summarizing all cost-optimization savings drivers - Attaches a formatted PDF report alongside the HTML summary ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin using the auto router has to remember to open the Admin UI to see savings 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=cost-optimization and check the Auto Router tab 2. They see an "estimated savings" tile, but get no periodic export or historical snapshot 3. There is no way to share these numbers with their team without manually copying them out After: the same admin gets a recurring email with the numbers and a PDF they can forward 1. The proxy admin sets `general_settings.cost_savings_report_recipients: ["admin@example.com"]` in their config and restarts the proxy 2. On the configured cadence (`cost_savings_report_frequency`, default `7d`, plus a monthly report on the 1st), the proxy computes real spend and savings from the daily spend rollups for the window 3. The recipient receives an email with an HTML summary (total spend, auto-router/compression/caching savings, total savings) and a PDF attachment with the same numbers, left-aligned under the LiteLLM logo (or the proxy's own custom logo, if `SMTP_SENDER_LOGO`/`EMAIL_LOGO_URL` is set) 4. If there is nothing to report (zero spend and zero savings in the window), no email is sent ## Relevant issues Resolves #37076 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Commit: `be9a608912` Ran against a real Neon Postgres proxy DB and real Gmail SMTP relay (no mocks), computing the report from actual `LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend` rollups and sending a real email with a live SMTP connection: ```python import asyncio, datetime from litellm.proxy.utils import PrismaClient, ProxyLogging from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.cost_savings_report import get_cost_savings_report_for_time_range from litellm.integrations.email_alerting import send_cost_savings_report_email async def main(): proxy_logging_obj = ProxyLogging(user_api_key_cache=None) prisma_client = PrismaClient(database_url=os.environ["DATABASE_URL"], proxy_logging_obj=proxy_logging_obj) await prisma_client.connect() end_date = datetime.date.today() start_date = end_date - datetime.timedelta(days=30) report = await get_cost_savings_report_for_time_range(prisma_client, start_date, end_date) print("REPORT FROM DB:", report) sent = await send_cost_savings_report_email(recipient_emails=["mubashir@berri.ai"], report=report) print("EMAIL SENT:", sent) asyncio.run(main()) ``` Output: ``` REPORT FROM DB: CostSavingsReport(start_date=datetime.date(2026, 7, 17), end_date=datetime.date(2026, 8, 16), total_spend=1.0954538700000003, autorouter_savings_spend=0.0, compression_savings_spend=0.0, prompt_caching_savings_spend=0.010348109999999999) EMAIL SENT: True ``` Confirmed the email arrived with the correct numbers in both the HTML body and the PDF attachment (logo, title, date range, and the per-driver savings table, all left-aligned). Also confirmed the scheduler wires up correctly at proxy startup: with `cost_savings_report_recipients` set in `general_settings`, the log shows `Alerting: Initializing Weekly/Monthly Cost Savings Reports` and the two APScheduler jobs (`weekly_cost_savings_report_job`, `monthly_cost_savings_report_job`) register; with the key unset, no job is scheduled. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/cost_savings_report.py` (new): `CostSavingsReport` dataclass plus `get_cost_savings_report_for_time_range`, `send_weekly_cost_savings_report`, `send_monthly_cost_savings_report`, reusing the existing `get_daily_activity_aggregated` daily-rollup aggregation - `litellm/integrations/email_alerting.py`: `build_cost_savings_report_email` (HTML), `build_cost_savings_report_pdf` (reportlab, left-aligned, embeds a custom or bundled LiteLLM logo), `_fetch_custom_logo_bytes`, `send_cost_savings_report_email` - `litellm/proxy/utils.py`: `send_email` gains an optional `attachments: Sequence[EmailAttachment]` parameter - `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`: `ProxyStartupEvent._initialize_cost_savings_report_jobs` schedules the weekly/monthly jobs, gated on `general_settings.cost_savings_report_recipients` - `litellm/types/llms/custom_http.py`: new `httpxSpecialProvider.EmailReporting` for the custom-logo fetch - `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`: adds `reportlab` to the `proxy-runtime` extra - Tests: `tests/test_litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/test_cost_savings_report.py`, `tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_email_alerting.py`, plus additions to `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_utils.py` and `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(responses): support dict input item and validate non-iterable input types
signal.text: ## Title fix(responses): support dict input item and validate non-iterable input types ## Description The Responses API input transformation previously only handled string or list input types. When a single dictionary input item was passed (e.g. `input={"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": "..."}`), it resulted in an empty message list. When a non-iterable type like an integer was passed, it caused downstream TypeErrors. This PR adds support for dictionary input items and adds validation to raise a `BadRequestError` for invalid input types. ## Tests Added unit tests to `tests/test_litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/test_litellm_completion_responses.py`: - `test_transform_response_input_param_dict_input` - `test_transform_response_input_param_invalid_type_raises_bad_request` All 118 responses transformation tests pass.

signal.title: feat(perplexity): add Agent API third-party models
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Perplexity's Agent API now routes to third-party open-weight models, but litellm has no cost map entries for them - Calling these models raises "model isn't mapped yet" and litellm can't tell which optional params they support - Separately: `litellm/llms/perplexity/cost_calculator.py` was silently recording $0 spend for every Responses-mode Perplexity model, because the `isinstance(cost_info, dict)` check it used to detect Perplexity's pre-calculated cost was always False on that path How it solves it: - Adds 4 Agent API models to the cost map: DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731, GLM 5.2, Kimi K3, Kimi K2.7 Code - Follows the existing double-prefixed key convention (e.g. `perplexity/perplexity/sonar`) since these models' raw Agent API ids already start with `perplexity/`, same as Perplexity's own `sonar` model - Adds `input_cost_per_token`/`output_cost_per_token`/`cache_read_input_token_cost` from Perplexity's published Agent API rates, as a fallback for the (rare) case their response omits the pre-calculated cost - Sets `supports_reasoning` per model based on whether it accepts a `reasoning_effort`-style param upstream (true for DeepSeek V4 Flash, GLM 5.2, and Kimi K3; false for Kimi K2.7 Code, whose thinking is always-on and not user-configurable) - Fixes `litellm/llms/perplexity/cost_calculator.py::cost_per_token` to also accept a plain float for `usage.cost`, not just a dict: `ResponseAPIUsage.parse_cost` (litellm/types/llms/openai.py) already flattens Perplexity's `usage.cost.total_cost` dict down to a float before `_transform_response_api_usage_to_chat_usage` (litellm/responses/utils.py) copies it onto the chat `Usage` object, so the old dict-only check was dead code for every Responses-mode Perplexity model and silently fell back to manual token-rate calculation, recording $0 for any model missing static per-token rates (which was every existing Agent API entry before this PR) - Syncs the same entries into the bundled backup cost map ## User Flow Before: a developer configures a deployment for one of these models and litellm can't route or validate params for it, and even models with pricing configured had their spend silently recorded as $0 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3"` 2. The call fails cost tracking with "This model isn't mapped yet" 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request logged at $0 spend with no model metadata After: the same request is routed and priced correctly, using Perplexity's own metered cost, and reasoning_effort is exposed only for models that support it 1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3"`, optionally passing `"reasoning_effort": "high"` 2. The response returns normally, and Perplexity's own metered cost from the response is used for spend tracking (falling back to the new per-token rates if that's ever missing) 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the request logged with the correct spend and model name ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix No Perplexity API key was available in this environment to run a live curl proof. To verify locally: ### Before 1. Start the proxy with a config containing a deployment for `perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3` on the `litellm_internal_staging` commit before this PR merges 2. `curl http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "kimi-k3", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}]}'` 3. Expect a 500 with "This model isn't mapped yet" ### After 1. Rebuild the proxy on this branch's tip with the same config 2. Run the same curl command 3. Expect a normal completion response, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows the request with non-zero spend and `perplexity/perplexity/kimi-k3` as the model ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `supports_reasoning` values are based on each upstream provider's own docs (DeepSeek, Z.AI, Moonshot AI) as of 2026-08-16, not direct confirmation from Perplexity's Agent API surface - The fallback per-token pricing is only used if Perplexity's response omits `usage.cost.total_cost`; normal spend tracking uses Perplexity's own metered cost ## QA runbook ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(search): add Amazon Bedrock AgentCore web search provider
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No AWS-native web search provider in LiteLLM - Bedrock users need a third-party search key today - Web Search on Bedrock AgentCore speaks MCP, unsupported How it solves it: - Adds `agentcore` search provider calling an AgentCore Gateway - SigV4 for AWS_IAM gateways, bearer token for CUSTOM_JWT - Works for `/search` and for `websearch_interception` ## User Flow Before: a developer on AWS wants Claude Code on Bedrock to search the web, but every option needs a non-AWS search key 1. They set `callbacks: ["websearch_interception"]` in the proxy config and look for an AWS-backed `search_provider` 2. The only choices are third-party services (Tavily, Exa, Perplexity, Brave, ...), so they sign up for one and put its key in the proxy env 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `web_search` tool and their Bedrock model; the search leg leaves AWS and is billed by that third party 4. Calling POST https://litellm-domain/search with `"search_provider": "agentcore"` returns a 400 saying the provider isn't supported After: the same developer points the proxy at their AgentCore Gateway and search traffic stays inside AWS 1. They create an AgentCore Gateway with a web-search connector target and set `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` to its MCP endpoint 2. They add a `search_tools` entry with `search_provider: agentcore` (see `litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/agentcore_websearch_config.yaml`) and no third-party key 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_provider": "agentcore", "max_results": 5}` and get back the standard results list with `title`, `url`, `snippet`, `date` 4. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with a `web_search` tool and their Bedrock model; the search leg is a SigV4-signed call to their own gateway, billed by AWS 5. Pointing `api_base` at a host that is not the configured gateway returns an error instead of forwarding the server's `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, and a `tool_name` that is not a `___WebSearch` connector tool is rejected ## Relevant issues Fixes #31819 Supersedes #34098, which this builds on Docs live in the docs repo: BerriAI/litellm-docs#834, which has to merge first for the `documentation` check here to pass (it fails on `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` and `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME` being undocumented) ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests), except `documentation` and `code-quality`, which stay red until the docs PR merges - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I don't have an AgentCore Gateway or AWS credentials in this environment, so there is no live run to paste here. Reviewer runbook against a real gateway, with `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_URL` exported and AWS credentials in the environment: ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/example_config_yaml/agentcore_websearch_config.yaml --detailed_debug curl -sS http://localhost:4000/search \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ -d '{"query": "latest AI developments", "search_provider": "agentcore", "max_results": 5}' curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ -d '{"model": "claude-sonnet", "max_tokens": 1024, "tools": [{"type": "web_search_20250305", "name": "web_search"}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What happened in AI this week?"}]}' ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes `AgentCoreSearchConfig` (`litellm/llms/bedrock/search/transformation.py`) is a `BaseSearchConfig` that speaks MCP instead of a bespoke REST API: `transform_search_request` builds a JSON-RPC `tools/call` body, and `transform_search_response` accepts both a plain JSON reply and the Streamable HTTP SSE framing, picking the event that carries `result` or `error` so a progress notification can't shadow the response. ```python {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "web-search-tool___WebSearch", "arguments": {"query": query[:200], "maxResults": max_results}}} ``` Signing needed a new optional hook, because a SigV4 signature covers the exact bytes on the wire: ```python class BaseSearchConfig: def sign_request(self, headers, optional_params, request_data, api_base, api_key=None) -> tuple[dict, bytes | None]: return headers, None # default no-op ``` `BaseLLMHTTPHandler.search` / `async_search` call it and, when a signed body comes back, send it verbatim as `data=` rather than re-serializing it through `json=`. Two things the gateway makes easy to get wrong, both covered by tests: a caller-supplied `tool_name` must end in `___WebSearch`, so this provider can't be used to invoke unrelated tools on the same gateway with the proxy's credentials, and the server-managed `AGENTCORE_GATEWAY_TOKEN` is only attached when the request targets the operator-configured gateway host. The signing region comes from the gateway hostname, falling back to the AWS config chain and erroring out rather than guessing a region the gateway would reject. `api_key=""` is passed down to `BaseAWSLLM._sign_request` so the Bedrock Runtime `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` never leaks to an AgentCore endpoint. Also adds `agentcore/search` to the cost map (AWS bills the gateway directly) and an example proxy config wiring it into `websearch_interception` for Bedrock Claude Code. Search `pre_call` logs the headers as they were before signing, so a configured `logger_fn` never sees the SigV4 or bearer `Authorization` value; only the outbound request carries it Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e52bd0ebe8b7402490e13db8effd5f31

signal.title: fix(core): stop get_image_dimensions crashing on bare base64 and unfetchable URLs
signal.text: ## Bug `get_image_dimensions` documents `"The URL or base64 encoded string of the image."` as valid input, but two documented-or-implied inputs crash it: ```py >>> get_image_dimensions(data="<bare base64 png>") # docstring says this is supported ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1) # data.split(",", 1) >>> get_image_dimensions(data="https://host/x.png") # host unreachable / times out ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1) # falls into the base64 branch ``` The final fallback comment — *"return sensible default image dimensions if unable to get dimensions"* — was unreachable for these paths: the unconditional `_header, encoded = data.split(",", 1)` raised before the format detection, and a failed URL fetch dropped straight into that same branch. This matters for `calculate_img_tokens(..., mode="high")`, which is exported public API: a temporarily-unreachable image URL or a bare-base64 payload turns token counting into an exception instead of an estimate. ## Fix - The base64 branch accepts both data-URL form (`data:<mime>;base64,<payload>`) and bare base64; a decode error logs at debug and leaves the payload unset. - An unfetchable URL no longer falls into the base64 branch at all. - With no image data, format detection is skipped and `DEFAULT_IMAGE_WIDTH/DEFAULT_IMAGE_HEIGHT` is returned, as the fallback comment intended. ## Verification Three new hermetic tests next to the existing mocked-fetch ones (no network): bare base64 parses real PNG dimensions (100×200); a mocked failed fetch returns the defaults; undecodable input returns the defaults. `tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_token_counter.py`: 81 passed, 1 skipped (only the tokenizer-download tests deselected locally — those need network/model downloads and run in CI).

signal.title: feat: same-provider canonical model-name resolution (unknown-spelling requests route to the deployment that provably serves them)
signal.text: ## What this does Harnesses (e.g. Claude Code) hardcode concrete model IDs and resolve subagent tiers to dated Anthropic snapshots like `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, sent verbatim to whatever gateway `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at. A gateway that serves the *same model* under a different deployment name (e.g. `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) rejects the request today: ``` 403 key not allowed to access model. This key can only access models=['anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5', ...]. Tried to access claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 ``` The user *is* serving the requested model — only the spelling differs. This PR adds same-provider canonical model-name resolution: when an incoming request names a model no existing route recognizes, but the requested name and an already-served model group are provably the same model (same provider, cost-map -attested identity), route to it instead of failing. ## Design Four invariants drove every decision (happy to link the fuller design doc if useful): 1. **No behavior change for anything that works today.** The resolver runs strictly *after* every existing resolution path — exact model name, deployment id, `model_group_alias`, routing groups, team routes, wildcard/pattern routes, `default_deployment` — has declined. It can only convert a would-be 4xx into a success, never re-point a request that already succeeds. 2. **Identity, not similarity — and never cross-provider.** A rewrite fires only when both names are attested by the cost map as the same model (same `litellm_provider`, `mode`, and pricing), **and** the requested name's inferred provider matches the target deployment's `custom_llm_provider`. Family/version hops (`claude-sonnet-4-5` → `claude-sonnet-5`) are never equivalences. Bedrock ⇄ Vertex ⇄ first-party substitution is explicitly excluded — same weights on a different provider means different credentials, data residency, quota pool, and bill, and choosing between providers is an operator decision, not something the gateway should infer. That case stays exactly what it is today: define a `model_group_alias`. 3. **Auth is AND-on-target.** Manual `model_group_alias` uses OR-semantics (allowed if either the alias or the target is on the allowlist) because the alias itself is admin-authored. Auto-resolution has no such authorship, so it's stricter: the request is allowed **iff the resolved target** is allowed. The raw requested string's presence in an allowlist grants nothing by itself — this is what prevents a stale/unserved allowlist entry from becoming a privilege escalation onto a deployment the key was never granted. 4. **Observable.** Requested spelling is preserved in request metadata (`requested_model`), each new (requested → target) pair is logged once at INFO, and ambiguous identities (two same-provider groups serving one model) fail closed with a startup-time log naming the conflict, rather than picking one silently. Default is **on** (`router_settings.model_name_resolution: canonical`), since the feature can only turn deterministic failures into successes and cannot expand any key's effective grants. `strict` opts out entirely for shops that want unknown-name-is-a-hard-error semantics. ## Changes - `litellm/router_utils/canonical_model_resolution.py` (new): `canonicalize`, `build_canonical_index`, `lookup` — pure functions, no I/O. - `litellm/router.py`: `Router.resolve_canonical_model_name()`, lazily-built index cached and invalidated alongside the existing model-group-info cache and on cost-map mutation. - `litellm/types/router.py`: `RouterGeneralSettings.model_name_resolution` (`"canonical"` default | `"strict"`). - `litellm/proxy/route_llm_request.py`: resolution hook as the last step before the existing `ProxyModelNotFoundError`, with a re-auth check against the resolved target (AND-on-target) and `requested_model` metadata stamping. - `litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py`: `_can_object_call_model` consults the resolver with AND-on-target semantics, distinct from the existing OR-semantics alias check right above it. - `tests/test_litellm/router_utils/test_canonical_model_resolution.py`: 23 tests covering identity/cross-provider/ambiguity rules and auth semantics. ## Testing ``` pytest tests/test_litellm/router_utils/test_canonical_model_resolution.py -q # 23 passed ``` Manually verified end-to-end against `route_request` and `_can_object_call_model`: - Dated request (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`) against a key allowed only on `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` → routes correctly (the Claude Code case). - Same request against a key allowed only on the stale dated string (nothing serves it) → still rejected (AND-on-target holds). - Unrelated model name → unchanged 400. - Already-recognized model → unchanged routing path (I1 spot check). ## Follow-up (not in this PR) **Cross-deployment resolution when only one provider exists.** If an operator serves a model through exactly one provider (e.g. Claude only via Bedrock), this PR intentionally does *not* auto-resolve an Anthropic-form request to that Bedrock deployment — see invariant 2 above. A follow-up could allow that specific case (single-provider deployment, unambiguous by construction) behind its own explicit opt-in, once we have data (via the resolution-decline counter this PR could log) on how common that shape is in practice. Flagging now so reviewers can weigh in on whether that's worth pursuing and what guardrails it would need. <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 84e2d4e23cdc2cf5dd0c5b176827476553e08072. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: feat(router): Auto Router v2 session_key_fallback derivation (#34766)
signal.text: ## Summary Closes #34766 This PR introduces `session_key_fallback` support in LiteLLM's Auto Router v2 (`ComplexityRouter` and `AdaptiveRouter`) to automatically derive session keys when `session_id` is not explicitly provided in the request metadata or headers. ### Key Changes 1. **Router Configuration (`session_key_fallback`)**: - Added `session_key_fallback` to `ComplexityRouterConfig` and `AdaptiveRouterConfig` with supported modes: - `"none"` (default): Preserves existing behavior without automatic session derivation. - `"prompt_cache_key"`: Uses `prompt_cache_key` from request kwargs, metadata, `litellm_params`, `extra_body`, or headers. - `"prefix_hash"`: Computes a deterministic SHA-256 hash of `user_identifier:model_group:first_system_msg:first_user_msg`. 2. **Session Key Resolution & Propagation**: - `ComplexityRouter._resolve_session_id`: Resolves explicit `session_id` first; if absent and a fallback strategy is enabled, derives the key and populates `metadata["session_id"]`. - Propagated session keys enable downstream `DeploymentAffinityCheck` and `AdaptiveRouterPostCallHook` to maintain affinity across multi-turn requests without requiring clients to supply custom headers. - Added debug/info logging via `verbose_router_logger` upon fallback session key resolution. 3. **Adaptive Router Hook Compatibility**: - Enhanced `_resolve_session_key` in `adaptive_router/hooks.py` to inspect direct `kwargs["metadata"]` and `prompt_cache_key`. 4. **Comprehensive Unit Tests**: - Added `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_session_key_fallback.py` verifying: - Explicit `session_id` resolution precedence. - Fallback to `prompt_cache_key` (via params, extra_body, headers). - Fallback to `prefix_hash` across multi-turn conversations and segregation between different callers/prompts. - Default `"none"` behavior preserving unpinned reclassification. - Deployment affinity interaction with derived session keys. - Adaptive router post-call hook key extraction. ## Test Verification - All 12 unit tests in `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/test_session_key_fallback.py` pass 100%. - All 98 adaptive routing and router pre-call check tests in `tests/test_litellm/router_strategy/adaptive_router/` and `tests/test_litellm/router_utils/pre_call_checks/` pass cleanly.

signal.title: [Feature]: Support Azure AI Foundry Agents v2 (Responses API with agent_reference)
signal.text: ## Feature Request ### What is your use case? We are integrating with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service. We've deployed agents using the new Foundry Agents v2 experience, which uses the Responses API with `agent_reference` (referencing agents by name and version) rather than the deprecated Assistants API (thread/run pattern with `asst_*` IDs). The current `azure_ai/agents/{agent_id}` route in LiteLLM implements the old Assistants API pattern, which: 1. Requires agent IDs beginning with `asst_` (but the new Foundry experience does not surface these IDs) 2. Uses the thread → message → run → poll flow (but the new Foundry Agents v2 uses `openai_client.responses.create()` with an `agent_reference` in `extra_body`) Microsoft has [deprecated the Assistants API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/how-to/assistant) with retirement set for **August 26, 2026**. ### The new API pattern From the Azure AI Foundry getting-started code: ```python from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential project_client = AIProjectClient( endpoint="https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>", credential=DefaultAzureCredential(), ) openai_client = project_client.get_openai_client() response = openai_client.responses.create( input=[{"role": "user", "content": "Tell me what you can help with."}], extra_body={ "agent_reference": { "name": "my-agent-name", "version": "1", "type": "agent_reference", } }, ) ``` Key differences from the current `azure_ai/agents` implementation: - **Endpoint**: Project-level (`https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project>`) - **API**: Responses API (`/openai/responses`), not Assistants/Threads API - **Agent identification**: By `name` + `version` via `agent_reference` in extra_body, not by `asst_*` ID - **Auth**: Azure AD (Entra ID) bearer token — same as current implementation ### Proposed model format ``` azure_ai/agents/<agent_name>:<version> ``` For example: `azure_ai/agents/my-agent-name:1` ### Reference docs - [Agent identity concepts in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity) - [Authentication and authorization in Microsoft Foundry](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry) - [Assistants API deprecation notice](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry-classic/openai/how-to/assistant) ### Are you a LiteLLM Enterprise customer? No

signal.title: feat(helm): compose DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from a reader host secret key
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - No way to compose DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA from separate secret keys - envFrom vars don't resolve in $(VAR) env interpolation - Secret stores often hold a bare reader hostname, not a full URL How it solves it: - New db.secret.readReplicaEndpointKey injects DATABASE_READER_HOST into the env array - db.readReplicaUrl can then reference $(DATABASE_READER_HOST), same pattern as the writer URL ## User Flow Before: an operator whose secret store holds the reader hostname as its own secret key cannot enable read-replica routing 1. They store username, password, writer host, and reader host as separate keys in one Kubernetes secret synced from their secret store 2. They set db.readReplicaUrl to `postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require` and mount the secret via environmentSecrets 3. The pod starts with DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA containing the literal text `$(DATABASE_READER_HOST)` because Kubernetes only interpolates vars defined in the env array, not envFrom 4. The proxy fails to reach the reader and read-replica routing never activates After: the same operator enables read-replica routing with the same secret layout 1. They store the same keys in the same Kubernetes secret 2. They set db.secret.readReplicaEndpointKey to the reader host key and keep the same db.readReplicaUrl 3. The pod starts with DATABASE_READER_HOST sourced from the secret and placed before DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA, so the URL interpolates fully 4. The proxy connects to the reader and routes read-only queries there ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: values file used for both renders ```yaml db: deployStandalone: false useExisting: true database: litellm url: postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require secret: name: pg-creds usernameKey: username passwordKey: password endpointKey: writer-host readReplicaEndpointKey: reader-host readReplicaUrl: postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require ``` ### Before (973329e986) 1. `helm template litellm helm/litellm-helm -f reader-values.yaml -s templates/deployment.yaml` 2. Rendered env has DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA referencing `$(DATABASE_READER_HOST)` but no DATABASE_READER_HOST entry anywhere in the env array, so Kubernetes leaves the reference as literal text at runtime ```yaml - name: DATABASE_URL value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" - name: DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" ``` ### After (d256f42f27) 1. Same `helm template` command 2. DATABASE_READER_HOST is now sourced from the secret and rendered immediately before DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA, so the $(VAR) reference resolves ```yaml - name: DATABASE_URL value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" - name: DATABASE_READER_HOST valueFrom: secretKeyRef: name: pg-creds key: reader-host - name: DATABASE_URL_READ_REPLICA value: "postgresql://$(DATABASE_USERNAME):$(DATABASE_PASSWORD)@$(DATABASE_READER_HOST):5432/$(DATABASE_NAME)?sslmode=require" ``` 3. `helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm` passes: 14 suites, 96 tests ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - readReplicaUrlKey still wins when both keys are set Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/4977773ef12040748630173bf865083a

signal.title: fix(azure): forward context_management on Azure Responses API
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `AzureOpenAIResponsesAPIConfig` listed `context_management` as unsupported and stripped it from the supported params. With `drop_params: true` the param was silently dropped, so callers got no server-side compaction and no error - Azure now documents `context_management` on the Responses API (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/responses), so the exclusion is wrong How it solves it: - Remove the Azure-specific `context_management` exclusion (the attribute and the `get_supported_openai_params` override) so the class inherits the base `OpenAIResponsesAPIConfig` supported params, which include `context_management` - The O-series subclass keeps dropping `temperature` through its own override; its `super()` call now resolves to the base config and picks up `context_management` too ## User Flow A caller sends an Azure Responses request (`azure/<deployment>`) with `context_management` set and `drop_params: true`. The param is now forwarded to Azure instead of being dropped, enabling server-side compaction. ## Relevant issues Fixes #36391 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Unit RED to GREEN on the supported-params contract. RED on `litellm_internal_staging` (before the fix), `context_management` missing from supported params: ``` FAILED tests/test_litellm/llms/azure/response/test_azure_transformation.py::test_azure_responses_api_supports_context_management 1 failed, 13 warnings in 0.53s ``` GREEN with the fix: ``` tests/test_litellm/llms/azure/response/test_azure_transformation.py::test_azure_responses_api_supports_context_management PASSED 1 passed, 13 warnings in 0.34s ``` Live check runbook against an Azure deployment: ``` curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{ "model": "azure-responses", "input": "hello", "drop_params": true, "context_management": {"type": "server_side"} }' ``` Before the fix the proxy dropped `context_management`; after the fix it is forwarded to Azure. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/llms/azure/responses/transformation.py`: remove the `AZURE_UNSUPPORTED_PARAMS` exclusion and the `get_supported_openai_params` override so `context_management` is inherited from the base config - `tests/test_litellm/llms/azure/response/test_azure_transformation.py`: drop the stale test that asserted `context_management` was unsupported, add a regression test asserting it is supported for both the regular and O-series Azure configs (O-series still drops `temperature`) ## QA runbook Run `make test-unit` for `tests/test_litellm/llms/azure/response/test_azure_transformation.py`. For a live check, send an Azure Responses request with `context_management` and `drop_params: true` and confirm the param reaches Azure. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): stop listing literal wildcard routes as models
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - With wildcard routes configured (`model_name: "openai/*"`, `anthropic/*`), the `/v1/models` and `/models` listing correctly expands them into concrete provider models, but it also returns the literal `openai/*` and `anthropic/*` entries - Clients read those literals as callable model ids, which is misleading How it solves it: - `get_complete_model_list` expands wildcards via `_get_wildcard_models`. Two of its three branches already dropped the literal pattern after expansion, but the branch used when the router holds a deployment for the wildcard did not, so the literal leaked into the list - Drop the literal in that branch as well. The pattern is still surfaced when a caller passes `return_wildcard_routes=true`, so that opt-in behavior is unchanged - `_get_wildcard_models` no longer mutates its `unique_models` argument in place. It returns an immutable `_WildcardModels` tuple of kept and expanded models, and `get_complete_model_list` builds the final list functionally. This also removes a duplicate-leak edge Greptile flagged, where the old `set` plus `list.remove` loop dropped only the first occurrence of a repeated literal ## User Flow An operator configures wildcard passthrough (`openai/*`, `anthropic/*`). A consumer calls `GET /v1/models`. They now see only concrete, callable model ids, not the `*` routing patterns. ## Relevant issues Fixes #13752 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Unit RED to GREEN on the listing helper. RED on `litellm_internal_staging` (before the fix), the literal wildcard is still listed: ``` tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_model_checks.py:785: AssertionError 1 failed, 1 warning in 4.63s ``` GREEN with the fix: ``` tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_model_checks.py::test_get_complete_model_list_omits_literal_wildcard_when_router_has_deployment PASSED 1 passed, 1 warning in 3.13s ``` Follow-up regression for the mutation and duplicate-leak edge, RED on the pre-fix remove-in-place code: ``` > assert unique_models == original E AssertionError: assert ['openai/*'] == ['openai/*', 'openai/*'] 1 failed, 1 warning in 3.71s ``` GREEN after returning the immutable tuple: ``` tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_model_checks.py::test_get_wildcard_models_does_not_mutate_input_and_drops_all_literals PASSED 30 passed, 1 warning in 3.41s ``` Live check runbook for a proxy with a wildcard config (`model_name: "openai/*"`): ``` curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" | jq -r '.data[].id' | grep -c '^openai/\*$' ``` Before the fix this prints `1` (the literal is listed), after the fix it prints `0` while concrete `openai/...` ids are still returned. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/proxy/auth/model_checks.py`: `_get_wildcard_models` now drops the literal wildcard pattern from the listing once expanded, in every branch including the router-backed one that previously kept it. It returns an immutable `_WildcardModels` tuple instead of mutating its `unique_models` argument, so `get_complete_model_list` builds the result functionally and no repeated literal can leak. Wildcard expansion itself lives in the typed `_expand_wildcard_model` helper - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_model_checks.py`: regression tests covering `return_wildcard_routes` false (literal absent, concretes present) and true (literal present exactly once), plus non-mutation of the input and removal of duplicated literals ## QA runbook Configure a wildcard model, start the proxy, call `GET /v1/models`, and confirm the response contains expanded provider models but not the `*` pattern. Run `make test-unit` for `tests/test_litellm/proxy/auth/test_model_checks.py`. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
